ingredients: 8 slices pane casereccio (rustic country bread) or ciabatta, 1.5 cm thick
500 g ripe plum or cherry tomatoes, diced
steps: Toss the diced tomatoes with the basil, salt, pepper and 2 tbsp olive oil and leave to stand for 10 minutes so the juices start to run.
Toast or grill the bread over high heat for about 2 minutes per side until crisp and lightly charred at the edges.
Rub the hot toast once or twice with the cut side of the garlic, then drizzle with the remaining olive oil.
Spoon the tomato mixture onto the toast just before serving so the bread stays crisp, and eat right away as an antipasto.

ingredients: 100 g salame (such as Milano or Felino), thinly sliced
150 g Parmigiano Reggiano, broken into chunks
200 g mozzarella bocconcini or 1 ball fior di latte
150 g carciofini sott'olio (artichokes in oil), drained
steps: Take the cured meats and cheeses out of the fridge 20 minutes before serving so their flavour opens up.
Arrange the prosciutto, salame and mortadella in loose folds on a large wooden board or platter.
Add the Parmigiano chunks, the mozzarella drizzled with olive oil, the olives and the drained artichokes in separate clusters.
Stand the grissini in a glass or lay them alongside and serve as a shared starter with bread.

ingredients: 1 ripe cantaloupe melon (melone retato), about 1.2 kg
120 g prosciutto crudo di Parma or San Daniele, very thinly sliced
steps: Chill the melon for at least 1 hour, then halve it, scoop out the seeds and cut into 8 wedges, removing the rind.
Drape a slice of prosciutto over or around each melon wedge.
Finish with a few drops of olive oil, a twist of black pepper and the mint leaves.
Serve cold as a summer antipasto straight away, before the ham dries out.

ingredients: 1 onion, 1 carrot and 1 celery stalk, finely diced (soffritto)
150 g green beans, cut in 2 cm pieces
200 g cavolo nero or savoy cabbage, shredded
400 g can borlotti or cannellini beans, drained
40 g vegetarian Italian-style hard cheese, grated, to serve
steps: Warm the olive oil in a large pot over medium-low heat and cook the onion, carrot and celery for 10 minutes until soft and sweet but not browned.
Add the potatoes, zucchini, green beans and cabbage, stir for 3 minutes, then add the tomatoes, stock and salt.
Bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer gently, partly covered, for 35 minutes until the vegetables are very tender.
Add the beans and pasta and cook for another 10 minutes until the pasta is al dente, adding a splash of water if the soup gets too thick.
Rest the soup for 5 minutes off the heat and serve with a drizzle of raw olive oil and the grated cheese.

ingredients: 1 onion, 1 carrot and 1 celery stalk, finely chopped
2 x 400 g cans borlotti beans, drained (or 250 g dried, soaked overnight and boiled)
1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp black pepper
steps: Heat the olive oil in a heavy pot over medium heat and fry the pancetta for 5 minutes until its fat runs and it starts to crisp.
Add the onion, carrot, celery, garlic and rosemary and cook for 8 minutes until softened, then stir in the tomato paste for 1 minute.
Add the beans and stock, bring to a boil and simmer for 20 minutes; remove the rosemary and mash or blend about a third of the beans to thicken the soup.
Add the pasta, salt and pepper and simmer, stirring often, for 10 minutes until the pasta is tender and the soup is thick and creamy.
Rest for 5 minutes, then serve with grated Parmigiano and a thread of olive oil.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Warm the olive oil in a pot over medium-low heat and gently cook the onion, garlic and rosemary for 6 minutes until the onion is soft.
Stir in the tomato paste and chickpeas, cook for 2 minutes, then pour in the stock and simmer for 15 minutes.
Remove the rosemary and garlic and blend about half the chickpeas with a stick blender to make a creamy base.
Add the pasta and salt and cook for 10 minutes, stirring often, until the pasta is al dente and the soup is thick.
Serve hot with a drizzle of raw olive oil and a pinch of peperoncino.

ingredients: 750 ml homemade brodo (meat or chicken stock)
80 g pastina (stelline or tiny star pasta)
steps: Bring the brodo to a boil in a saucepan over medium-high heat and season with salt.
Add the pastina and simmer, stirring occasionally so it does not stick, for 5 to 7 minutes until tender.
Take off the heat and stir in the butter and Parmigiano until melted.
Ladle into bowls and serve warm, the classic comfort dish for children and anyone feeling unwell.

ingredients: 800 g beef shin or brisket on the bone
steps: Put the beef and chicken in a large stockpot with the cold water and bring slowly to a simmer over medium heat, skimming off the grey foam as it rises.
Add the onion, carrots, celery, tomato, parsley and salt, and keep at the barest simmer, uncovered, for 3 hours.
Strain the brodo through a fine sieve lined with muslin and let it cool, then chill so the fat sets and can be lifted off.
Use as a clear soup with pastina or tortellini, and serve the boiled meat (bollito) separately with salsa verde.

ingredients: 1 dried red chilli (peperoncino), crumbled, or 1/2 tsp chilli flakes
1 tbsp coarse salt for the pasta water
steps: Bring a large pot of water to a boil, add the coarse salt and cook the spaghetti until 1 minute short of al dente.
Meanwhile, warm the olive oil in a wide pan over low heat and cook the garlic and chilli for 2 to 3 minutes until the garlic is pale gold, never brown.
Transfer the spaghetti to the pan with a ladle of pasta water and toss over medium heat for 1 minute until the oil and water emulsify into a glossy coating.
Toss in the parsley and serve immediately; traditionally no cheese is added.

ingredients: 800 g canned whole San Marzano or plum tomatoes, crushed by hand
1 tbsp coarse salt for the pasta water
30 g vegetarian Italian-style hard cheese, grated
steps: Warm the olive oil in a wide pan over medium-low heat and sizzle the garlic for 2 minutes until fragrant, then remove it.
Add the tomatoes and salt, bring to a simmer and cook for 20 minutes, stirring now and then, until thickened and the oil separates at the edges.
Cook the spaghetti in boiling salted water until just al dente, then drain, reserving a cup of the water.
Toss the spaghetti in the sauce with the torn basil and a splash of pasta water over medium heat for 1 minute, then serve with grated cheese.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 x 160 g cans tuna in olive oil, drained
steps: Warm the olive oil in a wide pan over medium heat and cook the garlic and chilli for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes and salt and simmer for 12 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Stir in the flaked tuna and capers and heat through for 2 minutes without breaking the tuna up too much.
Toss the al dente spaghetti in the sauce with a little pasta water, sprinkle with parsley and serve without cheese, as is customary with fish.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 small onion or 2 shallots, finely chopped
40 g vegetarian Italian-style hard cheese, grated
steps: Melt the butter with the oil in a wide pan over medium-low heat and cook the onion and garlic for 6 minutes until soft.
Pour in the vodka and let it bubble for 2 minutes over medium heat until the sharp alcohol smell fades.
Add the passata, chilli and salt and simmer for 12 minutes, then stir in the cream and heat until the sauce is a uniform pink.
Toss the al dente penne in the sauce with a splash of pasta water and the grated cheese, and serve at once.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 150 g Italian sausage (salsiccia), casing removed, crumbled
300 g mixed mushrooms (champignon and porcini), sliced
1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp black pepper
steps: Heat the oil in a large pan over medium-high heat and brown the crumbled sausage for 6 minutes until cooked through with no pink remaining.
Add the garlic and mushrooms and sauté for 6 minutes until the mushrooms release their liquid and it evaporates.
Stir in the passata, salt and pepper and simmer for 8 minutes, then add the cream and warm through.
Toss with the al dente pasta, parsley and Parmigiano, loosening with pasta water if needed, and serve hot.

ingredients: 1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp black pepper
200 g mozzarella (fior di latte), diced and drained
steps: Cook the onion in the oil over medium heat for 6 minutes, add the mince and brown for 8 minutes, then add the passata, salt and pepper and simmer gently for 40 minutes to make a ragù.
Heat the oven to 200°C and boil the pasta for half its packet time, then drain.
Mix the pasta with the ragù, half the besciamella, the mozzarella, basil and half the Parmigiano.
Spread in a buttered baking dish, top with the remaining besciamella and Parmigiano, and bake for 25 to 30 minutes until bubbling with a golden crust.
Rest for 10 minutes before cutting into portions.

ingredients: 400 g fresh porcini (or 300 g chestnut mushrooms plus 20 g dried porcini, soaked)
1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp black pepper
40 g vegetarian Italian-style hard cheese, grated
steps: Clean the porcini with a brush and damp cloth (never soak fresh ones) and slice them 5 mm thick; if using dried, chop them and keep the strained soaking water.
Heat the oil and garlic in a wide pan over medium-high heat, add the mushrooms and sauté for 6 to 8 minutes until golden, then season with salt, pepper and parsley.
Boil the tagliatelle in salted water for 2 to 3 minutes until just tender, then drain, saving a cup of the water.
Toss the pasta with the mushrooms, butter and a splash of pasta or porcini water until glossy, and serve with grated cheese.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 12 dried cannelloni tubes or 12 fresh lasagne sheets
500 g fresh spinach, wilted, squeezed and chopped
60 g vegetarian Italian-style hard cheese, grated
steps: Heat the oven to 190°C and mix the ricotta, spinach, egg, half the cheese, nutmeg and salt into a smooth filling.
Pipe or spoon the filling into the cannelloni tubes, or roll it up inside the fresh pasta sheets.
Spread the tomato sauce in a buttered baking dish, lay the cannelloni on top in one layer and cover completely with besciamella.
Scatter over the remaining cheese and dots of butter and bake for 35 to 40 minutes until the pasta is tender and the top is golden.
Rest for 10 minutes before serving.

ingredients: 300 g spinach, wilted, squeezed dry and finely chopped
50 g vegetarian Italian-style hard cheese, grated
steps: Knead the flour and eggs into a smooth, firm dough for 8 minutes, wrap and rest for 30 minutes.
Mix the ricotta, spinach, half the cheese, nutmeg and salt to make the filling.
Roll the dough into thin sheets, place teaspoons of filling 4 cm apart, cover with a second sheet, press out the air and cut into squares, sealing the edges well.
Cook the ravioli in gently boiling salted water for 3 to 4 minutes until they float and the pasta is tender.
Meanwhile melt the butter with the sage over medium heat until foaming and nutty, then toss the drained ravioli in it and serve with the remaining cheese.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg floury potatoes (such as russet), unpeeled
250 g tipo 00 flour, plus extra for dusting
40 g vegetarian Italian-style hard cheese, grated
steps: Boil the whole potatoes in salted water for 35 to 40 minutes until a knife slides in easily, then peel while hot and pass through a potato ricer.
Spread the riced potato to let steam escape for 5 minutes, then add the salt and work in the flour lightly with your hands just until a soft dough forms.
Roll into 2 cm ropes, cut into 2 cm pieces and roll each over a fork or gnocchi board to make ridges.
Drop the gnocchi into boiling salted water in batches and lift out with a slotted spoon 1 minute after they float to the surface.
Toss in butter foamed with sage over medium heat and serve with the grated cheese, or with sugo al pomodoro.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g mixed mushrooms, sliced, plus 15 g dried porcini, soaked
50 g vegetarian Italian-style hard cheese, grated
steps: Sauté the fresh mushrooms and chopped porcini in 1 tbsp oil over high heat for 6 minutes until golden, season and set aside; add the strained porcini water to the stock.
In a heavy pan, soften the onion in the remaining oil and 10 g butter over medium-low heat for 5 minutes, then add the rice and toast for 2 minutes until the grains turn translucent at the edges.
Pour in the wine and let it evaporate, then add the hot stock a ladle at a time, stirring often and adding more only when the last is absorbed, for about 16 minutes.
Stir in the mushrooms for the last 3 minutes; when the rice is creamy and al dente, take it off the heat.
Beat in the remaining cold butter and the cheese (the mantecatura), rest covered for 2 minutes, then serve with parsley; the risotto should flow gently, all'onda.

ingredients: 500 g mussels and clams, scrubbed and purged
200 g squid, cleaned and cut in rings
200 g raw prawns, peeled and deveined
steps: Steam the mussels and clams with half the wine in a covered pan over high heat for 4 minutes until they open, discard any that stay shut, shell most of them and strain the liquor into the stock.
In a wide pan, warm the oil with the garlic over medium heat, add the rice and toast for 2 minutes, then add the remaining wine and let it evaporate.
Add the tomatoes and then the hot stock a ladle at a time, stirring, for about 12 minutes.
Add the squid and prawns and continue cooking and adding stock for 5 to 6 minutes until the rice is al dente and the prawns are pink and opaque throughout.
Stir in the shellfish, a drizzle of raw olive oil and the parsley (no butter or cheese), rest for 1 minute and serve.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 160 g tuna in olive oil, drained
200 g giardiniera (pickled vegetables in oil or vinegar), chopped
steps: Cook the rice in plenty of boiling salted water for 13 to 15 minutes until just tender, then drain and rinse under cold water to stop the cooking.
Spread the rice on a tray, toss with 2 tbsp oil and let it cool completely.
Mix in the tuna, ham, cheese, giardiniera, peas, olives and tomatoes with the remaining oil and salt.
Chill for at least 1 hour and serve cold as a summer one-dish meal or picnic salad.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 3/4 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp black pepper
steps: Sauté the onion and zucchini in 2 tbsp oil in a 24 cm non-stick pan over medium heat for 8 minutes until soft and lightly golden.
Beat the eggs with the Parmigiano, basil, salt and pepper, pour over the vegetables and stir once to spread them evenly.
Cook over low heat, without stirring, for 6 to 8 minutes until the edges are set and the centre is just slightly wobbly.
Slide onto a plate, invert back into the pan with the remaining oil and cook for 2 to 3 minutes until fully set; serve warm or at room temperature.

ingredients: 500 g minced beef (or half beef, half pork)
80 g stale bread, crusts removed, soaked in milk and squeezed
1 clove garlic, minced, and 2 tbsp parsley, chopped
1 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp black pepper
steps: Mix the mince, soaked bread, egg, Parmigiano, garlic, parsley, salt and pepper until combined, then roll into walnut-sized balls with wet hands.
Brown the meatballs in 2 tbsp oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat for 6 minutes, turning, then set aside.
In the same pan soften the onion in the remaining oil for 5 minutes, add the passata and basil, and bring to a simmer.
Return the meatballs to the sauce, cover and simmer gently for 30 minutes until cooked through (71°C inside) and the sauce has thickened.
Serve with crusty bread as a secondo, or use the sauce to dress pasta as a first course.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.2 kg chicken pieces, skin on, bone in
150 ml dry red or white wine
1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp black pepper
steps: Season the chicken and brown it skin-side down in the oil in a heavy casserole over medium-high heat for 8 minutes, turning to colour all sides, then remove.
Lower the heat to medium, cook the onion, garlic, carrot and celery for 6 minutes, then pour in the wine and let it reduce by half.
Add the tomatoes, rosemary and chicken, cover and simmer gently for 35 minutes.
Add the olives and cook uncovered for 10 minutes until the sauce is thick and the chicken is tender and cooked through (74°C at the bone); serve with polenta or bread.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Flatten the spatchcocked chicken well and rub it with the oil, lemon juice, garlic, chilli, pepper, rosemary and salt; marinate in the fridge for 2 hours.
Heat a large cast-iron pan or grill over medium heat and lay the chicken skin-side down, pressing it flat with a heavy pan or brick on top.
Cook for 20 minutes until the skin is deep golden and crisp, then turn, press again and cook for another 15 to 20 minutes until the thigh juices run clear (74°C).
Rest for 5 minutes, cut into pieces and serve with lemon wedges and a green salad.

ingredients: 8 thin veal escalopes (or chicken breast), about 500 g, pounded to 5 mm
1 lemon, juiced, plus slices to garnish
100 ml chicken stock or white wine
steps: Season the escalopes and dust them lightly in flour, shaking off the excess.
Heat the oil and half the butter in a wide pan over medium-high heat and cook the meat for 1 to 2 minutes per side until golden and just cooked through; set aside.
Deglaze the pan with the stock and lemon juice, scraping up the brown bits, and simmer for 1 minute.
Swirl in the remaining butter to make a silky sauce, return the escalopes for 30 seconds to coat, and serve with parsley and lemon slices.

ingredients: 8 thin veal escalopes, about 500 g, pounded to 5 mm
3/4 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp black pepper
steps: Season the escalopes and dredge them lightly in flour.
Brown them in the oil and half the butter over medium-high heat for 1 to 2 minutes per side until golden and cooked through, then remove.
Pour the Marsala into the pan and let it bubble for 2 minutes, scraping the bottom, then add the stock and reduce for 2 minutes until syrupy.
Whisk in the remaining butter, return the veal to coat in the glossy sauce for 30 seconds, sprinkle with parsley and serve with mashed potato.

ingredients: 8 thin slices beef topside or veal, about 500 g, pounded thin
2 tbsp parsley and 1 clove garlic, finely chopped
steps: Lay out the meat slices, top each with a slice of ham and a sprinkle of Parmigiano, parsley and garlic, then roll up tightly and secure with a toothpick.
Brown the rolls in the oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat for 5 minutes, turning, then pour in the wine and let it evaporate.
Add the passata, salt and pepper, cover and simmer gently for 30 minutes until the meat is tender and cooked through.
Remove the toothpicks and serve the involtini with their sauce and mashed potatoes or bread.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg beef chuck, cut in 4 cm cubes
1 onion, 1 carrot and 1 celery stalk, finely chopped
500 g potatoes, peeled and cut in chunks
steps: Dust the beef in flour and brown in batches in the oil in a heavy casserole over high heat, 5 minutes per batch, then set aside.
Lower the heat and cook the onion, carrot and celery for 8 minutes, then stir in the tomato paste and pour in the wine, scraping up the browned bits.
Return the beef with the stock, herbs, salt and pepper, cover and simmer gently for 1 1/2 hours.
Add the potatoes and cook for 30 minutes more until the meat is fork-tender and the sauce is thick; serve with polenta or bread.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.2 kg veal loin or rump, tied with string
steps: Rub the veal with salt and pepper and tuck the rosemary and sage under the string.
Brown the meat on all sides in the oil and butter in a heavy casserole over medium-high heat for 10 minutes, then add the garlic, onion and carrot.
Pour in the wine and let it evaporate, then cover and cook over low heat (or in a 170°C oven) for about 1 1/2 hours, adding stock a little at a time, until the centre reaches 65°C.
Rest the meat for 10 minutes, blend or strain the pan juices into a sauce, and serve thinly sliced with the gravy and roast potatoes.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 sirloin or rib-eye steaks, about 800 g total, 3 cm thick
2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, plus extra to drizzle
1 tsp flaky sea salt and 1/2 tsp black pepper
steps: Bring the steaks to room temperature for 30 minutes and rub with oil and rosemary.
Sear in a very hot griddle pan over high heat for 3 to 4 minutes per side for medium-rare (54°C inside), or longer to taste.
Rest the steaks for 5 minutes, then slice across the grain into 1 cm strips.
Lay the slices over the rocket, season with flaky salt and pepper, and finish with Parmigiano shavings, a drizzle of oil and balsamic.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 whole sea bass (branzino), about 500 g each, gutted and scaled
1 small bunch parsley and 2 sprigs rosemary
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C and toss the potatoes with 2 tbsp oil and half the salt in a roasting tin; bake for 10 minutes.
Season the fish inside and out and fill the cavities with lemon, garlic and herbs.
Lay the fish on the potatoes, scatter the tomatoes around, drizzle with the remaining oil and the wine.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes until the flesh is opaque and flakes easily from the backbone (63°C), then fillet at the table and serve with the potatoes.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g squid, cleaned and cut into rings
300 g small raw prawns, shell on or peeled
200 g small fish such as anchovies or whitebait, cleaned
150 g semola rimacinata (fine durum semolina) or plain flour
1 litre sunflower or peanut oil for frying
steps: Pat all the seafood very dry with kitchen paper.
Heat the oil in a deep pan to 180°C.
Toss the seafood in the semolina in small batches, shaking off the excess, and fry for 2 to 3 minutes until crisp, pale gold and cooked through.
Drain on paper, salt immediately and serve piping hot with lemon wedges.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 clove garlic and 2 tbsp parsley, finely chopped
steps: Heat the oven to 190°C, halve the zucchini lengthwise and scoop out the flesh to leave 5 mm shells; chop the flesh.
Fry the chopped flesh in 1 tbsp oil for 4 minutes, cool slightly, then mix with the mince, egg, Parmigiano, half the breadcrumbs, garlic, parsley, salt and pepper.
Fill the zucchini shells, set them on a layer of passata in a baking dish, sprinkle with the remaining breadcrumbs and drizzle with oil.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until the filling is browned and cooked through (71°C) and the zucchini are tender.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 large red or yellow bell peppers
300 g minced beef or sausage meat
100 g cooked rice or stale bread soaked and squeezed
1 tbsp capers and 4 anchovy fillets, chopped
steps: Heat the oven to 190°C, cut the tops off the peppers and remove the seeds.
Mix the meat, rice, egg, Parmigiano, capers, anchovies, parsley and salt into a firm filling and pack it into the peppers.
Stand the peppers in a baking dish with the passata and a splash of water around them, replace the tops and drizzle with oil.
Bake for 45 to 50 minutes, basting once, until the peppers are soft and blistered and the filling is cooked through (71°C); serve warm or at room temperature.

ingredients: 600 g squid, cleaned, bodies cut into 1 cm rings, tentacles kept
120 g semola rimacinata or plain flour
1 litre sunflower or peanut oil for frying
steps: Pat the squid completely dry with kitchen paper.
Heat the oil in a deep pan to 180°C.
Toss the squid in the flour, shake off the excess and fry in small batches for 1 1/2 to 2 minutes until golden and crisp; longer cooking makes them rubbery.
Drain on paper, salt immediately and serve with lemon wedges.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g squid, cleaned and cut into rings
250 g raw prawns, peeled and deveined
200 g baby octopus or extra squid
steps: Steam the mussels in a covered pan over high heat for 4 minutes until open, discard any closed ones and shell them.
Simmer the octopus in salted water for 10 to 15 minutes until tender, the squid for 2 minutes and the prawns for 2 minutes until pink and opaque; drain each.
Combine all the warm seafood with the celery, garlic, oil, lemon juice, parsley and salt.
Chill for at least 1 hour to let the flavours marry and serve cold within the day.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 200 g mixed lettuce (lattuga, radicchio, rucola), washed and dried
steps: Tear the leaves into a large bowl and add the tomatoes, carrot and cucumber.
Just before serving, season with salt first, then the vinegar, and toss.
Drizzle with the olive oil, toss again and serve as a contorno alongside the main course.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g potatoes, peeled and diced 1 cm
steps: Boil the potatoes and carrots in salted water with the vinegar for 8 to 10 minutes until just tender, adding the peas for the last 3 minutes, then drain and cool completely.
Hard-boil the eggs for 9 minutes, cool in cold water, peel and chop two of them, keeping one for decoration.
Fold the cold vegetables, chopped eggs and gherkins into the mayonnaise with the salt.
Mound on a plate, smooth the top, decorate with slices of the remaining egg and chill for 1 hour before serving, a favourite at holiday buffets.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 red and yellow bell peppers, cut in strips
300 g ripe tomatoes, chopped, or canned
steps: Warm the oil in a wide pan over medium heat and cook the onions for 6 minutes until soft.
Add the peppers and salt, cover and cook for 15 minutes, stirring now and then, until they start to soften.
Add the tomatoes and cook uncovered for 20 minutes until the peppers are silky and the sauce has reduced.
Stir in the vinegar and basil and serve warm or at room temperature as a contorno or on bread.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg waxy or all-purpose potatoes, cut in 3 cm chunks
4 cloves garlic, unpeeled and lightly crushed
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C and dry the potato chunks well.
Toss them with the oil, rosemary, garlic, salt and pepper in a large roasting tin in a single layer.
Roast for 40 to 45 minutes, turning once halfway, until golden and crisp outside and soft inside.
Serve hot as a contorno to roasts and grilled meats.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 red peppers, cut in wide strips
1 red onion, cut in thick rounds
steps: Heat a ridged griddle pan or barbecue over high heat until very hot.
Grill the vegetables in batches without oil for 2 to 4 minutes per side until marked and tender.
Lay them in a dish and dress with the oil mixed with garlic, herbs and salt.
Leave to marinate for at least 20 minutes and serve at room temperature.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 600 g mushrooms (champignon, porcini or mixed), sliced
3/4 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp black pepper
steps: Heat the oil and garlic in a wide pan over medium-high heat for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the mushrooms and cook, stirring, for 10 minutes until their liquid has evaporated and they turn golden.
Season with salt and pepper, stir in the butter and parsley and cook for 1 more minute.
Serve as a contorno, on toast, or with polenta.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g tomato passata or chopped tomatoes
steps: Blanch the beans in boiling salted water for 4 minutes, then drain.
Soften the onion and garlic in the oil over medium heat for 5 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and salt and simmer for 5 minutes, then add the beans, cover and stew gently for 12 to 15 minutes until tender.
Stir in the basil and serve warm as a side dish.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g small brown lentils (such as Castelluccio), rinsed
1 onion, 1 carrot and 1 celery stalk, finely chopped
steps: Soften the onion, carrot, celery and garlic in the oil over medium-low heat for 8 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste and lentils for 1 minute, then add the herbs and stock.
Simmer gently, partly covered, for 30 to 35 minutes until the lentils are tender and the liquid has thickened, adding salt in the last 10 minutes.
Serve as a side or main with bread; they are traditionally eaten at New Year for luck.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 x 400 g cans whole peeled San Marzano or plum tomatoes
1 small onion, finely chopped, or 2 garlic cloves
1 pinch sugar, if the tomatoes are acidic
steps: Warm the oil in a saucepan over medium-low heat and cook the onion for 6 minutes until soft and translucent.
Add the tomatoes, crushing them with a spoon, then add the salt and the sugar if needed.
Simmer uncovered for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thick and glossy.
Pass through a food mill for a smooth sauce or leave rustic, stir in the basil and use for pasta, pizza or baked dishes.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Warm the milk in a saucepan until steaming but not boiling.
Melt the butter in another pan over medium-low heat, whisk in the flour and cook the roux for 2 minutes without letting it colour.
Pour in the hot milk gradually, whisking constantly to prevent lumps.
Simmer, still whisking, for 8 to 10 minutes until thick enough to coat a spoon, then season with salt and nutmeg; press cling film on the surface if not using at once.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 large bunch flat-leaf parsley (about 60 g leaves)
1 slice stale white bread, crust removed, soaked in 1 tbsp vinegar
steps: Chop the parsley, anchovies, capers and garlic very finely by knife (or pulse briefly in a food processor).
Squeeze the bread and mash it into the mixture with the egg yolk if using.
Stir in the oil and vinegar to make a loose, bright green sauce and season with salt.
Rest for 30 minutes and serve with bollito misto, boiled meats or grilled fish.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: extra flour or semolina for dusting
steps: The night before, mix 200 g flour, 200 ml water and a pinch of the yeast into a loose biga, cover and leave at room temperature for 12 to 16 hours until bubbly.
Add the remaining flour, water, yeast, salt and oil and mix into a very wet, sticky dough; do 4 sets of stretch-and-folds in the oiled bowl every 30 minutes.
Turn onto a heavily floured surface, cut into 2 rectangles without knocking out the air, and prove on floured cloth for 45 minutes.
Bake on a hot stone or tray at 230°C with a tray of water for steam for 22 to 25 minutes until deep golden and hollow-sounding when tapped.
Cool on a rack for at least 30 minutes before slicing.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 8 slices soft white sandwich bread (pane in cassetta), crusts removed
160 g tuna in olive oil, drained
steps: Spread each slice of bread thinly with mayonnaise, right to the edges.
Fill two sandwiches with tuna and tomato and two with ham, egg and lettuce, piling the filling slightly higher in the centre.
Cover with the remaining bread, press gently and cut each diagonally into two triangles.
Wrap in damp cloth or cling film until serving so the bread stays soft, as served in Italian bars with an aperitivo.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 tbsp apricot jam, warmed, to glaze
steps: Mix the flour, sugar, eggs, milk, yeast, zests, vanilla and salt into a soft dough, knead 8 minutes, then wrap and chill for at least 2 hours.
Roll the dough into a rectangle, enclose the butter flattened into a slab, then roll and fold into thirds; repeat for 3 turns, chilling 30 minutes between each.
Roll out 4 mm thick, cut long triangles, roll each up from the wide end into a crescent and prove covered at warm room temperature for 2 to 3 hours until doubled (or overnight in the fridge).
Brush with beaten yolk and bake at 190°C for 16 to 20 minutes until deep golden, then brush with the warm jam for shine.
Serve warm for breakfast with a cappuccino, plain or filled with crema or jam.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 vanilla pod, split (or 1 tsp vanilla extract)
steps: Heat the milk, cream, vanilla and lemon zest in a saucepan over medium heat until steaming, then remove from the heat and infuse for 10 minutes.
Whisk the yolks and sugar until pale, pour in the hot milk gradually while whisking, and return to the pan.
Cook over low heat, stirring constantly, for 6 to 8 minutes until the custard (crema inglese) coats the spoon and reaches 82°C; do not boil.
Strain, add the salt, cool quickly over iced water and chill for at least 4 hours.
Churn in an ice-cream machine until thick and creamy, then freeze for 1 hour before serving in cones or cups (gelato is served slightly softer than ice cream).
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 scoops vanilla gelato (fior di latte or crema)
4 single espresso shots (about 120 ml), freshly made
20 g dark chocolate, grated, or 4 amaretti biscuits
steps: Chill 4 small glasses or cups in the freezer for 10 minutes.
Put one firm scoop of gelato into each glass.
Brew the espresso and pour one hot shot over each scoop at the table, adding amaretto if you like.
Top with grated chocolate or crushed amaretti and eat immediately while it is half melted.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 100 g torrone (Italian nougat) or toasted almonds, chopped
steps: Whisk the yolks with 80 g sugar in a bowl over simmering water for 6 to 8 minutes until thick, pale and 75°C, then cool.
Whip the cream with the vanilla to soft peaks, and separately whisk the whites with the salt and remaining sugar over simmering water to 70°C, then beat to a glossy meringue.
Fold the cream into the yolk mixture, then fold in the meringue, torrone and chocolate gently to keep the air in.
Pour into a loaf tin lined with cling film and freeze for at least 6 hours.
Turn out, slice and serve straight from the freezer with berries or chocolate sauce.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 80 ml dry or sweet Marsala wine
200 g fresh berries or 8 savoiardi biscuits, to serve
steps: Bring a pan of water to a gentle simmer and set a heatproof (ideally copper) bowl over it without touching the water.
Whisk the yolks and sugar in the bowl until pale, then add the Marsala.
Whisk constantly for 8 to 10 minutes until the mixture triples in volume, is thick enough to hold a ribbon and reaches 75°C.
Spoon warm into glasses over berries or serve with savoiardi for dipping.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Rub the butter into the flour, sugar, baking powder, salt and zest until sandy, then add the egg and yolk and bring together into a pasta frolla dough; wrap and chill for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 180°C and roll two thirds of the dough 5 mm thick to line a buttered 24 cm tart tin.
Spread the jam evenly in the base, then cut the remaining dough into strips and lay them in a lattice on top, pressing the ends to the rim.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until the pastry is golden and the jam bubbles, then cool completely before slicing.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 100 g butter, melted, or 80 ml sunflower oil
16 g baking powder (1 sachet lievito per dolci)
3 apples (about 600 g), peeled and thinly sliced
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C and grease and line a 24 cm round cake tin; toss the apple slices with the lemon juice.
Whisk the eggs and sugar for 5 minutes until pale and fluffy, then beat in the butter, milk and zest.
Fold in the flour and baking powder, then fold in two thirds of the apples and pour into the tin.
Arrange the remaining apple slices in a fan on top and bake for 40 to 45 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Cool, dust with icing sugar and serve for breakfast or merenda.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 tbsp cocoa powder, optional for a marbled cake
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C and butter and flour a 24 cm ring (bundt) tin.
Whisk the eggs and sugar for 6 minutes until thick and pale, then beat in the oil, milk and zest.
Fold in the flour and baking powder; if marbling, stir the cocoa into a third of the batter and swirl it through the plain batter in the tin.
Bake for 40 to 45 minutes until risen, golden and a skewer comes out clean, then cool and dust with icing sugar; serve with caffelatte for breakfast.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 litre sunflower or peanut oil for frying
steps: Knead the flour, sugar, eggs, butter, grappa, zest and salt into a smooth, firm dough, wrap and rest for 30 minutes.
Roll the dough very thin (1 to 2 mm), ideally with a pasta machine, and cut into rectangles with a fluted wheel, making a slit in the centre of each.
Fry a few at a time in oil at 175°C for 30 to 60 seconds per side until blistered and pale golden.
Drain on paper, cool and dust generously with icing sugar; these are the classic Carnival fritters.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 250 g dry biscuits (such as Oro Saiwa or rich tea), roughly broken
steps: Melt the chocolate over a pan of barely simmering water and let it cool slightly.
Beat the butter and sugar until creamy, add the yolks, cocoa, melted chocolate and rum, and mix until smooth.
Fold in the broken biscuits, shape the mixture into a log on baking paper, roll it tight and twist the ends.
Chill for at least 4 hours until firm, then roll in icing sugar so it looks like a salami and slice into rounds.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 200 ml freshly squeezed lemon juice (about 5 lemons)
steps: Heat the water, sugar and zest in a saucepan over medium heat for 3 minutes until the sugar dissolves, then cool completely.
Strain the syrup, stir in the lemon juice and salt, and chill for at least 2 hours.
Churn in an ice-cream machine until smooth, or freeze in a shallow tray for 4 hours, raking with a fork every 30 minutes.
Serve in small glasses as a palate cleanser between courses or after a fish dinner.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Toss the apples, pears and bananas with the lemon juice straight away to stop them browning.
Add the strawberries, peaches and grapes.
Stir in the orange juice and sugar, cover and chill for at least 1 hour so the fruit releases its juices.
Serve cold in bowls with mint, optionally with a scoop of gelato.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Fill the portafilter with the ground coffee, level it and tamp firmly and evenly.
Lock it into the machine and extract for 25 to 30 seconds into a warmed cup, aiming for about 25 to 30 ml with a thick hazelnut-coloured crema.
Stir in sugar if you like and drink at once at the bar, standing, as Italians do; with a moka pot, brew over medium-low heat until it gurgles.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Brew the espresso into a warmed 150 to 180 ml cup.
Steam the milk with the wand, first letting in air to build foam, then submerging to heat it to about 60 to 65°C until silky and glossy.
Pour the milk into the espresso, letting the foam crown the top in roughly equal parts coffee, milk and foam.
Dust with cocoa if desired and drink in the morning with a cornetto; Italians don't usually order it after lunch.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Brew the espresso into a small warmed espresso cup.
Steam the milk briefly until hot and foamy.
Spoon a small dollop of milk foam onto the espresso to "stain" it (macchiato means stained) and serve immediately.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Steam or heat and froth the milk to about 65°C until creamy with a thick foam.
Pour the milk into a tall glass and let it settle for 30 seconds so the foam rises.
Slowly pour the freshly brewed espresso through the foam so it forms a layer between the milk and foam, then serve with a long spoon.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 15 ml grappa, sambuca or brandy (bought from a licensed producer)
steps: Brew a fresh espresso into a warmed espresso cup.
Add the grappa or sambuca, stir in sugar if desired and serve at once after a meal; some bars serve the spirit on the side to pour in yourself.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Whisk the cocoa, sugar, cornflour and salt with 100 ml cold milk to a smooth paste.
Heat the remaining milk in a saucepan over medium heat until steaming, then whisk in the paste and the chopped chocolate.
Cook, whisking constantly, for 4 to 5 minutes over low heat until thick enough to coat a spoon.
Pour into cups and top with whipped cream (con panna); it should be thick enough to eat with a spoon.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.2 l light chicken or vegetable stock
0.3 g saffron threads (zafferano), soaked in 2 tbsp warm water
50 g butter and 60 g grated caciocavallo or pecorino
300 g ragù of beef and pork mince with peas, cooked thick and cooled
100 g caciocavallo or provola, cut into small cubes
150 g plain flour whisked with 250 ml water into a smooth batter
1.5 l sunflower or peanut oil for frying
steps: Simmer the rice in the stock with the saffron for about 15 minutes until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is just tender, then stir in the butter and grated cheese.
Spread the rice on a tray and cool completely, at least 1 hour, so it holds its shape.
Take a handful of rice in a damp palm, press a hollow, add a spoon of ragù and a few cheese cubes, close it and shape into a ball (Palermo, arancine) or a cone (Catania, arancini).
Dip each one in the flour batter, then roll in breadcrumbs until fully coated.
Fry in oil at 175 C, a few at a time, for 5-6 minutes until deep golden; the filling should be piping hot. Drain and serve warm.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 large aubergines (melanzane), cut into 1.5 cm slices or cubes
1 tbsp coarse salt for salting the aubergine
250 ml olive oil for frying, plus 3 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
800 g ripe tomatoes, peeled and chopped (or 2 x 400 g tins)
80 g ricotta salata, coarsely grated (substitute: feta or mild pecorino)
steps: Salt the aubergine and leave in a colander for 30 minutes, then pat dry.
Fry the aubergine in hot olive oil over medium-high heat for 4-5 minutes until golden and soft; drain on paper.
Warm the extra-virgin oil with the garlic over low heat for 2 minutes, add the tomatoes and a pinch of salt and simmer for 20 minutes until thick; tear in half the basil.
Boil the pasta in salted water until al dente, drain and toss with the sauce and two-thirds of the aubergine.
Serve topped with the remaining aubergine, plenty of ricotta salata and fresh basil.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g fresh sardines, cleaned, heads and bones removed
1 large bunch wild fennel fronds (finocchietto selvatico), about 200 g (substitute: fennel bulb fronds plus 1 tsp fennel seed)
30 g raisins (uvetta), soaked, and 30 g pine nuts
0.2 g saffron dissolved in 2 tbsp warm water
steps: Boil the fennel fronds in a large pot of salted water for 10 minutes, lift them out, chop finely and keep the green water for the pasta.
Fry the onion in the oil over medium-low heat for 8 minutes until soft, then melt in the anchovies.
Add the sardines, raisins, pine nuts and saffron and cook gently for 8-10 minutes, breaking the fish into pieces, until cooked through; stir in the chopped fennel.
Cook the bucatini in the fennel water until al dente, drain and toss with the sauce.
Serve sprinkled with toasted breadcrumbs instead of cheese.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 250 g fresh sea urchin roe (polpa di ricci), from about 40 live urchins
steps: Buy very fresh, live sea urchins from a trusted fishmonger, or pasteurised roe; keep chilled until use and use the same day.
Boil the spaghetti in salted water until just al dente.
Meanwhile warm the oil with garlic and chilli over low heat for 2 minutes, then remove the garlic and take the pan off the heat.
Drain the pasta, add to the oil with a splash of cooking water and toss; off the heat fold in the urchin roe so it warms through without scrambling.
Finish with parsley and lemon zest and serve at once.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Pasta con la Mollica (Pasta ca Muddica)

ingredients: 100 g stale bread, crust removed, crumbled into fine crumbs (muddica)
steps: Toast the breadcrumbs in a dry pan with 1 tbsp oil over medium heat, stirring, for 5 minutes until golden; set aside.
Warm the remaining oil with garlic and chilli over low heat, add the anchovies and stir for 2-3 minutes until they melt.
Boil the pasta until al dente, drain, reserving a cup of water, and toss in the anchovy oil with a splash of water.
Add half the crumbs and the parsley, toss and serve with the rest of the crumbs on top.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Pasta con il Nero di Seppia

ingredients: 600 g cuttlefish (seppia), cleaned, ink sacs reserved, body cut in strips
2 sachets (8 g) cuttlefish ink if the sacs are small
steps: Soften the onion and garlic in the oil over medium-low heat for 6 minutes.
Add the cuttlefish and cook over medium-high heat for 3 minutes, then pour in the wine and let it evaporate.
Add the passata and a little water, cover and simmer for 25 minutes until the cuttlefish is tender.
Stir in the ink diluted in a spoon of water and simmer 2 minutes until the sauce is glossy black.
Cook the spaghetti until al dente, toss with the sauce and serve sprinkled with parsley.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 large cauliflower (broccolo in Palermo), about 1 kg, cut into florets
30 g raisins, soaked, and 30 g pine nuts
0.2 g saffron dissolved in 2 tbsp warm water
steps: Boil the cauliflower in salted water for 10 minutes until tender, lift out and keep the water.
Fry the onion in the oil over low heat for 8 minutes, melt in the anchovies, then add raisins, pine nuts and saffron.
Add the cauliflower and a ladle of its water and cook for 10 minutes, mashing and stirring (arriminari) into a creamy sauce.
Cook the pasta in the cauliflower water until al dente, drain and toss with the sauce.
Serve topped with toasted breadcrumbs and, if you like, pecorino.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g ripe cherry or plum tomatoes, finely chopped raw
steps: Mix the raw tomatoes, garlic, basil, chilli, oil and a good pinch of salt in a large serving bowl and leave 10 minutes.
Boil the spaghetti in salted water until al dente.
Drain and toss straight into the raw sauce, adding a splash of cooking water.
Serve at once with plenty of grated pecorino.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g busiate (Trapani twisted pasta; substitute: fusilli lunghi or casarecce)
steps: Pound the garlic and almonds with a pinch of coarse salt in a mortar (or pulse in a processor) to a coarse paste.
Add the basil and work it in, then the tomatoes, and finally stir in the oil and pecorino to a loose, pink pesto.
Boil the busiate in salted water for about 12-15 minutes until al dente.
Drain and toss with the raw pesto and a spoon of cooking water; serve at room temperature or warm.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g minced beef and 200 g minced pork
1 onion, 1 carrot and 1 celery stalk, finely chopped
1 l tomato passata plus 2 tbsp tomato paste
2 aubergines, sliced and fried (optional, Palermo style)
200 g caciocavallo, diced, and 80 g grated caciocavallo
150 g mortadella or cooked ham, diced
60 g breadcrumbs and 4 tbsp olive oil
steps: Brown the soffritto in oil for 8 minutes, add the mince and brown well, deglaze with wine, then add passata and paste and simmer for 1 hour; add peas for the last 10 minutes.
Boil the anelletti for half their stated time, drain and mix with most of the ragù, the diced cheese, ham and half the grated cheese.
Oil a deep round tin and dust with breadcrumbs; layer the pasta with the fried aubergine, finishing with ragù, grated cheese and crumbs.
Bake at 190 C for 40 minutes until crusty, rest 15 minutes, then turn out like a timballo and slice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 large aubergines, sliced and fried in olive oil
200 g caciocavallo or tuma, diced, and 60 g grated pecorino
3 tbsp olive oil and 3 tbsp breadcrumbs
steps: Fry the onion in oil for 5 minutes, brown the mince, add passata and basil and simmer for 35 minutes.
Boil the pasta for 2 minutes less than stated, drain and mix with most of the sauce.
Line an oiled baking dish with fried aubergine, then layer pasta, egg slices, salami, diced cheese and grated pecorino, ending with sauce, pecorino and crumbs.
Cover the top with remaining aubergine and bake at 190 C for 30 minutes until bubbling; rest 10 minutes before cutting.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.5 kg mixed firm fish (scorfano, grouper, gurnard), cleaned, plus heads for stock
1 onion, 3 garlic cloves and 1 bunch parsley, chopped
1 tsp ground cinnamon and 1 pinch chilli flakes
steps: Rub the couscous with 3 tbsp oil, a little salt and a splash of water, then steam it over simmering water (or in a couscoussier) for 40 minutes, fluffing twice.
Meanwhile fry onion, garlic, parsley and almonds in the remaining oil for 5 minutes, add tomatoes, bay, chilli, saffron and 2 l water with the fish heads; simmer 30 minutes and strain.
Poach the fish pieces (and shellfish) in the strained broth for 10-12 minutes until the flesh flakes and shells open.
Put the couscous in a bowl, ladle over hot broth to moisten generously, sprinkle with cinnamon, cover with a cloth and rest 20 minutes.
Serve the couscous with the fish and extra broth on the side.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g dried split broad beans (fave secche), soaked overnight
1 small bunch wild fennel fronds, chopped (substitute: fennel fronds plus 1/2 tsp fennel seed)
200 g short pasta or broken spaghetti (optional)
steps: Drain the soaked beans and put them in a pot with onion, fennel, tomatoes and water.
Simmer gently, half covered, for 2 hours, stirring often, until the beans collapse into a thick purée; season.
If using pasta, cook it in the maccu for the last 10 minutes, adding water as needed.
Serve in bowls with a generous drizzle of raw olive oil and black pepper; leftovers set firm and can be sliced and fried.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 3 aubergines, cut into 2 cm cubes and salted
300 g tomato passata or chopped tomatoes
2 tbsp sugar and 80 ml red wine vinegar
2 tbsp toasted pine nuts or almonds and fresh basil
steps: Rinse and dry the salted aubergine, then fry in hot oil for 5 minutes until golden; drain.
Blanch the celery for 3 minutes and fry it briefly; drain.
In 3 tbsp oil soften the onion for 8 minutes, add the tomato and simmer 10 minutes, then add olives and capers.
Add the aubergine and celery, sprinkle with sugar, pour in the vinegar and cook 5 minutes until the sharp smell softens into sweet-sour (agrodolce).
Cool, rest for several hours, and serve at room temperature topped with nuts and basil.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g fresh broad beans in pods (yield about 200 g shelled)
500 g fresh peas in pods (about 200 g shelled)
4 small artichokes, trimmed and cut in wedges, kept in lemon water
1 large spring onion or 2 small onions, sliced
2 tbsp white wine vinegar and 1 tbsp sugar
1 small bunch wild fennel or mint, chopped
steps: Soften the onion in the oil over low heat for 5 minutes.
Add the artichokes and a splash of water, cover and cook 10 minutes.
Add the broad beans and peas, season, cover and cook 10-15 minutes until all are tender, adding water if dry.
Stir in the vinegar and sugar with the herbs and cook 2 minutes; serve warm or at room temperature.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g firm sheep's milk ricotta, well drained
1/2 tsp black pepper or dried chilli
steps: Heat the oven to 200 C and oil a small baking dish.
Turn the drained ricotta out into the dish, season and drizzle with oil and herbs.
Bake for 30-35 minutes until a golden-brown crust forms on top.
Serve warm or cool, sliced, with bread and salad.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 oranges (blood oranges or Tarocco if possible), peeled and sliced
1/2 tsp dried oregano or a few mint leaves
steps: Peel the oranges with a knife, removing all white pith, and slice into rounds.
Arrange on a plate with the onion and olives.
Season with salt, pepper and oregano and drizzle with olive oil; rest 10 minutes before serving.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g ripe tomatoes, cut in wedges
5 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil and 1 tbsp red wine vinegar
steps: Boil the potatoes in their skins for 20-25 minutes until a knife slides in, cool, peel and cut into chunks.
Combine with tomatoes, onion, olives and capers in a bowl.
Dress with oil, vinegar, oregano and salt, toss gently and rest 15 minutes before serving.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 600 g swordfish (pesce spada), cut into 8 very thin slices
20 g raisins and 20 g pine nuts
2 tbsp chopped parsley and 1 lemon, zested and juiced
8 bay leaves and 1 onion, cut in wedges
steps: Toast the breadcrumbs in 2 tbsp oil until golden, then mix with cheese, raisins, pine nuts, parsley, lemon zest and a little oil to a moist filling.
Flatten the swordfish slices gently, spread with filling and roll up tightly.
Thread on skewers alternating rolls with bay leaves and onion, brush with oil and roll in remaining crumbs.
Grill or bake at 200 C for 12-15 minutes, turning once, until the fish is opaque and cooked through; serve with lemon juice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 60 g green olives and 1 tbsp capers
5 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil and 2 tbsp flour
steps: Fry onion, garlic and celery in the oil for 6 minutes, add tomatoes, olives and capers and simmer 10 minutes.
Dust the swordfish with flour and sear in a hot pan for 1 minute per side.
Lay the fish in the sauce, cover and simmer for 10-12 minutes until the flesh flakes.
Scatter parsley over and serve with crusty bread.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 800 g fresh sardines, butterflied, heads and bones removed
100 g breadcrumbs, toasted in 2 tbsp oil
30 g raisins and 30 g pine nuts
2 tbsp chopped parsley and 1 tsp sugar
1 orange and 1 lemon, juice and zest
steps: Mix the toasted crumbs with raisins, pine nuts, anchovies, parsley, sugar, zest and a little juice and oil.
Put a spoonful of filling on each sardine and roll up from head to tail with the tail sticking up like a little bird (beccafico).
Pack the rolls in an oiled dish, tucking bay leaves between them, sprinkle with remaining crumbs and drizzle with oil and citrus juice.
Bake at 190 C for 18-20 minutes until the fish is cooked and the tops are golden; serve warm or at room temperature.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 fresh tuna steaks, about 2 cm thick, 180 g each
steps: Cook the onions slowly in 3 tbsp oil over low heat for 15 minutes until soft and golden.
Add the vinegar and sugar and cook 3 minutes until syrupy.
Dust the tuna with flour and sear in the remaining oil over high heat for 2-3 minutes per side, cooking it through to at least medium.
Pour the onions over the tuna, add mint and serve warm or at room temperature.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 rabbit, about 1.4 kg, cut in pieces
1 onion, sliced, and 2 celery stalks, chopped
80 g green olives and 2 tbsp capers
30 g raisins and 30 g pine nuts
80 ml red wine vinegar and 2 tbsp sugar
steps: Brown the rabbit pieces in the oil over medium-high heat for 10 minutes, then lift out.
Soften the onion and celery in the same pan for 6 minutes, return the rabbit, add wine and let it evaporate.
Add water, cover and simmer 45 minutes until the rabbit is tender and cooked through.
Add olives, capers, raisins and pine nuts, then the vinegar mixed with sugar, and cook uncovered for 10 minutes until glossy.
Rest 10 minutes and serve warm.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 800 g beef topside or veal in one large thin slice
50 g breadcrumbs and 40 g grated pecorino
100 g caciocavallo or provola, cut in sticks
1 onion, chopped, and 125 ml red wine
steps: Pound the meat into a large rectangle; mix mince, crumbs, pecorino and raw egg and spread over it.
Lay pancetta, cheese sticks and whole boiled eggs down the middle, roll up tightly and tie with string.
Brown the roll in oil on all sides for 10 minutes, add onion, then wine and let it evaporate.
Add the passata, cover and simmer gently for 1 hour 15 minutes, turning occasionally, until cooked through (70 C inside).
Rest 15 minutes, slice and serve with the sauce, which can also dress pasta.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 600 g thin beef slices (topside), about 12 pieces
1 garlic clove and 2 tbsp parsley, finely chopped
1 onion, cut in pieces, and bay leaves for the skewers
steps: Mix breadcrumbs, grated cheese, garlic, parsley, salt and pepper.
Brush the meat with oil, dip in the crumb mix, put a few cheese cubes on each and roll up.
Brush the rolls with oil, coat again in crumbs and thread onto skewers with onion and bay.
Grill over hot charcoal or under a hot grill for 10-15 minutes, turning, until golden and cooked through.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 600 g thin veal or beef slices
20 g raisins and 20 g pine nuts
1 tbsp chopped parsley and 1 tsp sugar
2 onions in wedges and 16 bay leaves
steps: Mix crumbs, cheese, raisins, pine nuts, parsley, sugar, orange juice and a little oil into a moist filling.
Spread on each meat slice, roll up and thread onto skewers alternating with onion and bay leaves.
Brush with oil and roll in extra crumbs.
Grill or bake at 200 C for 12-15 minutes, turning once, until cooked through and golden.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Whisk the flour, water and salt in a pan until smooth, then cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, for 15 minutes until very thick and it pulls from the sides.
Stir in parsley and quickly spread 5 mm thick on an oiled tray or between wooden moulds; cool 1 hour until set.
Cut into rectangles and fry in oil at 180 C for 2-3 minutes until puffed and golden.
Salt, squeeze lemon over and eat as is or in a sesame bun, often with cazzilli.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Boil the potatoes in their skins for 25 minutes until tender, peel and mash while hot.
Mix in parsley, garlic, salt, pepper and cheese; no egg is used.
Shape into finger-length cylinders and fry at 180 C for 3-4 minutes until golden.
Drain and serve hot with panelle, in a bun or on their own.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g veal spleen (meusa) and 300 g veal lung, cleaned
4 vastedda sesame buns (substitute: soft sesame rolls)
100 g caciocavallo, grated, or fresh ricotta (for maritata version)
steps: Simmer the spleen and lung in salted water with the bay leaf for 1.5-2 hours until fully cooked and tender; cool and slice thinly.
Melt the lard in a wide pan and fry the slices for 5 minutes until hot through.
Split the buns, fill generously with the meat and a spoonful of lard.
Serve "schietta" with lemon, or "maritata" topped with caciocavallo or ricotta.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg lamb or kid intestines, thoroughly cleaned and washed
steps: Buy intestines already cleaned from a butcher, rinse again several times in salted water and parboil 10 minutes.
Wrap lengths of intestine around spring onion and parsley sprigs on skewers.
Brush with oil and grill over hot coals for 15-20 minutes, turning, until crisp and fully cooked.
Season with salt, pepper and lemon and serve hot.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Bring a large pot of water to the boil with bay and peppercorns; dip the octopus three times to curl the tentacles, then submerge.
Simmer gently for 45-60 minutes until a fork slides easily into the thickest tentacle.
Rest in the water 10 minutes, then cut into pieces.
Serve warm with lemon juice, olive oil and coarse salt, as at the Palermo street stalls.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Cook the onions in oil over low heat for 15 minutes until soft, add passata and simmer 5 minutes; cool.
Cut pastry into 10 cm squares or rounds; put onion sauce, ham and mozzarella in the middle.
Fold or cover with another piece, seal well and brush with egg.
Bake at 200 C for 20-25 minutes until puffed and deep golden.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g semola rimacinata (durum wheat flour) and 7 g dried yeast
350 ml warm water, 1 tsp sugar, 2 tsp salt
steps: Mix flour, yeast, sugar, water, salt and 2 tbsp oil into a soft sticky dough; knead 10 minutes and rise 2 hours.
Cook onions in 3 tbsp oil for 15 minutes, add passata, half the anchovies and oregano and simmer 15 minutes.
Press the dough 2 cm thick into an oiled 30x40 cm tray, push in the cheese and remaining anchovies and rise 30 minutes.
Spread with the sauce, cover with crumbs mixed with oregano and drizzle with oil.
Bake at 220 C for 25-30 minutes until golden underneath and spongy inside; serve warm.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 7 g dried yeast and 300 ml warm water
1 tsp salt and 2 tbsp olive oil
400 g tomato passata cooked thick with basil
200 g caciocavallo ragusano, grated or thinly sliced
steps: Make a firm smooth dough with flour, yeast, water, salt and oil; knead 10 minutes and rise 2 hours.
Roll out into a very thin rectangle, spread with thick tomato sauce and cheese, and fold in thirds lengthwise, then fold the ends in so you have a layered loaf.
Brush with oil and bake at 200 C for 35-40 minutes until golden and crisp.
Cool slightly and slice; serve warm or at room temperature.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 600 g semola rimacinata, 7 g dried yeast, 350 ml warm water
2 tsp salt and 3 tbsp olive oil plus 1 tbsp lard
400 g tuma or fresh pecorino, sliced (substitute: young provolone)
1 cauliflower (broccolo), blanched and chopped, or 300 g broccoli
steps: Make a soft dough with flour, yeast, water, salt, oil and lard; knead and rise 2 hours.
Divide in two; roll one piece thin and line an oiled 28 cm tin, leaving the edges hanging.
Fill with layers of cheese, anchovies, cauliflower and olives, seasoning and drizzling with oil.
Cover with the second sheet, seal the edges, prick the top and brush with egg yolk.
Bake at 200 C for 40-45 minutes until deep golden; rest before slicing.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 thick slices or 1 round loaf of crusty Sicilian semolina bread
steps: Split the bread (warm it briefly if a day old) and drizzle the cut sides with olive oil.
Layer tomato, cheese and anchovies on the bottom half.
Season with oregano, salt and pepper, close and press; serve at once.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g plain flour, 100 g sugar, 100 g lard or butter, 2 eggs
200 g ground almonds and 150 g sugar
80 g dark chocolate (Modica chocolate if possible), grated
1 tsp ground cinnamon and a pinch of ground cloves
steps: Rub flour, sugar and lard together, add eggs and a little water and knead to a smooth pastry; rest 30 minutes.
Cook the mince in a dry pan with a little water for 10 minutes until fully cooked and dry; cool and grind finely.
Mix the meat with almonds, sugar, chocolate, spices and egg white to a stiff filling.
Roll the pastry thin, cut 10 cm rounds, fill, fold into half-moons, seal and cut a small slit on top.
Bake at 180 C for 20-25 minutes until golden; dust with icing sugar when cool.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg sheep's milk ricotta, drained overnight in the fridge
250 g plain flour, 25 g sugar, 30 g lard, 1 tsp cocoa
1 egg plus 1 egg white for sealing
80 ml Marsala wine and 1 tsp vinegar
1 l peanut or sunflower oil for frying (traditionally lard)
candied orange peel, pistachios and icing sugar to finish
steps: Drain the ricotta overnight, then press it through a sieve with the sugar and fold in the chocolate; chill.
Knead flour, sugar, cocoa, lard, egg, Marsala and vinegar into a firm dough; rest 1 hour.
Roll very thin, cut 10 cm ovals, wrap around metal tubes and seal with egg white.
Fry at 175 C for 2 minutes until blistered and golden, then cool and slide off the tubes.
Fill the shells just before serving, dip the ends in pistachio or candied peel and dust with icing sugar.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 sponge cake (pan di Spagna) of 4 eggs, 120 g sugar, 120 g flour, 24 cm
800 g sheep's milk ricotta, drained overnight
250 g caster sugar and 80 g dark chocolate chips
250 g green almond paste (marzipan tinted with pistachio or food colouring)
300 g icing sugar mixed with water to a fondant glaze
4 tbsp Marsala or orange syrup for brushing
steps: Bake the sponge: whisk eggs and sugar 10 minutes until thick, fold in flour and bake at 175 C for 30 minutes; cool.
Sieve the drained ricotta with sugar and fold in chocolate chips.
Line a sloped cassata tin with cling film, set alternating strips of green almond paste and sponge around the sides and a sponge disc on the base; brush with syrup.
Fill with the ricotta cream, cover with sponge and chill at least 4 hours.
Turn out, cover with white fondant glaze and decorate generously with candied fruit; keep refrigerated.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 sponge cake (from 4 eggs, 120 g sugar, 120 g flour), baked and cooled
600 g sheep's milk ricotta, drained overnight
180 g sugar and 60 g chocolate chips
steps: Sieve the ricotta with sugar and stir in chocolate and candied peel.
Line small dome moulds with thin green almond paste and a thin layer of sponge.
Fill with ricotta cream, close with a disc of sponge and chill 3 hours.
Turn out, coat with white fondant and top each with a candied cherry; keep chilled.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g plain flour, 150 g sugar, 150 g butter or lard, 2 eggs, 1 tsp baking powder
600 g sheep's milk ricotta, drained overnight
60 g dark chocolate chips and 50 g diced candied fruit
300 g icing sugar mixed with a little lemon juice and water
steps: Make shortcrust (pasta frolla) from flour, sugar, butter, eggs and baking powder; chill 30 minutes.
Sieve ricotta with sugar and stir in chocolate and candied fruit.
Line dome moulds with pastry, fill with ricotta, close with a pastry disc and bake at 180 C for 25 minutes; cool.
Turn out, glaze with white icing and set a cherry on top of each; chill before serving.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 250 ml water and 100 g butter or lard
600 g sheep's milk ricotta, drained overnight, sieved with 180 g sugar and 50 g chocolate chips
candied orange peel, chopped pistachios and candied cherries
steps: Boil water, butter, salt and sugar, add the flour all at once and stir 3 minutes until the dough comes away from the pan; cool.
Beat in the eggs one at a time to a smooth, glossy choux paste.
Drop spoonfuls into oil at 160 C and fry for 8-10 minutes, turning, until puffed, cracked and golden; drain.
Split or top each sfincia with the ricotta cream and decorate with pistachios, candied peel and a cherry.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g strong flour, 80 g sugar, 10 g fresh yeast, 2 eggs
200 ml milk and 70 g butter or lard
400 g sheep's milk ricotta, drained overnight, mixed with 120 g sugar and 40 g chocolate chips
steps: Knead flour, sugar, yeast, eggs, milk and butter into a soft brioche dough and rise 2 hours.
Divide into 8 balls, flatten each, fill with ricotta cream, seal into a round and rise 45 minutes.
Dip in beaten egg, then breadcrumbs.
Fry at 170 C for 5-6 minutes, turning, until deep golden and cooked through; dust with icing sugar and eat warm.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g plain flour, 150 g sugar, 150 g lard or butter, 2 eggs, 1 tsp baking powder
100 g raisins and 100 g almonds, toasted
50 g walnuts and 50 g dark chocolate
1 tsp cinnamon and 1/4 tsp ground cloves
coloured sprinkles (diavulicchi) and icing to finish
steps: Make a pastry with flour, sugar, lard, eggs and baking powder; chill 1 hour.
Mince the figs, raisins, nuts and chocolate with zest, honey and spices to a thick paste.
Roll pastry into strips, lay a log of filling down the centre, roll up and cut into 6 cm pieces, snipping decorative cuts.
Bake at 180 C for 20-25 minutes until lightly golden; cool, glaze with icing and add sprinkles.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 200 g dark chocolate melted with 50 g butter for the black glaze
300 g icing sugar, 2 egg whites and juice of 1 lemon for the white glaze
steps: Knead flour, eggs, yolks and alcohol into a firm dough, roll into ropes and cut into small chickpea-sized pieces.
Fry at 170 C for 3-4 minutes until golden and crisp; drain and cool.
Heap the pieces into a mound, coat half with the chocolate glaze and half with the lemon glaze (whisk icing sugar, whites and lemon juice and heat briefly in a bain-marie until glossy).
Leave to set 2 hours before serving.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Mix almond flour, sugar and zest, then work in honey and egg whites to a soft, sticky paste.
Roll into walnut-size balls, dust with icing sugar and press an almond or cherry on top.
Rest 1 hour or overnight to firm up.
Bake at 180 C for 12-15 minutes until lightly coloured but still soft inside; cool fully.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 tbsp gum arabic dissolved in 3 tbsp water for glaze
steps: Cook the sugar and water to the soft-ball stage (117 C), stir in the glucose and almond flour off the heat and work to a smooth paste.
Knead on a marble surface until cool and pliable.
Press into plaster fruit moulds or shape by hand into figs, oranges, prickly pears and so on; dry 24 hours.
Paint with food colourings and finish with gum arabic glaze for shine.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 l whole milk or almond milk
chopped pistachios and cinnamon to decorate
steps: Infuse the milk with lemon peel and cinnamon over low heat for 10 minutes, then remove them.
Whisk the cornflour and sugar with a little cold milk, add to the pan and stir constantly over medium heat for 5 minutes until thick.
Pour into wetted moulds and chill at least 4 hours.
Turn out and decorate with pistachios and a dusting of cinnamon.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 l strained watermelon juice (from about 2 kg flesh)
1 tsp jasmine water or a few jasmine flowers (optional)
30 g chopped pistachios and cinnamon to decorate
steps: Blend the watermelon and strain it, discarding seeds and pulp.
Whisk cornflour and sugar into the cold juice, then cook over medium heat, stirring, for 5-7 minutes until thick and glossy.
Cool slightly, add jasmine water and pour into bowls; when lukewarm scatter chocolate chips to look like seeds.
Chill 4 hours and finish with pistachios and cinnamon.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g whole wheat berries (grano duro), soaked 2-3 days with daily water changes
50 g dark chocolate chips and 50 g candied orange peel
steps: Drain the soaked wheat and boil with salt and bay in plenty of water for 2 hours until tender and swollen; drain and cool.
Sieve the ricotta with sugar and stir in chocolate and candied peel.
Fold the wheat into the ricotta cream, sprinkle with cinnamon and chill; it is eaten on 13 December for Saint Lucy.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Heat water and sugar until dissolved, add the zest and cool completely.
Stir in the lemon juice and pour into a shallow metal tray.
Freeze 4-5 hours, scraping and stirring with a fork every 30 minutes to form fine, creamy crystals (or churn in an ice-cream machine).
Serve in glasses with a warm brioche, as for a Sicilian summer breakfast.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 250 g blanched almonds (or 250 g unsweetened almond paste)
steps: Blend the almonds with the water for 3 minutes, steep 1 hour, then squeeze through a cloth to get almond milk.
Warm a little of the milk with the sugar to dissolve it, then mix back in and cool.
Freeze in a shallow tray for 4-5 hours, scraping with a fork every 30 minutes until creamy and fine.
Serve with brioche or topped with a little cinnamon.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Knead flour, sugar, yeast, eggs, milk, zest and honey 10 minutes, then work in the butter and salt until smooth and elastic.
Rise covered in the fridge overnight, then 1 hour at room temperature.
Divide into 10 balls of 70 g and 10 small balls of 15 g; press each small ball (the tuppo) firmly onto a large one.
Rise 2 hours until doubled, brush with yolk mixed with milk.
Bake at 180 C for 15-18 minutes until deep golden; serve with granita.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Blend the almonds with half the water for 3 minutes until very fine.
Add the remaining water, sugar and lemon peel and steep in the fridge for 2 hours.
Strain through a fine cloth, squeezing well, and serve ice-cold.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 250 ml very cold seltzer or sparkling water
steps: Pour the lemon juice into a tall glass and add the salt and sugar if using.
Top with cold seltzer and stir quickly; it will fizz up, so drink it at once as at Catania kiosks.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 g fresh yeast (or a pinch of instant yeast)
200 g San Marzano tomatoes, crushed by hand with a pinch of salt
200 g fior di latte mozzarella, torn and drained
steps: Dissolve the yeast in the water, add half the flour, then the salt and remaining flour, and knead 10 minutes into a smooth, slightly tacky dough.
Cover and leave 2 hours at room temperature, divide into two 250 g balls, then let them rise covered for 6–8 hours (or overnight in the fridge, brought back to room temperature for 2 hours).
Heat the oven with a pizza stone or steel at its maximum (250–280°C) for 45 minutes; a wood oven at 430°C is traditional.
Press each ball from the centre outwards with your fingertips, leaving a puffy rim (cornicione), and spread on a thin layer of tomato.
Bake 5–7 minutes on the stone, adding the mozzarella for the last 2–3 minutes, until the rim is blistered and the cheese bubbling.
Finish with basil, a drizzle of olive oil and the grated cheese, and serve whole, uncut, as in Naples.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g Neapolitan pizza dough (two 250 g balls, as for Margherita)
250 g San Marzano tomatoes, crushed by hand
steps: Leave the dough balls covered at room temperature until soft and airy, and preheat the oven with a stone at its maximum (250–280°C) for 45 minutes.
Season the crushed tomatoes with the salt and a little of the oil.
Stretch each ball by hand into a 30 cm round with a raised rim, spread with tomato, and scatter over garlic and oregano.
Drizzle with olive oil and bake 6–8 minutes until the rim is charred in spots and the garlic is just golden; serve at once (no cheese on a true marinara).
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g Neapolitan pizza dough (two 250 g balls)
150 g fior di latte mozzarella, diced and drained
100 g Neapolitan salame or cooked ham, diced
steps: Preheat the oven with a stone to its maximum (250–280°C) for 45 minutes.
Mix the ricotta, mozzarella, salame, Parmigiano, pepper and torn basil.
Stretch each dough ball into a 28 cm disc and spoon the filling onto one half, leaving a 2 cm border.
Fold over into a half moon, press the edges firmly to seal, and spread a spoon of passata and a drizzle of oil on top.
Bake 12–15 minutes until puffed and well browned; rest 2 minutes before serving as the filling is very hot.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g Neapolitan pizza dough (two 250 g balls)
100 g ciccioli (pressed pork cracklings) or diced salame
4 tbsp tomato sauce, cooked with a little salt
1 l sunflower or peanut oil, for frying
steps: Divide the risen dough into 4 balls and let them relax 30 minutes under a cloth.
Mix the ricotta, ciccioli, provola and pepper.
Stretch each ball into a 20 cm disc, spread a spoon of tomato on one half, add the filling and fold into a half moon, pressing the edges hard to seal.
Heat the oil to 175°C in a deep pan and fry each pizza 2–3 minutes, ladling oil over the top, until puffed and deep golden on both sides.
Drain on paper and eat immediately, wrapped in paper, as street food.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg Neapolitan pizza dough (four 250 g balls)
300 g fior di latte mozzarella, torn and drained
steps: Heat the oven with a stone at its maximum (250–280°C) for 45 minutes.
Stretch each ball into a 25 cm disc, top with salted tomato, mozzarella, basil and a drizzle of oil.
Bake 5–7 minutes until the rim is blistered and the cheese is melted.
