Fold each pizza in half and then in half again (a portafoglio, "wallet"), wrap in paper, and eat on the street while hot.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g bucatini, broken into short lengths
50 g butter and 60 g flour (for the béchamel)
100 g flour mixed with 150 ml water (batter)
1/2 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp black pepper
steps: Make a thick béchamel: melt the butter, stir in the flour 1 minute, whisk in the milk and simmer 5 minutes until very thick; season with salt and pepper.
Boil the bucatini until very al dente, drain, and mix with the béchamel, ham, peas, provola and Parmigiano.
Press the mixture 3 cm deep into a lined tray, cover and chill at least 4 hours (overnight is best) until firm.
Cut into 8 cm rounds or rectangles, dip in the flour-water batter, and fry in oil at 170°C for 4–5 minutes until golden and crisp all round.
Drain on paper and serve hot in a paper cone.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 eggs, plus 2 more beaten for coating
150 g fior di latte mozzarella, cut into small sticks
1 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp black pepper
steps: Boil the potatoes in their skins 25–30 minutes until tender, peel while warm and pass through a ricer.
Mix in 2 eggs, cheese, parsley, salt and pepper, and let cool until easy to handle.
Shape into 8 cm logs around a stick of mozzarella, then roll in beaten egg and breadcrumbs.
Fry at 170°C for 3–4 minutes, turning, until deep golden; drain and serve hot.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 7 g fresh yeast (or 3 g instant yeast)
30 g fresh sea lettuce (alghe, ulva) or dried nori, finely chopped
steps: Dissolve the yeast in the water, beat in the flour and salt to a soft, sticky batter, then fold in the seaweed (rehydrate dried seaweed 5 minutes first).
Cover and let rise in a warm place about 1 1/2 hours until doubled and bubbly.
Heat the oil to 175°C and drop in walnut-sized spoonfuls with a wet spoon, a few at a time.
Fry 3–4 minutes, turning, until puffed and golden; drain, salt lightly, and serve hot in a cuoppo.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g small squid, cleaned and cut into rings
300 g small prawns, shell on or peeled
1 l peanut or sunflower oil, for frying
steps: Pat all the seafood very dry with paper towels.
Heat the oil to 180°C in a deep, heavy pan.
Toss the seafood in semolina, shake off the excess, and fry in small batches 2–3 minutes until crisp and pale gold; the squid should be just opaque.
Drain on paper, salt at once, and serve piled into paper cones (cuoppi) with lemon wedges.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 8 slices day-old sandwich bread, crusts removed
250 g mozzarella, sliced and drained overnight on paper
steps: Make four sandwiches of bread and well-drained mozzarella, pressing the edges firmly so they seal.
Beat the eggs with milk and salt; dust each sandwich in flour, then soak 1 minute in the egg on each side.
Shallow-fry in oil at 170°C for 2–3 minutes a side until golden and the cheese is melting.
Drain on paper and serve hot, halved, so the cheese pulls in strings.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 10 g fresh yeast (or 4 g instant yeast)
steps: Dissolve the yeast in the water, then knead with flour, lard, salt and pepper for 10 minutes into a smooth dough.
Divide into 50 g pieces, roll each into two thin ropes, twist them together with 3–4 almonds pressed into the twist, and close into rings.
Set on a lined tray and leave to rise about 1 1/2 hours until puffy.
Bake at 180°C for 20 minutes, then at 150°C for 40 minutes until golden and dry right through.
Cool completely; they keep for a week and are eaten with a cold beer by the Naples seafront.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg live clams (vongole veraci), purged in salted water
1 tbsp salt, for the pasta water
steps: Soak the clams 1–2 hours in cold salted water to purge sand, discarding any that are broken or stay open when tapped.
Warm the oil with the garlic and chilli over medium heat until the garlic is golden, add the clams and wine, cover and cook 3–4 minutes until they open; discard any that stay closed.
Meanwhile cook the spaghetti in salted boiling water 2 minutes less than the packet time.
Lift out the clams, strain their juices into the pan, add the pasta and toss over high heat 2 minutes until the liquid emulsifies.
Return the clams, add parsley and serve at once (no cheese).
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 tbsp salt, for the pasta water
steps: Cook the pasta in salted boiling water until 2 minutes short of al dente, keeping a cup of the water.
Fry the garlic and chilli in the oil over medium heat until golden, then add the tomatoes and cook 3 minutes until just softened.
Add the pasta and a ladle of cooking water and toss over high heat for 2 minutes until glossy.
Finish with parsley; this "clams that ran away" dish has the scent of vongole without any seafood.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Warm the oil with garlic, chilli and anchovies over low heat, stirring until the anchovies melt.
Add the tomatoes, olives and capers and simmer 12–15 minutes until thickened.
Cook the spaghetti in lightly salted boiling water until al dente (the sauce is salty already).
Toss the pasta in the sauce over high heat 1 minute with a splash of cooking water, sprinkle with parsley and serve.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 800 g small courgettes, thinly sliced into rounds
120 g Provolone del Monaco, grated (or a mild provolone with Parmigiano)
steps: Fry the courgette slices in batches in the sunflower oil at 170°C until golden, drain, salt, and leave several hours or overnight for best flavour (or use at once).
Warm the olive oil with garlic, remove the garlic, add the fried courgettes and half the basil, and mash a third of them into a cream.
Cook the spaghetti until 2 minutes short of al dente, then finish it in the courgette pan with ladles of pasta water.
Off the heat stir in the cheese vigorously to make a creamy sauce, and serve with the remaining basil.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Fry the garlic and chilli in the oil over medium heat until fragrant, add the tomatoes and salt and cook 10 minutes, pressing them lightly, until saucy.
Cook the spaghetti until 2 minutes short of al dente.
Toss the pasta in the sauce with a ladle of cooking water for 2 minutes.
Off the heat add both cheeses and the basil, and stir quickly until creamy; serve at once.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g clams, purged in salted water
steps: Purge the clams 1–2 hours; open the mussels and clams in a covered pan with a splash of wine over high heat for 3–4 minutes, discarding any that stay closed, and strain the juices.
Fry the garlic and chilli in the oil, add the squid and prawns and cook 2 minutes, then add the remaining wine and let it bubble off.
Add the tomatoes and shellfish juices and simmer 8 minutes until saucy; the prawns should be fully pink.
Cook the paccheri until 2 minutes short of al dente, finish in the sauce with the shellfish for 2 minutes, add parsley and serve.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g scialatielli (fresh Amalfi pasta; or fresh tagliatelle)
500 g clams, purged in salted water
steps: Steam open the mussels and clams with half the wine in a covered pan for 3–4 minutes; discard any closed ones and strain the liquid.
Fry the garlic in the oil, add squid and prawns for 2 minutes until opaque, splash in the rest of the wine and let it evaporate.
Add the tomatoes and shellfish liquid and simmer 6–8 minutes.
Boil the scialatielli 4–5 minutes until just tender, toss in the sauce with the shellfish 1–2 minutes, scatter with parsley and serve.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Pasta e Patate con la Provola

ingredients: 1 onion, 1 celery stick and 1 carrot, finely chopped
2 tbsp tomato paste or 5 cherry tomatoes
1.2 l hot water or vegetable stock
1 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp black pepper
steps: Sweat the onion, celery and carrot in the oil over medium heat for 8 minutes until soft.
Add the potatoes and tomato, stir 2 minutes, then cover with hot stock and simmer 15 minutes until the potatoes start to break.
Add the pasta directly and cook, stirring often and adding hot water as needed, until al dente and the mixture is thick and creamy.
Off the heat stir in the Parmigiano and provola, cover 2 minutes until the provola melts into strings, and serve with black pepper.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg beef chuck or girello, in 2 large pieces
1 carrot and 1 celery stick, finely chopped
steps: Brown the beef and pancetta in the oil over medium-high heat for 8 minutes.
Add the carrot, celery and all the onions with the salt, cover and cook very gently 3 hours, stirring occasionally, until the onions collapse to a sweet golden cream.
Uncover, add the wine a little at a time and cook 30 minutes more, until thick and amber and the beef is fork tender.
Cook the ziti until al dente and toss with the onion sauce and Parmigiano; serve the sliced beef as the second course.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g Neapolitan salame or cooked sausage, sliced
400 g fior di latte mozzarella, diced and drained
300 g minced beef and pork, rolled into tiny polpettine and fried
steps: Make the ragù ahead (about 4 hours); fry the tiny meatballs in oil for 5 minutes until browned.
Cook the lasagna sheets 2 minutes in boiling salted water and lay them on cloths; loosen the ricotta with a ladle of ragù.
In a deep oiled dish, layer ragù, pasta, ricotta, meatballs, salame, egg, mozzarella and Parmigiano, repeating 4–5 times and ending with ragù and Parmigiano.
Cover with foil and bake at 180°C for 45 minutes, uncover and bake 15 minutes more until bubbling.
Rest 30 minutes before cutting; this is the traditional Carnival Sunday lasagna.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 250 g fior di latte mozzarella, diced and drained
steps: Boil the potatoes in their skins 25–30 minutes, peel while hot, rice onto a board and work in the flour and a pinch of salt to a soft dough.
Roll into ropes, cut into 2 cm gnocchi and keep on a floured tray.
Fry the garlic in oil, add the passata and salt and simmer 15 minutes; add basil.
Boil the gnocchi until they float, then 30 seconds more; drain and toss with the sauce.
Spread in terracotta dishes, top with mozzarella and Parmigiano, and bake at 220°C for 10 minutes until the cheese is melted and bubbling.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 l Neapolitan ragù sauce (see Ragù Napoletano)
250 g minced beef, rolled into tiny meatballs and fried
200 g Italian sausage, crumbled and browned
200 g fior di latte or provola, diced
30 g butter and 50 g breadcrumbs, for the mould
steps: Cook the rice in half the ragù plus water, risotto-style, for about 14 minutes until very al dente and thick; cool, then stir in the beaten eggs and half the Parmigiano.
Mix the meatballs, sausage, peas and a few spoons of ragù for the filling.
Butter a 24 cm ring or dome mould and coat with breadcrumbs; line with two-thirds of the rice, fill with the meat mixture, cheese and egg, then cover with remaining rice and breadcrumbs.
Bake at 180°C for 45–50 minutes until crusted, rest 15 minutes, then turn out onto a plate.
Serve in wedges with the remaining hot ragù.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 600 g beef chuck in one piece
400 g pork ribs or pork shoulder
steps: Brown all the meat well in the oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat for 15 minutes, then remove.
Soften the onion in the same oil, add the wine and reduce by half, then stir in the tomato paste and fry 2 minutes.
Add the passata, salt and the meats, bring just to a simmer and cook barely bubbling ("pippiare") 5–6 hours, partly covered, stirring often, until dark and thick and the meat falls apart.
Add basil at the end; serve the sauce on ziti or rigatoni and the meats as a second course, as on a Neapolitan Sunday.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 350 g spaghetti or leftover cooked pasta
1/2 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp black pepper
steps: Boil the spaghetti until al dente and drain well (or use leftover pasta with sauce).
Beat the eggs with cheese, parsley, salt and pepper, and mix in the pasta and provola.
Heat the oil in a 26 cm non-stick pan, add the mixture and press flat; cook on medium-low 10–12 minutes until the base is golden and crisp.
Flip onto a plate, slide back in and cook 8–10 minutes more until set through; serve warm or cold, often packed for picnics.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.5 kg aubergines, sliced lengthways 1 cm thick
400 g fior di latte mozzarella, sliced and drained
steps: Salt the aubergine slices in a colander for 1 hour, then rinse and pat dry.
Fry the slices in batches in sunflower oil at 170°C until golden on both sides; drain on paper.
Simmer the passata with olive oil, garlic, a pinch of salt and half the basil for 20 minutes.
Layer sauce, aubergine, mozzarella, Parmigiano and basil in a baking dish 4–5 times, ending with sauce and Parmigiano.
Bake at 180°C for 40 minutes until bubbling, then rest at least 1 hour; it is even better the next day.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Fry the garlic and chilli in the oil over medium heat until fragrant, add the tomatoes and salt and simmer 10 minutes until thickened.
Make 4 hollows in the sauce, crack an egg into each, cover and cook on low 5–6 minutes until the whites are set and the yolks still soft.
Sprinkle with cheese and basil and serve straight from the pan with toasted bread.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 thin beef steaks (about 600 g), such as topside
1/2 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp black pepper
steps: Sear the steaks in hot oil 1 minute per side and remove.
Fry the garlic in the same oil, add tomatoes, oregano, capers and salt and simmer 15 minutes.
Return the beef and simmer gently 8–10 minutes, turning once, until tender and cooked through.
Season with pepper and serve with bread to mop up the "pizza-maker's" sauce.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg friarielli (broccoli rabe / cime di rapa), trimmed
steps: Wash the friarielli well and trim tough stems.
Brown the sausages in 1 tbsp oil in a covered pan over medium heat, turning, for 15–18 minutes until cooked through with no pink inside.
In a wide pan fry the garlic and chilli in the remaining oil, add the wet friarielli and salt, cover and cook 10 minutes until tender, then uncover to dry slightly.
Add the sausages to the greens for 3 minutes to mingle flavours and serve with crusty bread.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 200 ml dry white wine (Ischia Biancolella if possible)
1 sprig rosemary, 4 sprigs thyme and 10 basil leaves
steps: Pat the rabbit dry; brown it in the oil with garlic over medium-high heat in a terracotta or heavy pot for 15 minutes until golden all over.
Add the wine and let it bubble until mostly evaporated.
Add tomatoes, chilli, rosemary, thyme and salt; cover and simmer gently 60 minutes until the meat is tender and comes from the bone.
Add basil and serve; the sauce is traditionally used to dress bucatini as a first course.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg octopus, cleaned (frozen and thawed is more tender)
400 g tinned peeled tomatoes or cherry tomatoes
steps: Fry the garlic and chilli in oil in a heavy pot, add the whole octopus and cook covered 10 minutes over low heat until it releases its juices and turns pink.
Add the tomatoes, olives and capers, cover tightly and simmer very gently 50–60 minutes until a knife slides easily into the thickest tentacle.
Let it rest in its sauce off the heat 10 minutes (as they say, octopus cooks in its own water).
Cut into pieces, sprinkle with parsley and serve with the sauce over toasted bread.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 kg live mussels, scrubbed and debearded
steps: Discard any mussels that are cracked or stay open when tapped.
Warm the oil with garlic in a wide pot, add the mussels, cover and cook over high heat 4–6 minutes, shaking, until all have opened; discard any that remain closed.
Add plenty of black pepper and parsley, toss well and serve at once in bowls with lemon and bread for the juices.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 whole sea bream or sea bass (about 500 g each), cleaned and scaled
steps: Fry the garlic and chilli in oil in a wide pan over medium heat for 1 minute, add tomatoes and cook 3 minutes until they begin to burst.
Add the water and salt, bring to a simmer, then lay in the fish, stuffed with a little parsley.
Cover and simmer gently 15–18 minutes, spooning the "crazy water" over, until the flesh flakes from the bone at the thickest part.
Sprinkle with parsley and serve with the broth and bread.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g pork ribs or pork shank
300 g borage or Swiss chard, chopped
1 1/2 tsp salt and 80 g grated Parmigiano
steps: Simmer the pork, prosciutto rind, Parmigiano rind and vegetables in 3 litres of water for 2 hours, skimming, until the meat is very tender.
Meanwhile blanch the greens in salted water for 5 minutes and drain.
Strip the meat from the bones, slice the sausage, and strain the broth.
Return meat and greens to the broth with salt and simmer together 30–40 minutes until "married"; serve with Parmigiano.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg pork offal (heart, lungs, liver, spleen), cleaned and diced
2 tbsp Neapolitan chilli paste (pasta di peperoncino) or 2 tsp chilli flakes
steps: Wash the offal well, blanch 5 minutes in boiling water and drain.
Melt the lard in a heavy pot and brown the offal over medium-high heat for 10 minutes, turning, until well coloured.
Add the wine and let it evaporate, then stir in tomato paste, chilli paste and herbs.
Add hot water and salt, cover and simmer 1 1/2 hours until thick and the meat is very tender and fully cooked.
Serve the dense, spicy stew over toasted bread, Neapolitan street-kitchen style.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg friarielli (broccoli rabe / cime di rapa)
steps: Wash the greens and remove tough stems and yellow leaves.
Fry the garlic and chilli in oil over medium heat for 1 minute.
Add the wet greens and salt, cover and cook 10 minutes, stirring, until tender; uncover for the last 2 minutes to evaporate excess water.
Serve warm with bread or with sausages.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 800 g aubergines, cut into 2 cm cubes
steps: Salt the aubergine cubes in a colander 30 minutes, then rinse and dry well.
Fry in sunflower oil at 170°C until golden, like little mushrooms, and drain.
Fry the garlic in olive oil, add the tomatoes and cook 6–8 minutes until soft.
Fold in the aubergines and basil for 2 minutes and serve warm or at room temperature.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 heads escarole (about 1 kg), cut into strips
steps: Wash the escarole and blanch 2 minutes in boiling water; drain and squeeze lightly.
Warm the garlic and anchovies in oil over low heat until the anchovies melt.
Add olives, capers, pine nuts and raisins and stir 1 minute.
Add the escarole, cover and cook 10–12 minutes until tender and the liquid has evaporated; serve as a side or use as a filling.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g ripe tomatoes (cuore di bue or San Marzano), sliced
400 g buffalo mozzarella (mozzarella di bufala Campana), sliced
steps: Bring the mozzarella to room temperature 30 minutes before serving.
Alternate tomato and mozzarella slices on a platter with basil leaves.
Season with salt and oregano, drizzle with olive oil and serve at once (no balsamic in the Capri original).
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Boil the cauliflower in salted water 6–8 minutes until tender but still firm; drain and cool.
Combine with papaccelle, giardiniera, olives, anchovies and capers.
Dress with oil, vinegar and salt and leave at least 1 hour; it is "reinforced" daily with more pickles through the Christmas holidays.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 10 g fresh yeast (or 4 g instant yeast)
10 g salt and 2 tsp black pepper
steps: Knead the flour, water, yeast, 80 g lard, salt and pepper 10 minutes; reserve a 100 g piece of dough for the crosses.
Roll the main dough into a rectangle, spread with remaining lard, scatter the meats and cheeses, roll up and place in a greased ring tin, ends joined.
Press the 4 raw eggs into the top and secure each with a cross of the reserved dough.
Leave to rise slowly 6–10 hours (overnight) until doubled.
Bake at 180°C for 60–70 minutes until deep golden and hollow-sounding; cool before slicing (the eggs bake hard through), traditionally eaten at Easter.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 10 g fresh yeast (or 4 g instant yeast)
10 g salt and 2 tsp black pepper
steps: Knead flour, water, yeast, 80 g lard, salt and pepper for 10 minutes into a smooth dough and let rise 2 hours.
Roll into a rectangle, spread with the remaining lard, and scatter over meats, cheeses and chopped boiled eggs (inside, unlike Casatiello).
Roll up tightly and place in a greased ring tin, joining the ends.
Let rise 4–8 hours until doubled, then bake at 180°C for 60–70 minutes until deep golden; cool before slicing.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 7 g fresh yeast (or 3 g instant yeast)
3 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil plus 4 tbsp for the filling
40 g pine nuts and 40 g raisins
steps: Knead flour, water, yeast, 3 tbsp oil and salt into a soft dough and let rise 2 hours until doubled.
Cook the escarole in 4 tbsp oil with the anchovies, olives, capers, pine nuts and raisins, covered, for 15 minutes until wilted, then uncover to dry; cool.
Line an oiled 28 cm tin with two-thirds of the dough, fill with the escarole and cover with the rest, sealing the edges and pricking the top.
Bake at 200°C for 35–40 minutes until golden; serve warm or cold, a Christmas Eve classic.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 250 g semolina cooked in 500 ml water with a pinch of salt
1 tsp cinnamon and 1 tsp vanilla extract
steps: Knead the flour, water, honey and salt into a very firm dough, rest 1 hour, then pass repeatedly through a pasta machine into a paper-thin sheet 2 m long.
Brush the sheet with lard and roll it up into a tight cylinder; wrap and chill at least 8 hours (overnight).
Cook the semolina in salted water 5 minutes until thick, cool, then blend with ricotta, sugar, candied peel, cinnamon and vanilla.
Cut the log into 1.5 cm discs, push the centre outward with your thumbs to make shell-shaped cones of fanned layers, and fill each with filling.
Bake at 200°C for 20–25 minutes until crackling and golden; dust with icing sugar and serve warm.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 10 g fresh yeast (or 4 g instant yeast)
steps: Beat the flour, yeast, sugar and eggs one at a time in a mixer 10 minutes until elastic, then add salt and butter and beat until shiny and stringy.
Fill buttered babà moulds a third full and let rise 1–2 hours until the dough reaches the rim.
Bake at 180°C for 20–25 minutes until deep golden and dry inside; cool and leave to dry for several hours.
Simmer the water, sugar and lemon zest 5 minutes, cool slightly and stir in the rum.
Soak the babà in the warm syrup until saturated and soft, squeeze gently, and serve, optionally with whipped cream.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 100 g candied citron and orange peel, diced
500 g pasta frolla (sweet shortcrust made with lard or butter)
steps: Simmer the grano cotto with milk, butter and lemon zest 15 minutes until creamy; cool.
Beat the ricotta with sugar (best rested overnight), then add yolks, wheat cream, candied peel, orange-flower water and cinnamon; fold in the stiffly whipped whites.
Line a 28 cm tin with frolla, pour in the filling and lay seven pastry strips on top in a lattice.
Bake at 180°C for 75–90 minutes until set and amber; cool and rest 1–2 days before serving, at Easter.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 80 g candied fruit and coloured sprinkles (diavulilli)
steps: Knead the flour, eggs, butter, sugar, liqueur and zest into a smooth dough and rest 30 minutes.
Roll into thin ropes and cut into 1 cm pieces, the size of chickpeas.
Fry in batches at 170°C for 1–2 minutes until golden, and drain.
Warm the honey until fluid, toss in the fried balls, candied fruit and sprinkles, and shape into a ring on a plate; set 1 hour before serving at Christmas.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 ml milk, 4 yolks, 120 g sugar and 40 g cornflour (for the custard)
steps: Make the custard: heat the milk with lemon zest, whisk yolks with sugar and cornflour, pour on the milk and cook, stirring, 3–4 minutes until thick; cover and cool.
For choux, boil water, butter and salt, tip in the flour and stir 2 minutes until it leaves the pan; cool slightly and beat in eggs one at a time.
Pipe 8 cm double-ring wheels onto squares of baking paper.
Fry at 165°C for 6–8 minutes, turning, until puffed and golden (or bake at 200°C 20 minutes then 180°C 10 minutes).
Pipe a rosette of custard in the centre, top with an amarena, dust with icing sugar; made for Saint Joseph's Day, 19 March.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 250 g floury potatoes, boiled and riced
60 g sugar plus 150 g for coating
12 g fresh yeast (or 5 g instant yeast)
steps: Knead the flour, potato, eggs, sugar, milk, yeast and zest 10 minutes, then add butter and salt and knead until smooth and elastic.
Let rise 1 1/2 hours, shape 60 g pieces into ropes and close into rings on squares of paper, and rise 1 hour more.
Fry at 170°C about 2 minutes per side until deep golden.
Roll hot in sugar and serve warm.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Melt the chocolate gently and cool slightly; heat the oven to 170°C and line a 24 cm tin.
Beat the butter and sugar until pale, add yolks one at a time, then the chocolate and ground almonds.
Whip the whites with salt to firm peaks and fold in gently.
Bake 40–45 minutes until crusted on top but still slightly moist inside; cool and dust with icing sugar (it is flourless, from Capri).
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 Amalfi or Sorrento lemons, zested and juiced
500 ml milk, 4 yolks, 100 g sugar and 40 g cornflour (lemon custard)
100 ml limoncello and 100 ml water and 50 g sugar (syrup)
steps: Whisk eggs and sugar 10 minutes until thick, fold in the flour and half the zest, and bake in buttered dome moulds at 180°C for 15–18 minutes until springy; cool.
Cook the custard: heat milk with zest, whisk with yolks, sugar and cornflour and cook until thick; cool, then fold in half the whipped cream.
Boil water and sugar, cool, add limoncello and lemon juice.
Hollow each dome from below, brush with syrup and fill with custard.
Loosen the remaining custard with cream and a little milk, coat the domes completely, and chill 1 hour before serving.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Heat milk, water, butter and zest to a simmer, rain in the semolina while whisking and cook 5 minutes until very thick; cool.
Beat the eggs with sugar until pale, then mix in the ricotta and vanilla, and combine with the semolina until smooth.
Pour into a buttered 26 cm tin and bake at 180°C for 50–60 minutes until set and golden.
Cool completely, dust with icing sugar; a Carnival cake.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 100 g candied orange and citron peel, chopped
1 tbsp pisto (Neapolitan spice mix: cinnamon, clove, nutmeg, star anise)
1/2 tsp baking ammonia or baking powder
steps: Mix all the dry ingredients with the almonds, candied peel and zest.
Add water gradually to make a firm, sticky dough and rest 30 minutes.
Shape 70 g pieces into ropes, close into rings and flatten slightly; brush with water.
Bake at 180°C for 20–25 minutes until golden and firm; cool (they are hard and meant for dunking in wine or coffee at Christmas).
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 tbsp pisto spice mix (cinnamon, clove, nutmeg)
1/2 tsp baking ammonia or baking powder
steps: Warm the honey, sugar and water until dissolved, then mix with flour, cocoa, spice, zest and raising agent into a soft dough.
Roll 1 cm thick and cut into diamonds about 8 cm long.
Bake at 180°C for 15–20 minutes until set; cool.
Dip in melted dark chocolate and leave to harden; a Neapolitan Christmas biscuit.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 ml fresh pig's blood, filtered (from a licensed butcher; or omit for the modern blood-free version)
1 tsp cinnamon and 1 tsp vanilla extract
steps: Whisk the sugar, cocoa, cornflour and cinnamon into the cold milk until smooth, and strain in the blood.
Cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until it comes to the boil and simmers 5 minutes, thick and glossy (it must reach a full boil to be safe).
Off the heat stir in the chocolate, vanilla and candied citron until smooth.
Pour into bowls, cool and serve with savoiardi or chiacchiere at Carnival.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 8 unwaxed Sorrento or Amalfi lemons (Sfusato Amalfitano)
1 l neutral grain spirit, 95% (bought from licensed producers; or 1.5 l 40% vodka)
steps: Limoncello is a lemon liqueur from the Sorrento coast, made by infusing lemon peel in bought neutral spirit; it is served ice-cold in small chilled glasses after meals.
Peel the lemons thinly with no white pith and steep the peels in the spirit in a sealed jar in a dark place for 7 days, shaking daily.
Boil the water and sugar 5 minutes until clear and let cool completely.
Strain out the peels, stir the spirit into the syrup, bottle and rest at least 1 week; store in the freezer and drink responsibly.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 150 g guanciale (cured pork cheek), cut into short strips; pancetta is the common substitute
4 large egg yolks plus 1 whole egg
80 g Pecorino Romano DOP, finely grated, plus extra to serve
1 tbsp coarse salt for the pasta water
steps: Bring a large pot of water to the boil, salt it lightly (the pecorino and guanciale are salty) and cook the spaghetti until just al dente, about 9–10 minutes.
Meanwhile put the guanciale in a cold wide pan and render it over medium-low heat for 8–10 minutes until the fat is clear and the edges are crisp but still slightly chewy; turn off the heat.
Whisk the yolks, whole egg, pecorino and most of the pepper into a thick cream in a bowl, loosening it with 1–2 tbsp of hot pasta water.
Drain the pasta, keeping a cup of water, and toss it in the guanciale pan off the heat so it is coated in the fat.
Pour in the egg cream and toss quickly, adding splashes of pasta water, until it turns glossy and creamy without scrambling; the residual heat should bring the sauce to about 70 °C.
Serve at once with extra pecorino and black pepper; no cream, garlic or onion in the Roman version.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g tonnarelli (square egg-free fresh spaghetti) or spaghetti
200 g Pecorino Romano DOP, very finely grated
1 tbsp coarse salt for the pasta water
steps: Toast the peppercorns in a dry wide pan over medium heat for 1 minute until fragrant, then crush them coarsely in a mortar and return half to the pan.
Cook the pasta in less water than usual, lightly salted, so the water becomes starchy; cook until 1 minute short of al dente.
In a bowl, mash the pecorino with a few tablespoons of warm (not boiling) pasta water into a smooth, thick paste.
Add a ladle of pasta water to the pepper pan, transfer the pasta with tongs and toss over low heat for 1 minute until the water is mostly absorbed.
Take the pan off the heat, add the pecorino cream and toss vigorously, adding pasta water a spoon at a time until it forms a smooth, clinging sauce with no clumps.
Serve immediately with the remaining crushed pepper on top.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 150 g guanciale, cut into thick strips (pancetta as substitute)
400 g canned San Marzano tomatoes, crushed by hand
60 g Pecorino Romano (or Pecorino di Amatrice), grated
1 tbsp coarse salt for the pasta water
steps: Render the guanciale in a dry pan over medium heat for 6–8 minutes until golden and translucent, then lift out half the pieces to keep crisp.
Add the chilli, pour in the wine and let it bubble for 1 minute until the smell of alcohol is gone.
Add the tomatoes and simmer over medium-low heat for 15 minutes until the sauce thickens and the fat separates at the edges.
Meanwhile boil the bucatini in salted water until al dente, about 10–11 minutes.
Drain, toss into the sauce with the reserved guanciale and a splash of pasta water, then off the heat stir in most of the pecorino.
Serve with the remaining pecorino scattered over.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 200 g guanciale, cut into strips (pancetta as substitute)
80 g Pecorino Romano DOP, finely grated
1 tbsp coarse salt for the pasta water
steps: Cook the guanciale in a cold wide pan brought slowly to medium-low heat for 10 minutes until the fat runs and the strips are golden.
Boil the pasta in lightly salted water until 1 minute short of al dente.
Add a ladle of pasta water to the guanciale fat and swirl to form a light emulsion.
Transfer the pasta to the pan and toss over low heat for 1 minute, adding water as needed.
Off the heat, add the pecorino and pepper and toss hard until the sauce turns creamy and coats each piece; serve at once.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 dried red chillies (peperoncino), crumbled, or 1 tsp chilli flakes
steps: Warm the olive oil in a pan over low heat with the garlic and chilli for 2–3 minutes until the garlic is pale gold, not brown.
Add the tomatoes and salt and simmer over medium heat for 15 minutes until thick and glossy.
Boil the penne in salted water until al dente.
Drain and toss the pasta in the sauce over high heat for 1 minute with a splash of pasta water.
Finish with parsley and a drizzle of raw oil; Romans traditionally serve it without cheese, but vegetarian-rennet pecorino can be added.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 100 g best-quality unsalted butter, cut into cubes and softened
100 g Parmigiano Reggiano (aged 24 months), very finely grated
1 tbsp coarse salt for the pasta water
steps: Put the butter in a warmed wide serving bowl or pan.
Cook the fresh fettuccine in salted boiling water for 2–3 minutes until tender, then lift it out with tongs and keep a cup of the water.
Toss the pasta with the butter and 3–4 tbsp of pasta water until the butter melts into a pale sauce.
Add the Parmigiano in two batches, tossing vigorously and adding water as needed, until silky and creamy; no cream is used in the original.
Serve at once, with black pepper if liked.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 600 g pajata (milk-fed veal intestine with the chyme left in), cleaned by the butcher; ox tail tomato sauce is the usual stand-in where unavailable
steps: Cut the pajata into 15 cm lengths and tie each into a ring with kitchen string; rinse well and pat dry.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat, soften the onion and garlic for 6 minutes, then brown the pajata rings for 5 minutes.

Pour in the wine and let it evaporate, then add the tomatoes, chilli and salt, cover and simmer gently for 1 1/2–2 hours until the pajata is very tender and the sauce is thick and creamy (the chyme thickens it); make sure it is fully cooked through.
Boil the rigatoni until al dente, drain and toss with plenty of the sauce.
Serve the pasta with pecorino as the first course and the pajata rings as the second.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Bring the milk to a simmer with the salt, nutmeg and 30 g butter, then rain in the semolina while whisking constantly.
Cook over low heat, stirring with a wooden spoon, for 10–12 minutes until very thick and pulling from the sides of the pan.
Off the heat, beat in the yolks and half the cheese, then spread the mixture 1 cm thick on a wet tray and cool for at least 30 minutes until firm.
Cut into 5 cm discs, arrange them overlapping like roof tiles in a buttered baking dish, dot with the remaining butter and scatter the rest of the cheese.
Bake at 200 °C for 20–25 minutes until golden and crisp on top; rest 5 minutes before serving.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.2 litres homemade chicken or beef broth (brodo)
1 tbsp fine semolina or dry breadcrumbs
steps: Bring the broth to a steady simmer and season with salt.
Beat the eggs with the cheese, semolina, parsley and nutmeg in a bowl until smooth.
Pour the egg mixture into the simmering broth in a thin stream while whisking gently with a fork.
Simmer for 2–3 minutes until the egg sets into soft, ragged shreds ("stracci"); serve hot with extra cheese.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 skate wing (arzilla), about 800 g, skinned by the fishmonger; any firm white fish frames as substitute
1 onion, 1 celery stick and 1 bunch parsley for the stock
steps: Simmer the skate with the onion, celery, parsley and salt in 2 litres of water for 20 minutes until the flesh flakes off the cartilage; lift out, pick the flesh and strain the stock.
In a soup pot warm the oil over low heat with the garlic, anchovies and chilli until the anchovies melt, about 3 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes, then pour in the fish stock and bring to the boil.
Add the broccoli florets and cook for 8 minutes, then add the broken spaghetti and cook until al dente, about 8 minutes more.
Return the skate flesh to the pot to heat through and serve with a drizzle of raw olive oil.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g Roman meat ragù (beef and pork simmered in tomato)
150 g fior di latte mozzarella, cut into small batons and drained
1 litre sunflower or peanut oil for frying
steps: Combine the rice and ragù in a pan, then cook over medium heat adding hot broth a ladle at a time for 16–18 minutes until the rice is al dente and the mixture is thick.
Stir in the butter and Parmigiano, spread on a tray and cool completely, at least 30 minutes (or overnight in the fridge).
Take a tablespoon-sized portion in your palm, press a mozzarella baton in the middle and close into a 7 cm oval croquette.
Dip each one in beaten egg, then roll in breadcrumbs; repeat for a thicker crust.
Fry in oil at 175 °C for 4–5 minutes, turning, until deep golden; drain and serve hot so the cheese stretches like a telephone cord ("supplì al telefono").
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 600 g pollo alla cacciatora or coda alla vaccinara (Roman stew), hot
steps: Mix the flour, yeast and water, then add salt and oil and knead for 10 minutes; let rise for 3–4 hours until doubled.
Press the dough into an oiled rectangular tray 1.5 cm thick and let it rise 1 hour more.
Bake at 250 °C for 18–20 minutes until golden with an airy crumb (pizza bianca style), then cool slightly.
Cut into 10 cm squares, then cut each diagonally into triangles and slice open each triangle into a pocket.
Fill each pocket generously with the hot stew (cooked through, at least 2 hours of simmering), top with pecorino and serve wrapped in paper.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 3 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, plus extra for the tray
250 g fior di latte mozzarella, diced and drained
steps: Mix the flour, yeast and 350 ml water until shaggy, then add the salt, oil and remaining water and knead until smooth and very wet.
Cover and refrigerate for 24 hours (cold fermentation) for a light, bubbly dough, then bring to room temperature for 2 hours.
Stretch the dough gently into a well-oiled 30 x 40 cm tray with your fingertips, keeping the bubbles, and spread over the passata seasoned with salt and oil.
Bake on the lowest rack at 250 °C for 15 minutes, then add the mozzarella and bake 8–10 minutes more until the base is crisp and the cheese melted.
Top with basil, cut into rectangles with scissors and sell or serve by weight as Roman bakeries do.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 600 g salt cod (baccalà) fillet, thick part
1 tsp dried yeast or 1/2 tsp baking powder
1 litre sunflower or peanut oil for frying
steps: Soak the salt cod in cold water in the fridge for 24–48 hours, changing the water 3–4 times a day, until pleasantly salty.
Whisk the flour, yeast, salt and sparkling water into a smooth batter thick enough to coat a spoon and rest it for 30 minutes.
Remove skin and bones, pat the cod very dry and cut into 4 x 10 cm strips.
Dip each strip in batter and fry in oil at 180 °C for 4–5 minutes until puffed, crisp and golden and the fish is opaque throughout.
Drain on paper and serve hot with lemon, as in the Roman friggitorie.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Mix the flour, yeast, malt and most of the water, then add the salt, 1 tbsp oil and the rest of the water, kneading until the dough is very soft and elastic.
Cover and leave in the fridge for 18 hours, then at room temperature for 2 hours until bubbly.
Turn onto a floured surface, stretch into a long thin rectangle and dimple the surface deeply with your fingertips.
Brush with the remaining oil, sprinkle with flaky salt and rosemary and bake on a hot stone or tray at 250 °C for 15–20 minutes until golden and crisp outside, soft within.
Serve warm, plain or split and filled with mortadella or figs.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 125 g fior di latte mozzarella, cut into 12 sticks and drained
steps: Gently open each flower, remove the pistil and wipe clean without washing.
Tuck a stick of mozzarella and half an anchovy inside each flower and twist the petals closed.
Whisk the flour, salt and sparkling water into a light, lump-free batter.
Dip the flowers in batter and fry in oil at 180 °C for 2–3 minutes, turning once, until pale gold and crisp.
Drain on paper, sprinkle with salt and serve immediately.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg young fresh broad beans (fave) in their pods
200 g Pecorino Romano, young or aged
steps: Pile the raw broad beans in their pods in a basket or on a board.
Cut the pecorino into rough chunks or shards.
Serve together, letting everyone shell and eat the raw beans with bites of cheese; this is the traditional 1 May picnic snack in Rome.
Offer olive oil and pepper on the side and a glass of Lazio white wine, bought from licensed producers, for adults.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 large Roman artichokes (carciofi romaneschi or mammole)
1 small bunch Roman mint (mentuccia/nepitella), substitute with mint
steps: Trim the artichokes, snapping off the tough outer leaves, peel the stems and cut the tips; rub with lemon and keep in lemon water.
Chop the mint, parsley and garlic with a pinch of salt and pepper, then gently open the leaves and press the mixture into the centre of each artichoke.
Stand the artichokes upside down (stems up) close together in a deep pot, pour in the oil and water and season with salt.
Cover with a damp cloth under the lid and cook over low heat for 25–30 minutes until a knife slides easily into the heart.
Serve warm or at room temperature with the cooking oil spooned over.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 large round Roman artichokes (mammole); globe artichokes as substitute
1 litre extra-virgin olive oil or sunflower oil for frying
steps: Remove the tough outer leaves, then trim the artichokes in a spiral into a rounded rose shape; peel the stem and soak in lemon water for 15 minutes.
Drain well, then open them slightly by tapping upside down, and season the inside with salt and pepper.
Fry submerged in oil at 140 °C for 12–15 minutes until tender in the centre, then drain upside down and cool 10 minutes.
Press each artichoke on a board to splay open the leaves like a flower and fry again at 180 °C for 2–3 minutes until bronze and crisp.
Drain on paper, sprinkle with salt and serve hot, as in Rome's Jewish Ghetto.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg wild or cultivated chicory (cicoria), trimmed and washed; dandelion greens or broccoli rabe as substitutes
steps: Boil the chicory in salted water for 8–10 minutes until tender, then drain and squeeze out excess water.
Warm the oil in a wide pan over medium-low heat with the garlic and chilli for 2 minutes until the garlic turns pale gold.
Add the chicory, roughly chopped, and sauté ("ripassare") over medium heat for 5–6 minutes, stirring, until it absorbs the oil.
Season with salt and serve as a side to roasts or with pizza bianca.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 young artichokes, trimmed and cut into wedges
1 kg fresh broad beans in the pod, shelled (about 300 g)
1 kg fresh peas in the pod, shelled (about 300 g)
steps: Warm the oil in a wide pan over medium-low heat and cook the guanciale and spring onions for 5 minutes until soft and the fat runs.
Add the artichoke wedges, season, pour in the wine and simmer covered for 10 minutes.
Add the broad beans and cook 5 minutes, then the peas and cook 5 minutes more, adding a splash of water if dry.
Stir in the lettuce and mint and cook uncovered for 3–4 minutes until the lettuce wilts and the vegetables are tender.
Rest 10 minutes and serve lukewarm with bread; this spring stew is at its best in April and May.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 head puntarelle (Catalogna chicory shoots); Belgian endive or frisée as substitute
steps: Separate the hollow shoots, slice them lengthwise into thin strips and soak in iced water for 30 minutes until they curl.
Pound the anchovies and garlic to a paste in a mortar, then whisk in the vinegar and oil to make a creamy dressing.
Drain the puntarelle and dry very well.
Toss with the anchovy dressing just before serving.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 8 thin veal escalopes (about 500 g), pounded thin
steps: Lay a slice of prosciutto and a sage leaf on each escalope and pin with a toothpick.
Dust the meat side lightly with flour.
Heat the butter and oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat and cook the escalopes meat-side down for 2 minutes, then prosciutto-side for 1 minute, until just cooked through.
Remove the meat, pour in the wine and scrape the pan, reducing for 1–2 minutes into a glossy sauce.
Spoon the sauce over the saltimbocca and serve immediately.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.5 kg oxtail, cut at the joints
4 celery sticks, 1 chopped and 3 cut into 5 cm lengths
240 ml dry red or white wine
2 tbsp each raisins and pine nuts
steps: Blanch the oxtail in boiling water for 10 minutes, drain and pat dry.
Heat the oil and guanciale in a heavy pot over medium heat and brown the oxtail on all sides for 10 minutes.
Add the chopped onion, carrot, celery and garlic and cook 5 minutes, then pour in the wine and let it evaporate.
Add the tomatoes and enough water to almost cover, then simmer covered over low heat for 3–4 hours until the meat falls from the bone.
Boil the celery lengths in salted water 10 minutes, add them to the stew with the cocoa, raisins and pine nuts and simmer 15 minutes more; serve with bread, and use the sauce for rigatoni.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 12 milk-fed lamb chops (abbacchio), frenched; young lamb chops as substitute
steps: Flatten the chops slightly and marinate with the oil, garlic, rosemary and pepper for 2 hours.
Heat a grill or griddle until very hot (charcoal is traditional).
Grill the chops for 2–3 minutes per side until well browned outside and cooked to at least medium (63 °C inside).
Salt them off the heat and serve immediately with lemon, eaten by hand while "scorching the fingers" (scottadito).
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.2 kg milk-fed lamb shoulder and leg (abbacchio), cut into pieces on the bone
steps: Heat the oil in a heavy pan over medium-high heat and brown the lamb all over for 10 minutes, seasoning with salt.
Add the garlic, rosemary, sage and chilli, then pour in the wine and let it evaporate.
Cover and cook over low heat for 50–60 minutes, adding splashes of water, until the meat is tender and cooked through.
Pound the anchovies with a little rosemary and the vinegar, stir into the pan and cook uncovered for 5 minutes until the sauce is reduced and glossy.
Serve hot with roast potatoes.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg pre-cooked honeycomb beef tripe, cut into strips
1 onion, 1 carrot, 1 celery stick, finely chopped
1 small bunch Roman mint (mentuccia), substitute with mint
steps: Blanch the tripe in boiling salted water for 10 minutes and drain.
Heat the oil and guanciale in a pot over medium heat and soften the onion, carrot and celery for 8 minutes.
Add the tripe, pour in the wine and let it evaporate, then add the passata and salt.
Simmer covered over low heat for 1 1/2–2 hours until the tripe is very tender, adding water if needed.
Stir in the mint, serve topped with lots of pecorino; Romans eat it on Saturdays.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 3 large red and yellow peppers, cut into strips
steps: Brown the chicken in the oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat for 10 minutes, seasoning with salt.
Add the garlic, pour in the wine and let it evaporate.
In a separate pan fry the onion and peppers in a little oil for 10 minutes until soft.
Add the tomatoes and peppers to the chicken and simmer covered for 35–40 minutes until the chicken reaches 75 °C at the bone and the sauce is thick.
Finish with herbs; it is the traditional Roman Ferragosto (15 August) dish, served warm or at room temperature.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 800 g lamb pluck (coratella: lungs, heart, liver), cleaned and cut into small pieces
4 artichokes, trimmed and cut into thin wedges
steps: Cook the onion in the oil over medium-low heat for 6 minutes until soft, add the artichokes and cook 10 minutes until tender.
Add the lungs first and cook 5 minutes over high heat, then the heart for 3 minutes, and finally the liver for 2–3 minutes.
Pour in the wine and cook until evaporated and all the offal is cooked through with no pink juices.
Season with salt, pepper and lemon juice and serve hot; it is a Roman Easter dish.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 600 g beef sirloin or topside, sliced very thin into strips
steps: Toss the beef strips lightly in flour.
Heat the oil with the garlic and rosemary in a large pan over high heat, then remove the garlic.
Add the beef in a single layer and sear for 1–2 minutes, tossing, until browned and cooked through.
Pour in the wine and reduce for 1 minute, season with salt.
Serve the strips on a bed of rocket topped with Parmigiano shavings.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g leftover boiled beef (bollito), finely chopped
150 g stale bread, soaked in milk and squeezed
steps: Combine the beef, bread, eggs, cheese, garlic, parsley and salt and knead into a firm mixture.
Shape into oval patties about 6 cm long and roll in breadcrumbs.
Fry in oil at 175 °C for 4–5 minutes, turning, until golden and hot in the centre.
Drain on paper and serve hot, or simmer for 10 minutes in tomato sauce as Roman nonnas do.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 600 g leftover boiled beef (lesso), sliced or shredded
steps: Cook the onions in the oil over low heat for 15 minutes until soft and golden.
Add the chilli and tomatoes and simmer for 10 minutes until slightly thickened.
Add the boiled beef and salt and simmer gently for 15 minutes until heated through and coated in sauce.
Finish with basil and serve with bread.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 kg boneless pork belly with loin attached, skin on
1 tbsp wild fennel pollen or fennel seeds, crushed
steps: Score the meat side, rub with salt, pepper, garlic, rosemary and fennel, then roll tightly with the skin outside and tie with string.
Dry the skin overnight uncovered in the fridge for 24 hours for crackling.
Roast at 160 °C for 3 1/2–4 hours until the internal temperature reaches 70 °C.
Raise the oven to 240 °C for 20–30 minutes until the skin crackles and puffs.
Rest 30 minutes, slice thin and serve in rosette rolls, as at the fraschette of Ariccia in the Castelli Romani.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 ml whipping cream, whipped with 2 tbsp icing sugar
steps: Mix the flour, sugar, yeast, eggs, milk and zest, then knead in the butter and salt until smooth; rise 2–3 hours until doubled.
Divide into 8 pieces, shape into ovals and let rise on a tray for 1 1/2 hours.
Brush with milk and bake at 180 °C for 15–20 minutes until golden; cool completely.
Slice each bun open lengthwise and fill generously with the whipped cream, smoothing it flat.
Dust with icing sugar and serve for breakfast with a cappuccino.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 large eggs (1 for pastry, 1 for filling)
250 g visciole (sour cherry) jam; morello cherry jam as substitute
steps: Rub the flour, butter and 120 g sugar into crumbs, then add 1 egg and the lemon zest and bring into a pastry dough; chill 30 minutes.
Beat the ricotta with the remaining sugar and egg until smooth.
Roll two-thirds of the pastry to line a 24 cm tart tin, spread with the sour cherry jam and top with the ricotta mixture.
Cover with lattice strips from the remaining dough.
Bake at 180 °C for 40–45 minutes until golden and the filling is set; cool completely before slicing, as in the Ghetto bakeries.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 ml crema pasticcera (milk, egg yolks, sugar, lemon zest)
steps: Bring the water, butter and salt to the boil, add the flour all at once and stir over low heat for 2 minutes until it forms a ball.
Cool slightly, then beat in the eggs one at a time to a smooth, glossy choux paste.
Pipe 5 cm rounds onto a lined tray and bake at 200 °C for 25–30 minutes until puffed and dry (or fry in oil at 170 °C for the traditional version).
Cool, cut open and fill with custard.
Dust with icing sugar and top with an amarena cherry; eaten for St Joseph's Day (19 March).
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Mix the eggs, sugar, butter, zest and sambuca, then add the flour and baking powder and knead into a soft dough.
Pinch off walnut-sized pieces and roll into balls.
Fry at 160 °C for 4–5 minutes until golden and puffed and cooked inside.
Drain and roll in sugar while warm; a Carnival sweet.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 100 g walnuts, 100 g hazelnuts, 100 g almonds, toasted and chopped
2 tbsp olive oil and 2 tbsp flour with 1 pinch saffron for glaze
steps: Warm the honey and chocolate gently until melted, then mix with the nuts, raisins, peel, spices and flour into a dense dough.
Shape into 2 oval loaves on a lined tray.
Mix the oil, flour, saffron and a little water into a thin yellow batter and brush over the loaves.
Bake at 170 °C for 35–40 minutes until set and golden; cool fully before slicing; a Christmas sweet.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 150 g sugar, plus 100 g for coating
125 ml dry white or red wine
steps: Mix the wine, oil and sugar, then add the flour, baking powder and anise and knead into a soft dough.
Roll into thin 12 cm ropes and form small rings.
Dip the tops in sugar.
Bake at 180 °C for 18–20 minutes until golden; serve with wine for adults, bought from licensed producers.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 200 ml sour cherry (amarena) syrup or tamarind syrup
100 g fresh fruit (cherries, strawberries or coconut)
steps: Shave the ice block by hand into fine flakes.
Pack into cups.
Pour over syrup and lemon juice.
Top with fresh fruit and serve at once, as at the Tiber kiosks in summer.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.2 kg T-bone or porterhouse steak (Chianina beef if available), 5 cm thick
2 tbsp Tuscan extra-virgin olive oil, to serve
steps: Take the steak out of the fridge 1 hour before cooking so it comes to room temperature, and do not salt it yet.
Build a very hot wood-charcoal fire (or heat a cast-iron grill pan on high for 10 minutes) until the coals are glowing white.

Grill the steak about 5 minutes per side without moving it until a dark crust forms, then stand it upright on the bone for 5 to 7 minutes until the centre reaches about 50 C for the traditional rare (al sangue) finish.
Rest the steak on a board for 5 minutes, then season generously with salt and pepper.
Carve the fillet and sirloin off the bone, slice thickly, drizzle with olive oil and serve with lemon wedges and rocket.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g dried cannellini beans, soaked overnight
300 g cavolo nero (Tuscan black kale), stems removed, shredded
1 onion, 2 carrots and 2 celery sticks, finely diced
6 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, plus extra to serve
300 g stale Tuscan unsalted bread, sliced
1 tsp salt and black pepper to taste
steps: Simmer the soaked beans in 2 litres of fresh water for about 1 hour until tender, then blend half of them with some of their liquid and keep the rest whole.
Soften the onion, carrot, celery and garlic in the olive oil over medium-low heat for 10 minutes, then add the tomatoes and cook 5 minutes.
Add the cavolo nero, cabbage, potatoes, bean purée and bean liquid, season, and simmer gently for 1 hour until the greens are very soft; stir in the whole beans.
Layer the bread slices and the soup in a pot, finishing with soup, and leave to rest for a few hours or overnight.
Reheat ("ribollire", re-boil) the next day over low heat, stirring until thick, and serve with a generous drizzle of raw olive oil and black pepper.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g stale Tuscan bread, crusts removed, torn
800 g ripe tomatoes, peeled and chopped (or canned peeled tomatoes)
6 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, plus extra to serve
1 tsp salt and black pepper to taste
steps: Warm 4 tbsp olive oil with the garlic over low heat for 2 minutes until fragrant but not browned.
Add the tomatoes and half the basil, season, and simmer for 15 minutes until the tomatoes break down.
Add the bread and the hot stock, stir, and cook on low heat for 15 minutes, stirring often, until the bread dissolves into a thick porridge.
Remove from heat, tear in the remaining basil and rest 10 minutes; serve warm or at room temperature with a drizzle of raw olive oil.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 handful wild greens or chard, chopped
1.2 litres water or light vegetable stock
1 pinch chilli flakes and 1 tsp salt
steps: Cook the onions and celery in the olive oil over low heat for 20 minutes until very soft and sweet.
Add the tomatoes, greens and chilli and cook 10 minutes, then pour in the water, salt it and simmer for 20 minutes.
Crack the eggs one by one into the simmering soup and poach for 3 to 4 minutes until the whites are set.
Put a slice of toasted bread in each bowl, sprinkle with pecorino, ladle over the soup with one egg per bowl and serve hot.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg white or red onions, thinly sliced
1 carrot and 1 celery stick, finely diced
1 tsp sugar and 1 pinch ground cinnamon
50 g Parmigiano or Pecorino Toscano, grated
steps: Cook the onions, carrot and celery in the olive oil over low heat, covered, for 30 minutes until soft and golden, stirring often.
Add the wine, sugar and cinnamon (a Renaissance Florentine touch) and let the wine evaporate for 2 minutes.
Pour in the stock, season and simmer uncovered for 30 minutes until the soup is thick and sweet.
Place a slice of toast in each bowl, cover with cheese, ladle over the onion soup and serve hot.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 250 g farro (emmer wheat, ideally Farro della Garfagnana), rinsed
200 g dried borlotti beans, soaked overnight
1 onion, 1 carrot and 1 celery stick, finely diced
5 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, plus extra to serve
steps: Simmer the beans in the water with the sage for about 1 hour until tender, then blend half of them with their liquid.
Soften the onion, carrot, celery, garlic and rosemary in the oil for 10 minutes over medium-low heat, then stir in the tomato paste.
Add the bean purée, the whole beans and the farro, season and simmer 30 to 40 minutes, stirring often, until the farro is tender but still chewy (pearl barley is a substitute).
Serve hot with a thread of raw olive oil and black pepper.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.5 kg mixed fish and seafood (gurnard, monkfish, dogfish, squid, octopus, mussels, prawns), cleaned and cut
steps: Fry the sliced garlic, chilli and sage in the olive oil over medium heat for 2 minutes, then add the octopus and squid and cook 10 minutes.
Add the wine and let it evaporate, then add the tomatoes and stock and simmer 20 minutes until the octopus is tender.
Add the firm fish pieces first and cook 8 minutes, then the delicate fish, prawns and mussels for 5 more minutes until the fish flakes and the mussels open (discard any that stay closed).
Rub the toasted bread with the whole garlic cloves and place in deep bowls.
Ladle the Livornese fish stew over the bread and serve immediately.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g stale Tuscan unsalted bread, thickly sliced
steps: Soak the bread in cold water for 10 minutes, then squeeze it very dry with your hands and crumble it into a bowl.
Soak the onion slices in cold water for 10 minutes to soften their bite, then drain.
Add the tomatoes, cucumber, onion and torn basil to the bread.
Dress with oil, vinegar, salt and pepper, toss well and rest in the fridge for 30 minutes before serving cool.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 small artichoke or 1 head red chicory, cut in wedges
8 tbsp new-season extra-virgin olive oil (olio nuovo)
steps: Wash all the raw vegetables, cut them into sticks or wedges and keep them in iced water for 10 minutes for crunch, then pat dry.
Mix the olive oil with salt and pepper in small individual bowls, one per person.
Arrange the vegetables upright in glasses or on a platter and let everyone dip them into their own oil.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g durum and soft wheat flour mixed (or 400 g dried pici)
6 cloves aglione (giant Valdichiana garlic) or 8 regular garlic cloves, sliced
800 g ripe tomatoes, peeled and chopped (or canned)
steps: Knead the flour with the water, 1 tbsp oil and a pinch of salt for 10 minutes into a smooth dough, rest it 30 minutes covered, then roll pieces between your palms into thick spaghetti 3 to 4 mm wide.
Cook the garlic very gently in the remaining oil over low heat for 10 minutes, without browning, until soft.
Add the tomatoes and chilli, season and simmer 25 minutes, mashing the garlic into a thick sauce.
Boil the pici in salted water for 5 to 7 minutes (12 to 15 for dried) until al dente, drain and toss in the sauce; serve with pecorino.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg wild boar shoulder (cinghiale), cubed (pork shoulder as substitute)
750 ml red wine (Chianti) for marinade and cooking
1 onion, 1 carrot and 1 celery stick, finely diced
2 garlic cloves, 2 bay leaves and 1 sprig rosemary
steps: Marinate the boar overnight in the fridge with half the wine, the bay, rosemary and juniper, then drain and pat dry, discarding the marinade.
Brown the meat in the oil in a heavy pot over high heat for 10 minutes, then add the diced vegetables and garlic and soften 10 minutes.
Add the remaining wine, let it reduce by half, then add the tomatoes, season, cover and simmer on low for 2 to 2.5 hours until the meat is falling apart, adding water if needed.
Shred the meat into the sauce with a fork.
Boil the pappardelle in salted water for 3 to 4 minutes, drain and toss with the ragù before serving.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 50 g Parmigiano, grated, plus 20 g Pecorino
steps: Whisk the flour, water and salt into a smooth thin batter and rest it 10 minutes.
Heat a cast-iron testo or heavy frying pan over medium-high heat, oil it lightly and cook ladlefuls of batter into thin pancakes for 2 to 3 minutes per side until set; cool and cut into diamonds.
Pound or blend the basil, pine nuts, garlic and a pinch of salt, then stir in the cheeses and olive oil to make the pesto.
Drop the testaroli into boiling salted water, turn off the heat and leave 2 minutes, drain and toss with the pesto.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g "00" flour and 4 eggs for the pasta
300 g mixed minced beef and pork
80 g stale bread soaked in milk, squeezed
1 egg and 60 g Parmigiano, grated, for the filling
1 pinch nutmeg and 1 tsp chopped marjoram
500 ml beef ragù (meat sauce), to serve
steps: Knead the flour and eggs for 10 minutes into a firm smooth dough and rest it, wrapped, for 30 minutes.
Brown the minced meat in the oil over medium-high heat for 10 minutes until cooked through, then cool and mix with mortadella, bread, egg, Parmigiano, nutmeg, marjoram, salt and pepper.
Roll the dough thinly, cut 8 cm circles, put a teaspoon of filling on each, fold into half-moons and press the edges firmly with a fork.
Boil the tordelli in salted water for 4 to 5 minutes until they float and are tender.
Drain and layer with hot meat ragù and extra Parmigiano, as is done in Lucca.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g sheep's milk ricotta, well drained
80 g Parmigiano, grated, plus extra to serve
2 tbsp plain flour, plus extra for dusting
steps: Wilt the spinach in a dry pan for 3 minutes, squeeze it completely dry and chop it very finely.
Mix the spinach with ricotta, eggs, Parmigiano, flour, nutmeg and salt into a soft dough, then chill 20 minutes.
Shape walnut-sized balls with floured hands and roll them lightly in flour.
Poach the gnudi in gently simmering salted water for 3 to 4 minutes until they float, lifting them out with a slotted spoon.
Melt the butter with the sage over medium heat until foaming and nutty, spoon over the gnudi and serve with Parmigiano.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 3 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil and 20 g butter
100 ml Vin Santo or dry white wine
steps: Soften the onion in the oil and butter over medium-low heat for 8 minutes.
Add the livers and brown over medium-high heat for 5 minutes, then add the wine and let it evaporate.
Add the stock and cook covered on low for 15 minutes until the livers are cooked through with no pink.
Add the anchovies and capers and chop everything coarsely on a board (or pulse briefly), then season.
Toast the bread slices, dip the edges quickly in warm stock if you like, spread with the liver pâté and serve warm.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 6 tbsp new-season extra-virgin olive oil (olio nuovo)
steps: Toast the bread over embers or under a hot grill for 2 minutes per side until crisp and lightly charred.
Rub one side of each hot slice firmly with the cut garlic.
Pour the olive oil generously over each slice, sprinkle with salt and eat immediately, ideally in November with the new oil.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg lampredotto (abomasum, the fourth stomach of the cow), cleaned (honeycomb tripe as substitute)
1 onion, 1 carrot and 1 celery stick, halved
1 large bunch parsley, 2 garlic cloves, 2 anchovies and 1 tbsp capers for salsa verde
6 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil and 1 tbsp red wine vinegar
1 tsp chilli oil (optional) and 1 tsp salt
steps: Rinse the lampredotto well and simmer it in a large pot of salted water with the onion, carrot, celery, tomatoes and parsley stems for 2 to 2.5 hours until very tender.
Blend the parsley, garlic, anchovies, capers, oil and vinegar into a loose salsa verde.
Slice the hot lampredotto into strips, season with salt and pepper.
Cut the rolls open, dip the top half quickly in the cooking broth, fill with lampredotto, add salsa verde and chilli oil, and serve hot like a Florentine street cart.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Whisk the chickpea flour and water into a smooth batter, add the salt and leave it to rest for at least 4 hours, skimming off any foam.
Heat the oven to its maximum (250 to 280 C) and pour the oil into a large shallow copper or steel pan.
Stir the batter, pour it into the pan to about 5 mm deep and stir gently so the oil swirls through.
Bake on the lowest rack for 20 to 25 minutes until golden and crisp on top, then slice, grind on pepper and eat hot, often inside a focaccia as in Livorno.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg pre-cooked honeycomb tripe, cut in strips
1 onion, 1 carrot and 1 celery stick, finely diced
steps: Blanch the tripe in boiling water for 5 minutes, drain and rinse.
Soften the onion, carrot, celery and garlic in the oil over medium-low heat for 10 minutes.
Add the tripe and cook 5 minutes, then add the wine and let it evaporate.
Add the tomatoes, season and simmer covered on low for 45 to 60 minutes until the tripe is tender and the sauce is thick.
Stir in half the Parmigiano and serve with the rest on top and Tuscan bread.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.5 kg beef shin, cut in large chunks
10 garlic cloves, unpeeled and lightly crushed
6 slices Tuscan bread, toasted, to serve
steps: Put the beef, garlic, crushed pepper, salt and tomato paste in a terracotta or heavy pot.
Pour over the wine until the meat is just covered.
Cover and cook in a 150 C oven (or on very low heat) for 4 hours, stirring occasionally, until the meat falls apart and the sauce is dark and glossy, adding water if it dries.
Serve hot over toasted bread or with polenta, as the brick-makers of Impruneta did.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.5 kg pork loin on the bone (or boneless loin)
2 tsp salt and 1 tsp black pepper
steps: Heat the oven to 180 C and mix the garlic, rosemary, fennel, salt and pepper into a paste with 2 tbsp oil.
Make deep cuts between the bones and the meat and rub the paste into the cuts and all over the loin; tie with string.
Place in a roasting tin with the potatoes and remaining oil, pour in the wine and roast for about 1.5 hours, basting often, until the internal temperature reaches 63 to 65 C.
Rest the roast 10 minutes, slice between the bones and serve with the potatoes and pan juices; it is also excellent cold.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g chicken livers, hearts and cockscombs (or livers and hearts only), trimmed
steps: Blanch the cockscombs (if using) in boiling water for 5 minutes and peel them; cut the livers and hearts into pieces.
Soften the onion in the butter over low heat for 6 minutes, then add the giblets, dust with flour and cook over medium heat for 5 minutes.
Add the stock and simmer 15 minutes until the giblets are cooked through.
Off the heat, whisk the egg yolks with the lemon juice and stir them into the pan so they thicken into a silky sauce without scrambling; season and serve hot with bread.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 600 g pork liver, cut in 12 pieces
200 g pork caul fat (rete), soaked in warm water
2 tsp salt and 1 tsp black pepper
4 slices Tuscan bread, cut in squares
steps: Season the liver pieces with fennel, salt and pepper.
Wrap each piece in a square of caul fat with a bay leaf.
Thread onto skewers, alternating with bread squares and bay leaves.
Brown in the oil in a pan over medium-high heat for 5 minutes, add the wine, then cook 15 minutes on medium, turning, until the caul is crisp and the liver is cooked through.
Serve hot with greens or turnip tops.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 tsp salt and 1 tsp black pepper
steps: Flatten the spatchcocked chicken and marinate it in the fridge for 2 hours with the garlic, herbs, lemon juice, oil, chilli and pepper.
Heat a heavy cast-iron pan over medium heat, salt the chicken and lay it skin side down.
Weigh it down with a foil-wrapped brick (mattone) or a heavy pan and cook 20 minutes until the skin is deep golden and crisp.
Flip, replace the weight and cook another 15 to 20 minutes until the juices run clear and the thigh reaches 75 C; rest 5 minutes and serve with lemon.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.5 kg wild boar shoulder, cubed (pork shoulder as substitute)
1 bottle (750 ml) red wine, half for marinade
1 onion, 1 carrot and 1 celery stick, chopped
steps: Marinate the boar overnight in the fridge in half the wine with the herbs and juniper; drain, rinse and dry it.
Put the meat in a dry pot over medium heat for 10 minutes to release its water, then drain.
Add the oil, vegetables and garlic and brown everything for 10 minutes, then pour in the remaining wine and let it reduce by half.
Add the tomatoes, olives and seasoning, cover and simmer on low for 2.5 hours until very tender.
Serve hot with soft polenta or Tuscan bread.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Cook the onions in the oil over low heat for 25 minutes, covered, until very soft and sweet but not browned.
Add the tomatoes and chilli and simmer 10 minutes.
Add the beef and stock, season and simmer gently for 15 minutes until the meat is heated through and has absorbed the sauce.
Serve hot with Tuscan bread to mop up the onion sauce.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Fry the garlic and chilli in the oil over medium heat for 1 minute, then add half the parsley.
Add the tomatoes, season and simmer 10 minutes until slightly thickened.
Lay the mullets in the sauce in one layer, cover and cook gently for 8 to 10 minutes, without turning, until the flesh is opaque and flakes easily.
Sprinkle with the remaining parsley and serve with Tuscan bread.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 800 g salt cod (baccalà), soaked 48 hours, cut in pieces
steps: Soak the salt cod in cold water in the fridge for 48 hours, changing the water 3 times a day, then dry it well and skin and bone it.
Dust the cod with flour and fry in 5 tbsp oil over medium-high heat for 2 minutes per side until golden; set aside.
In another pan soften the onion and garlic in 3 tbsp oil for 5 minutes, add the tomatoes and chilli and simmer 15 minutes.
Lay the cod in the sauce and simmer gently for 10 minutes until heated through and flaky; sprinkle with parsley and serve.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g dried cannellini beans, soaked overnight (or 2 x 400 g cans, drained)
steps: Simmer the soaked beans in fresh water for 1 hour until tender, then drain, keeping a cup of the liquid.
Fry the garlic and sage in the oil over medium heat for 2 minutes until the sage crackles.
Add the tomatoes and cook 10 minutes, then add the beans and a little cooking liquid.
Season and simmer 15 minutes until thick and creamy; serve as a side, classically with grilled sausages.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g dried cannellini beans, soaked overnight
steps: Put the soaked beans, garlic, sage, 4 tbsp oil and water into a straw-stripped glass flask (fiasco) or an ovenproof lidded terracotta pot.
Plug the flask loosely with cotton wool (or cover the pot) so steam escapes.
Cook very slowly in the embers of a fire or in a 140 C oven for 3 to 4 hours until the beans are creamy and tender, topping up with hot water if needed.
Drain, season with salt, pepper and the remaining raw olive oil and serve warm.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Mix the flour, yeast, water, 2 tbsp oil and fine salt, knead 10 minutes and let rise covered for 1.5 hours until doubled.
Spread the dough in an oiled baking tray, cover and let rise 45 minutes.
Press dimples all over with your fingers, then drizzle with the remaining oil mixed with 2 tbsp water and sprinkle with coarse salt and rosemary.
Bake at 220 C for 20 to 25 minutes until golden and crisp at the edges; serve warm.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg black wine grapes (Canaiolo, or Concord as substitute)
steps: Make a dough with flour, yeast, water, 2 tbsp oil and salt, knead 10 minutes and let rise 1.5 hours until doubled.
Divide in two, stretch half into an oiled tray and cover with half the grapes, half the sugar and a drizzle of oil.
Cover with the second sheet of dough, press the edges, top with the remaining grapes, sugar, aniseed and oil, and rise 30 minutes.
