Bake at 190 C for 40 to 45 minutes until the dough is golden and the grapes are bursting and jammy; cool before slicing.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 200 g sourdough starter (or 7 g dried yeast)
steps: Mix the starter with the water, add the flour and knead for 15 minutes into a firm smooth dough, adding no salt as is traditional in Tuscany.
Let it rise covered for 6 to 8 hours (2 hours with dried yeast) until doubled.
Shape into a long oval loaf, dust with flour and let it rise on a floured cloth for 1.5 hours.
Bake on a hot stone at 230 C for 15 minutes, then at 200 C for 30 to 35 minutes until the crust is pale golden and the base sounds hollow.
Cool completely before slicing; serve with salty cured meats and soups.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g chestnut flour (farina di castagne), sifted
steps: Whisk the chestnut flour, salt and water into a smooth runny batter with no lumps.
Oil a 30 cm round tin well and pour in the batter about 1 cm deep.
Scatter the pine nuts, raisins, walnuts and rosemary over the top and drizzle with the remaining oil.
Bake at 200 C for 30 to 35 minutes until the top cracks and turns dark brown; serve warm or cool, with ricotta if liked.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Whisk the chestnut flour, salt and water into a smooth pourable batter and rest 10 minutes.
Heat a nonstick or cast-iron pan over medium heat and brush it lightly with oil (traditionally the batter is baked between hot stone discs, testi, lined with chestnut leaves).
Pour in a ladle of batter, spread thin and cook 2 minutes per side until set and spotted.
Fill each warm necci with a spoonful of ricotta, drizzle with honey, roll up and serve.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Mix the flour, sugar, baking powder, salt and zest, then work in the eggs and yolk to a firm dough and knead in the almonds.
Shape into flat logs about 4 cm wide on a lined tray and brush with beaten egg.
Bake at 180 C for 25 minutes until golden, then cool 10 minutes.
Slice diagonally into 1.5 cm biscuits, lay them flat and bake again at 160 C for 10 to 15 minutes until dry and crisp; serve dipped in Vin Santo.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 250 g candied orange and citron peel, chopped
2 tsp ground cinnamon and 1 tsp mixed spice (cloves, nutmeg, coriander, pepper)
steps: Mix the nuts, candied peel, flour and spices in a large bowl, and line a 22 cm tin with wafer paper.
Heat the honey and sugar together over low heat, stirring, until it reaches the soft-ball stage (about 115 C).
Pour the hot syrup into the nut mixture, stir quickly and press into the tin with wet hands.
Bake at 150 C for 30 to 35 minutes, cool completely, then dust with icing sugar and cut into thin wedges.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 220 g icing sugar, plus extra for coating
1 tbsp candied orange peel, finely chopped
steps: Mix the almonds, icing sugar, zest, candied peel and almond extract.
Whisk the egg whites to soft peaks and fold them in to form a soft paste.
Shape into oval diamonds about 1 cm thick, roll in icing sugar and place on wafer paper or a lined tray; leave to dry uncovered overnight.
Bake at 150 C for 12 to 15 minutes until cracked on top but still pale and soft inside; cool before serving.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g plain flour, 180 g butter, 150 g sugar and 2 eggs for the pastry
120 g sugar and 50 g cornflour for the custard
steps: Rub the butter into the flour, then add sugar, eggs and half the zest to form a short pastry, and chill 30 minutes.
Heat the milk with the remaining zest, whisk the yolks with sugar and cornflour, pour the hot milk over and cook, stirring, over low heat for 5 minutes until thick; cool.
Line a 24 cm tart tin with two thirds of the pastry, fill with custard and cover with the remaining pastry, sealing the edges.
Brush with water, scatter with pine nuts and bake at 175 C for 40 to 45 minutes until golden.
Cool completely and dust with icing sugar before serving.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g sponge cake (pan di Spagna), sliced
100 ml Alchermes liqueur mixed with 50 ml water (or cherry brandy)
steps: Line a dome-shaped bowl with cling film, then line it with sponge slices brushed with the diluted Alchermes, keeping some slices for the base.
Whip the cream with the icing sugar to soft peaks, divide in two, and fold chocolate and cocoa into one half and candied fruit and almonds into the other.
Spread the white cream over the sponge lining, fill the centre with the chocolate cream and cover with the remaining soaked sponge.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or freeze for 2 hours until firm.
Turn out onto a plate, dust with cocoa and icing sugar in segments and slice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 60 g sugar, plus 100 g for coating
500 ml pastry cream (crema pasticcera) or jam, to fill
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, milk, eggs, sugar, zest and salt, then knead in the butter for 10 minutes into a soft elastic dough; rise covered 2 hours until doubled.
Roll 1.5 cm thick, cut 8 cm rounds and let them rise on floured trays for 45 minutes.
Fry in oil at 170 C for 2 to 3 minutes per side until deep golden and cooked through.
Drain, roll in sugar while warm, then pipe pastry cream into the side of each bombolone.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 40 g icing sugar and 1 tbsp cocoa powder for the top
steps: Make a starter with 100 g flour, the yeast and milk and let it bubble for 30 minutes.
Add the remaining flour, yolks, sugar, orange zest and juice, vanilla and fat, and beat for 10 minutes into a soft sticky dough.
Spread into a buttered 30 x 20 cm tin and let rise 2 to 3 hours until doubled.
Bake at 180 C for 25 to 30 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Cool, dust thickly with icing sugar and stencil the Florentine lily (giglio) in cocoa on top; serve plain or split and filled with whipped cream at Carnival.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Mix the flour, yeast, milk, sugar, eggs and salt, then knead in the butter for 10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Knead in the aniseed and drained raisins and let rise covered for 2 hours until doubled.
Shape into a long loaf or ring, place on a lined tray, slash the top and let rise 1 hour.
Brush with beaten egg and sugared water and bake at 180 C for 35 to 40 minutes until deep golden; serve sliced, ideally with strawberries in wine as in Lucca.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Fill a mixing glass with ice and add the gin, Campari and vermouth (all bought from licensed producers).
Stir for 20 to 30 seconds until well chilled.
Strain into an old-fashioned glass over fresh ice and garnish with the orange peel, as first mixed in Florence for Count Camillo Negroni.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g "00" flour, plus extra for dusting
1 each carrot, celery stick and small onion, finely diced
2 tbsp tomato paste plus 300 g passata
30 g butter and 1 tbsp olive oil
50 g Parmigiano Reggiano, grated, to serve
steps: Melt the butter with the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat, render the pancetta 3 minutes, then add the carrot, celery and onion (the soffritto) and cook gently 10 minutes until soft and golden.
Raise the heat, add the beef and pork and brown for 10 minutes, breaking up lumps, then pour in the wine and simmer until it has evaporated.

Stir in the tomato paste and passata with 250 ml water, cover partly and simmer on the lowest heat for 3 hours, stirring the milk in a little at a time during the last hour; season with salt and pepper.
Meanwhile make a well in the flour, crack in the eggs, knead 10 minutes to a smooth firm dough, wrap and rest 30 minutes, then roll very thin (the sfoglia), roll up loosely and cut into 7 mm ribbons.
Boil the tagliatelle in well-salted water for 2–3 minutes until just tender, drain, toss in a wide pan with most of the ragù for 1 minute and serve topped with more ragù and Parmigiano.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 100 g fresh spinach, blanched, squeezed dry and finely chopped
steps: Knead the "00" flour with the eggs and spinach into a smooth green dough (pasta verde), rest 30 minutes, roll thin and cut into sheets about 10 x 20 cm.
Make a béchamel: melt the butter over medium heat, whisk in the flour for 2 minutes, then whisk in the warm milk and cook 8–10 minutes until it coats a spoon; season with salt and nutmeg.
Blanch the pasta sheets 30 seconds in boiling salted water, then cool them in cold water and lay them on cloths.
Butter a baking dish and layer: béchamel, pasta, ragù, béchamel, Parmigiano, repeating for at least 6 layers and finishing with ragù, béchamel, Parmigiano and dots of butter.
Bake at 180°C for 35–40 minutes until bubbling and browned at the edges, then rest 15 minutes before cutting.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 350 g gramigna pasta (short curly tubes; substitute garganelli or short egg pasta)
300 g fresh pork sausage (salsiccia), casing removed
100 ml single cream (optional, as in many Bologna trattorie)
steps: Soften the onion in the oil over medium-low heat for 8 minutes.
Add the crumbled sausage, raise the heat and brown for 8–10 minutes until cooked through with no pink, then add the wine and let it evaporate.
Stir in the passata, season lightly and simmer 15 minutes; stir in the cream for the last 2 minutes if using.
Boil the gramigna in salted water until al dente, drain, toss with the sauce and a handful of Parmigiano, and serve with more cheese.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 350 g garganelli (ridged egg-pasta quills; substitute penne rigate)
100 g prosciutto crudo di Parma, cut into strips
steps: Melt the butter in a wide pan over medium heat and soften the shallot for 4 minutes.
Add the peas with 3 tbsp water and cook 5–7 minutes until tender, then add the prosciutto and stir for 1 minute.
Pour in the cream and simmer 2 minutes until slightly thickened.
Cook the garganelli in salted water until al dente, toss them into the sauce with half the Parmigiano and a splash of pasta water, and serve with pepper and the rest of the cheese.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g sweet shortcrust pastry (pasta frolla), homemade or bought
500 ml ragù made with veal and pork
20 g dried porcini, soaked and chopped
steps: Warm the ragù with the porcini and simmer 15 minutes.
Boil the pasta until quite firm (3 minutes under al dente), drain and toss with the ragù, béchamel, Parmigiano, butter and truffle if using.
Line a buttered deep 24 cm tin with two thirds of the frolla, fill with the pasta and cover with the remaining pastry, sealing the edges and cutting a small steam hole.
Brush with egg yolk and bake at 180°C for 45–50 minutes until the crust is deep golden.
Rest 15 minutes, unmould and serve warm in wedges, as is traditional at Ferrara feasts.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 3 tbsp olive oil or 30 g butter
300 g passata plus 1 tbsp tomato paste
steps: Heat the fat in a heavy pot over medium heat, render the pancetta 3 minutes, then add carrot, celery and onion and stew 10 minutes until soft.
Add the beef and brown over medium-high heat for 10 minutes, stirring until it crackles and loses its raw colour.
Pour in the wine and simmer until evaporated, then add the passata, tomato paste and a ladle of broth.
Cover partly and simmer at the barest bubble for 3 hours, adding broth as needed and the milk gradually in the last hour; season with salt and pepper.
Serve on fresh tagliatelle or use in lasagne; Bolognesi never serve it with spaghetti.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg beef and capon (or chicken) pieces with bones, for broth
1 each onion, carrot, celery stick for the broth
100 g pork loin, sautéed in butter until cooked through
1 egg plus pinch of nutmeg for the filling
300 g "00" flour and 3 eggs for the pasta
steps: Simmer the meats and vegetables in 3 litres of cold salted water for 3 hours, skimming, then strain and keep the clear broth hot.
Grind the cooked pork, prosciutto and mortadella very finely, then mix with the Parmigiano, 1 egg and nutmeg; chill the filling.
Knead the flour and eggs into a firm dough, rest 30 minutes, roll paper-thin and cut 3 cm squares.
Put a chickpea-sized dot of filling on each square, fold into a triangle, then wrap the two corners around a fingertip and pinch together to form the navel-shaped tortellino.
Cook the tortellini in the simmering broth for 3–4 minutes until they float and are tender, and serve in bowls of broth with Parmigiano.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 litres capon or chicken and beef broth, strained
100 g raviggiolo or squacquerone cheese (substitute stracchino)
80 g Parmigiano Reggiano, grated, plus extra to serve
100 g chicken or capon breast, cooked in butter until no longer pink
1 egg plus pinch of nutmeg and lemon zest
300 g "00" flour and 3 eggs for the pasta
steps: Finely chop the cooked chicken and mix with ricotta, raviggiolo, Parmigiano, egg, nutmeg and lemon zest to a firm paste; this is the Romagna-style filling.
Knead flour and eggs into a dough, rest 30 minutes, roll thin and cut 4 cm squares.
Place a hazelnut of filling on each square, fold into a triangle, seal, then bring the two corners together around a finger to form the little hat (cappelletto).
Bring the broth to a gentle boil, add the cappelletti and cook 4–5 minutes until tender.
Serve in hot broth with grated Parmigiano, the classic Christmas first course in Romagna.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g "00" flour and 3 eggs for the pasta
steps: Brown the beef with the vegetables in a little butter, add the wine and cook covered on the lowest heat for 4 hours (traditionally longer) until it yields a thick dark sugo; cook to an internal temperature well past 70°C.
Moisten the breadcrumbs with the hot strained cooking juices, then mix with Parmigiano, 2 eggs and nutmeg to a firm filling (the meat itself is served as a second course in Parma/Piacenza).
Knead flour and eggs, rest 30 minutes, roll thin, dot with small balls of filling, cover with a second sheet and cut with a 3 cm round fluted cutter, sealing well.
Simmer the anolini in the broth for 3–4 minutes until tender and serve in the broth with more Parmigiano.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g cow's-milk ricotta, drained overnight if wet
100 g Parmigiano Reggiano, grated, plus extra
300 g "00" flour and 3 eggs for the pasta
steps: Mix the ricotta, Parmigiano, parsley, egg, nutmeg and a little salt into a smooth filling.
Knead flour and eggs into a dough, rest 30 minutes, roll thin and cut 7 cm squares.
Place a walnut of filling in each square, fold into a triangle, seal and wrap the corners around your finger to make large tortelloni.
Cook in gently boiling salted water for 4–5 minutes until tender.
Meanwhile melt the butter with the sage until fragrant and foaming, then toss the drained tortelloni in it and serve with Parmigiano.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 100 g Parmigiano Reggiano, grated, plus extra
300 g "00" flour and 3 eggs for the pasta
steps: Blanch the chard in salted boiling water for 3 minutes, cool, squeeze very dry and chop finely.
Mix chard with ricotta, Parmigiano, egg, nutmeg and salt.
Knead flour and eggs, rest 30 minutes, roll thin into long strips, dot with spoonfuls of filling, fold over and cut into 6 cm rectangles, pressing out air and sealing.
Cook in salted boiling water 4–5 minutes, drain and serve in the Parma way, layered with melted butter and plenty of Parmigiano (traditional on the night of San Giovanni, 23 June).
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g "00" flour and 3 eggs for the pasta
steps: Halve and seed the squash and roast at 190°C for 50–60 minutes until very soft, then scoop out and mash the flesh.
Mix the squash with half the Parmigiano, nutmeg, salt and enough breadcrumbs to make a firm filling (in Ferrara it is not sweetened; in Mantua amaretti and mostarda are added).
Knead flour and eggs, rest 30 minutes, roll thin and cut 7 cm squares; fill each with a spoonful, fold into a triangle and twist the corners together into a large hat.
Boil in salted water 4–5 minutes, drain and toss in butter melted with sage until foaming; serve with the rest of the Parmigiano.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 250 g borlotti beans, soaked overnight (or 2 x 400 g cans)
50 g Parmigiano or Grana Padano, grated
steps: Simmer the soaked beans in fresh water for 60 minutes until tender (canned beans just need draining).

Scald the breadcrumbs with 150 ml boiling water, mix with the flour and enough warm water to make a firm dough, knead 5 minutes, roll into thin ropes and cut chickpea-sized pieces, pressing each with the thumb on the board to make a little shell (the pisarei of Piacenza).
Melt the butter, fry the lardo and onion over medium heat for 8 minutes, add the passata and simmer 15 minutes, then add the beans with a ladle of their liquid and simmer 15 minutes more.
Boil the pisarei in salted water 5–6 minutes until they float and are cooked, drain, stir into the beans and serve with grated cheese.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 150 g fine dry breadcrumbs (from day-old bread)
150 g Parmigiano Reggiano, grated, plus extra
1 tbsp beef marrow or soft butter
Zest of 1/2 lemon and a pinch of nutmeg
steps: Mix breadcrumbs, Parmigiano, eggs, marrow, lemon zest and nutmeg into a firm, slightly sticky dough and rest it 20 minutes.
Bring the broth to a gentle boil.
Press the dough through a passatelli iron or a potato ricer with large holes, cutting the strands to 4 cm lengths directly over the broth.
Simmer 1–2 minutes until the passatelli rise to the surface, then serve immediately in the broth with extra Parmigiano.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 cotechino di Modena, about 800 g (or a precooked vacuum-packed one)
1 carrot and 1 celery stick, finely chopped
steps: Prick the raw cotechino in several places, soak 2 hours in cold water, then put it in a pot of cold water, bring slowly to a simmer and cook gently 2.5–3 hours until fully cooked (a precooked one needs only 20 minutes in its pouch in boiling water).
Meanwhile soften the onion, carrot and celery in the oil over medium heat for 10 minutes.
Add the rinsed lentils, tomato paste, bay leaf and broth and simmer 30–40 minutes until tender, adding broth as needed; season with salt and pepper.
Slice the hot cotechino about 1 cm thick and serve on the lentils, the New Year's Eve dish said to bring prosperity.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 zampone di Modena IGP, about 1.2 kg (stuffed pig's trotter; precooked is common)
steps: For raw zampone, soak in cold water overnight, prick the skin, wrap in cloth, tie, and simmer gently in plenty of water for 4 hours; for precooked, simmer the sealed pouch 30–40 minutes.
Boil the potatoes until tender, mash with hot milk, butter and Parmigiano and season.
Unwrap the zampone, drain, and slice thickly through the skin.
Serve hot with the purè, lentils or braised spinach and a spoonful of mostarda.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 veal escalopes, about 120 g each, pounded thin
8 thin slices prosciutto crudo di Parma
80 g Parmigiano Reggiano, shaved or grated
steps: Dip the veal in egg, then press into breadcrumbs on both sides.
Fry in the butter over medium heat for 3 minutes per side until golden and cooked through.
Lay two slices of prosciutto on each cutlet and cover with Parmigiano.
Add the broth to the pan, cover and simmer 4–5 minutes until the cheese has melted and the breading has absorbed some broth.
Serve at once with the pan juices and truffle shavings if you have them.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 salama da sugo IGP from Ferrara, about 1 kg (cured, spiced pork sausage aged in a bladder; order from Italian delis)
steps: Soak the salama in lukewarm water overnight to soften the casing.

Wrap it in a cloth, tie it to a wooden spoon laid across a tall pot so it hangs without touching the bottom, cover with water and simmer gently for 6 hours (4 hours for a smaller one), topping up with hot water.
Shortly before serving, boil the potatoes and mash with milk, butter, salt and nutmeg.
Lift out the salama, cut open the top of the casing and spoon out the soft, rich filling onto the mashed potatoes.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg eel, cleaned, skinned and cut into 6 cm pieces (ask your fishmonger)
steps: Rinse and dry the eel pieces and season with salt and pepper.
Soften the onion and garlic in the oil over medium heat for 8 minutes, then add the eel and sear 3 minutes per side.
Pour over the vinegar and let it evaporate, then add the passata and 100 ml water.
Cover and simmer gently 30–35 minutes until the eel is tender and flakes from the bone.
Scatter with parsley and serve with soft polenta, as in the lagoon town of Comacchio.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg white onions, very thinly sliced
600 g ripe tomatoes, peeled and chopped (or 400 g canned)
6 tbsp olive oil (originally lard; olive oil keeps it vegetarian)
steps: Put the onions in a heavy pan with the oil and a little salt, cover and cook over very low heat for 1 hour, stirring now and then, until completely soft and translucent.
Add the tomatoes and sugar and continue cooking uncovered over low heat for another 45–60 minutes until thick, jammy and reddish-gold.
Season with pepper and serve warm as a side, on bread, or with boiled meats — a Bologna classic.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Rub the flour with 2 tbsp lard, a pinch of salt and about 150 ml warm water into a soft dough; rest 30 minutes.

Blanch the greens 3 minutes, squeeze dry and chop; fry the pancetta, onion and garlic over medium heat 6 minutes, add the greens and cook 5 minutes, then cool and mix with Parmigiano, egg and parsley.
Roll two thirds of the dough thin to line an oiled 30 cm tin, fill with greens, cover with the rest of the dough rolled very thin, seal and prick the top.
Brush with the remaining lard and scatter a few cubes of pancetta on top.
Bake at 200°C for 40–45 minutes until crisp and golden; serve warm or at room temperature, as in Reggio Emilia.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 10 g fresh yeast or 4 g instant yeast
Lard or sunflower oil for deep frying
Salumi to serve: prosciutto, mortadella, salame, coppa
steps: Dissolve the yeast in the liquid, mix with flour, lard and salt and knead 10 minutes to a smooth dough; cover and rise 1 hour.
Roll the dough to 3 mm and cut into 8 cm diamonds.
Heat lard or oil to 180°C and fry a few diamonds at a time for 1 minute per side until puffed and golden.
Drain on paper and serve hot with platters of salumi and soft cheese, as in Modena.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: Cunza spread: 100 g lardo, 1 garlic clove and rosemary pounded together
Prosciutto, mortadella and soft cheese to serve
steps: Mix flour, yeast, salt, fat and liquid and knead 10 minutes into a soft dough; rise 1 hour until doubled.
Roll to 1 cm and cut 8 cm rounds, then rise 30 minutes more.
Cook in a preheated tigelliera (or a dry heavy frying pan covered with a lid) over medium heat for 4–5 minutes per side until risen and spotted golden.
Split hot and fill with cunza, Parmigiano and salumi, the Modenese Apennine way.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: Fillings: squacquerone cheese, rocket, prosciutto crudo
steps: Rub the flour, salt, soda and lard together, add the water and knead 5 minutes to a smooth firm dough; rest 30 minutes wrapped.
Divide into 6 balls and roll each to a 25 cm disc about 3 mm thick.
Cook each on a very hot dry iron griddle (testo) or heavy pan for 1–2 minutes per side, pricking any bubbles, until speckled brown.
Fill hot with squacquerone, rocket and prosciutto, fold in half and serve.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 10 g fresh yeast or 4 g instant yeast (traditionally a lievito madre)
steps: Mix flour, yeast, malt and water, then add the lard, oil and salt and knead 15 minutes into a very firm, smooth dough.
Pass the dough repeatedly through a pasta machine or roll and fold until silky; divide into 80 g pieces.
Roll each piece into a thin sheet, then roll up tightly from both corners to form two thin twisted horns joined at the middle, making an X shape.
Rise 1.5–2 hours, then bake at 220°C with steam for 20–25 minutes until the horns are golden and crisp.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 80 g butter or olive oil (lard is traditional; use butter/oil to keep vegetarian)
1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp bicarbonate of soda
800 g wild greens, chard or spinach
200 g squacquerone or mozzarella, plus 2 ripe tomatoes (optional variation)
steps: Make a piadina dough with the flour, fat, salt, soda and water, knead smooth and rest 30 minutes.
Blanch the greens 3 minutes, squeeze dry, then sauté with the garlic in oil for 5 minutes and season.
Roll the dough into 20 cm discs, put greens (or cheese and tomato) on one half, fold over and seal the edges with a fork.
Cook on a hot dry griddle 4–5 minutes per side until crisp and spotted, and serve hot.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 30 g dark chocolate, chopped (for half the custard)
300 g savoiardi or pan di Spagna sponge
150 ml Alchermes liqueur, diluted with 50 ml water (substitute cherry or raspberry syrup)
Cocoa or chocolate shavings to finish
steps: Heat the milk with lemon zest; whisk yolks, sugar and flour, pour on the hot milk, return to the pan and cook over medium-low heat, whisking, 5–6 minutes until thick.
Divide the custard in two and stir the chocolate into one half until melted; cool both covered.
Dip the sponge quickly in the diluted Alchermes and line a glass dish with a layer.
Spread with yellow custard, add another layer of soaked sponge, then the chocolate custard, and repeat, finishing with custard.
Chill at least 4 hours, then finish with chocolate shavings and serve cold.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 100 g blanched almonds, chopped (plus a few bitter almonds or amaretti if available)
Butter and breadcrumbs for the tin
steps: Simmer the rice in the milk with the lemon zest and half the sugar over low heat for 35–40 minutes, stirring, until thick and creamy; cool.
Beat the eggs with the remaining sugar and stir into the rice with the almonds, candied citron and liqueur.
Pour into a buttered and crumbed 24 cm tin and bake at 170°C for 60 minutes until set and golden.
While still warm, brush with a little more liqueur; cool completely and serve in small diamonds, as at Bologna's "addobbi" parish feasts.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Melt the chocolate and butter together over barely simmering water and cool slightly.
Beat the yolks with the sugar until pale, then stir in the chocolate, almonds, peanuts, coffee and rum.
Whisk the whites to soft peaks and fold in gently.
Pour into a lined 22 cm square tin and bake at 170°C for 35–40 minutes, until set at the edges but still moist inside (this flourless cake from Vignola stays fudgy).
Cool, dust with icing sugar and cut into small squares.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 150 g "00" flour and 1 egg plus 1 yolk, for very thin tagliatelle
steps: Make an egg-pasta dough, roll it paper-thin, dry 15 minutes and cut very fine tagliatelle.
Grind the almonds with the sugar and amaretti, then mix in the lemon zest.
Line a 24 cm tin with the frolla, then layer handfuls of raw tagliatelle with the almond mixture, drizzling melted butter between layers and finishing with a loose tangle of pasta on top.
Drizzle with the remaining butter and bake at 170°C for 40–45 minutes until the top strands are crisp and golden (cover with foil if browning too fast).
Brush with the liqueur while warm and serve at room temperature.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 tbsp pearl sugar (granella) and 1 beaten egg for topping
steps: Beat the eggs with the sugar, then add butter, milk and lemon zest.
Mix in the flour and baking powder to a soft, rather firm dough.
Shape into a thick log about 30 cm long on a lined tray (in Romagna it is a loaf, not a ring), brush with beaten egg and sprinkle with pearl sugar.
Bake at 180°C for 35–40 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Serve sliced and dunked in Albana passito or milk at breakfast.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Rub the butter into the flour, sugar, baking powder and zest, then add the eggs and milk and mix to a soft dough.
Shape into an oval loaf (or an S) on a lined tray and cut a shallow slit along the top.
Brush with yolk, scatter with pearl sugar and bake at 180°C for 30–35 minutes until golden.
Cool and serve sliced with a glass of Lambrusco to dip, the Modenese custom.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 250 g mostarda bolognese (thick quince-pear jam; substitute quince paste loosened with plum jam)
Icing sugar or Alchermes for finishing
steps: Mix flour, sugar, baking powder and zest, rub in the butter, then add eggs and milk to form a soft shortcrust; rest 20 minutes.
Roll to 4 mm and cut 8 cm rounds.
Put a teaspoon of mostarda on each, fold into a half moon and seal well with fingertips.
Bake at 180°C for 12–15 minutes until lightly golden, then dust with icing sugar or brush with Alchermes; traditional for San Giuseppe (19 March).
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 150 g mixed candied fruit, plus extra for decoration
100 g blanched almonds and 50 g pine nuts
80 g dark chocolate, chopped, plus 2 tbsp cocoa
100 g mostarda bolognese or fruit jam
1 tsp each cinnamon and aniseed, ground
1 tsp bicarbonate of soda and 100 ml sweet wine
steps: Warm the honey with the sugar and wine until fluid, then stir in the mostarda, chocolate, cocoa and spices.
Mix in the flour, soda, nuts and candied fruit to a stiff, sticky dough.
Press into a buttered ring tin, decorate the top with almonds and candied fruit, and bake at 170°C for 50–60 minutes until firm.
Glaze with warm honey, cool completely and age at least a week wrapped before slicing for Christmas.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 100 g walnuts and 50 g pine nuts, chopped
50 g raisins and 50 g candied citron
1 tsp mixed cinnamon, nutmeg and clove
steps: Rub the butter into the flour and sugar, add the wine and knead to a smooth pastry; rest 30 minutes.
Warm the honey, then stir in the nuts, raisins, citron, breadcrumbs and spices; cool.
Roll the pastry into two thin 24 cm discs, spread the filling on one, cover with the other and seal; prick the top.
Bake at 170°C for 30–35 minutes until pale golden, cool and dust heavily with icing sugar; it is a Christmas sweet of Busseto and the Reggio/Parma hills.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 100 g dark chocolate, melted, plus 300 g for coating
1 tsp each cinnamon, black pepper and nutmeg
1/2 tsp bicarbonate of soda and 100 ml water
steps: Warm the honey, sugar and water, then mix in the melted chocolate, cocoa and spices.
Add the flour, soda, almonds and candied peel and knead into a dense dough.
Shape into domes about 15 cm across and bake at 160°C for 35–40 minutes; cool completely.
Coat in tempered or melted dark chocolate and let set; slice thinly at Christmas.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 25 green unripe walnuts, picked around 24 June (San Giovanni)
1 litre neutral spirit or vodka at 40–45% abv, bought from a licensed retailer
1 cinnamon stick, 5 cloves and a strip of lemon zest
steps: Wearing gloves, quarter the green walnuts and put them in a large glass jar with the spices and lemon zest.
Pour over the spirit, seal and leave in the sun or a warm place for 40–60 days, shaking every few days, until dark brown.
Dissolve the sugar in the water over low heat, cool, then strain the walnut infusion and mix with the syrup.
Bottle and rest for several months; serve small glasses after dinner — the dark walnut liqueur of Modena — and enjoy responsibly.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 bottle (750 ml) Lambrusco (di Sorbara, Grasparossa or Salamino), bought from a licensed producer or shop
Platter of salumi and Parmigiano, to serve
steps: Lambrusco is Emilia's lightly sparkling (frizzante) red wine, made around Modena and Reggio Emilia from Lambrusco grapes; buy it from licensed producers rather than making it.
Chill to about 12–14°C and pour into wide tumblers or wine glasses so the violet foam shows.
Serve with gnocco fritto, tigelle, cotechino or bollito misto, whose richness the bubbles and acidity cut through; drink responsibly.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.2 l hot beef stock (brodo di manzo)
0.3 g saffron threads (zafferano), soaked in 3 tbsp hot stock
steps: Melt 30 g butter with the bone marrow in a wide heavy pan over medium-low heat and soften the onion for 5 minutes without colouring.
Add the rice and toast it for 2 minutes over medium heat until the grains look translucent at the edges, then pour in the wine and let it evaporate.
Add the hot stock a ladle at a time, stirring often and adding more only when the previous ladle is almost absorbed, for about 16 minutes.
Stir in the saffron with its liquid 2 minutes before the end; the rice should be creamy but still al dente.
Take the pan off the heat, beat in the remaining cold butter and the Grana Padano (mantecatura), cover for 2 minutes and serve all'onda, loose enough to ripple on the plate.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 600 g cold leftover risotto alla Milanese (made with beef marrow and stock)
steps: Chill the leftover risotto overnight so it firms up, then divide it into 4 portions.
Melt 10 g butter per portion in a small non-stick frying pan over medium heat.
Press one portion into a thin disc about 1 cm thick across the pan and cook for 6–8 minutes, shaking the pan, until a deep golden crust forms.
Flip it with the help of a plate, add a little more butter and crisp the second side for 4–5 minutes.
Slide onto a warm plate, scatter with Grana Padano and pepper and serve at once.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g pesto di maiale (fresh Mantuan pork sausage meat), crumbled; substitute plain fresh pork sausage
steps: Bring the salted water to a boil in a tall pan and pour the rice in through a funnel or all at once so it forms a cone that rises just above the water.
Boil for 12 minutes without stirring, tapping the pan sides occasionally, then turn off the heat, wrap the pan in a cloth, cover and leave for 15 minutes to finish by steam.
Meanwhile melt the butter in a frying pan over medium heat and cook the crumbled sausage for 10 minutes until browned and cooked through with no pink.
Fluff the rice with a fork, fold in the sausage with its butter and the Grana Padano, season with pepper and serve hot; the grains should stay separate, not creamy.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 veal shank slices (ossibuchi), 4 cm thick, about 300 g each
1 tbsp tomato paste (optional, as many Milanese families add it)
for the gremolata: 1 lemon zest, 1 garlic clove and 2 tbsp parsley, all finely chopped
steps: Snip the membrane around each shank in 2–3 places so it does not curl, season and dust lightly with flour.
Brown the shanks in the butter in a wide casserole over medium-high heat, 3–4 minutes per side, then remove.
Soften the onion in the same pan for 5 minutes, return the meat in one layer, pour in the wine and let it bubble off for 2 minutes.
Add the tomato paste dissolved in the stock, cover and simmer very gently for 1 hour 45 minutes, turning once and adding stock if dry, until the meat comes away from the bone.
Scatter the gremolata over the shanks for the last 2 minutes and serve with risotto alla Milanese, telling guests to scoop out the marrow.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 bone-in veal loin chops, 2 cm thick, about 250 g each
2 eggs, beaten with a pinch of salt
steps: Trim fat and sinew from the chops, scrape the bone clean and beat the meat gently to an even 1.5 cm, keeping the bone attached.
Dip each chop in egg, then press firmly into the breadcrumbs on both sides; repeat egg and crumbs for a thicker crust and pat the edges.
Heat the clarified butter in a large frying pan over medium heat until a crumb sizzles steadily.
Fry the chops for 5–6 minutes per side, basting with the butter, until the crust is deep golden and the meat reaches 63 °C inside.
Drain briefly on paper, sprinkle with flaky salt and serve with lemon wedges and a green salad or roast potatoes.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g pork rind (cotenna), scraped and cut into strips
400 g verzini (small fresh pork sausages); substitute luganega
2 tbsp tomato paste in 250 ml hot stock
steps: Blanch the rind and trotters in boiling water for 10 minutes, drain and rinse.
Melt the butter in a large heavy casserole and soften the onion, carrot and celery for 8 minutes over medium heat, then brown the ribs for 5 minutes.
Add the rind, trotters and tomato stock, cover and simmer gently for 1 hour 30 minutes.

Wilt the cabbage leaves in a separate pot for 5 minutes, drain, then layer them over the meat with the sausages, cover and cook for 1 hour more until the trotters are gelatinous and the sauce is thick and sticky.
Season, rest 10 minutes and serve hot with soft yellow polenta; it is the classic dish of Sant'Antonio, 17 January.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 thick veal loin chops, about 250 g each
steps: Season the chops and dust lightly with flour.
Melt the butter with the pancetta, rosemary and sage in a wide pan over medium heat for 3 minutes.
Brown the chops for 4 minutes per side until golden.
"Drown" them (negàa means drowned) with the wine, let it bubble for 2 minutes, then add the stock, cover and cook gently for 15–20 minutes until the meat is cooked through and tender.
Remove the herbs, reduce the pan juices for 2 minutes and pour over the chops; serve with risotto alla Milanese or mashed potatoes.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 800 g beef chuck, cut into very small 5 mm dice (not minced)
60 g lardo or pancetta, finely chopped
1 tsp wild fennel seeds (finocchietto), tied in muslin
steps: Melt the butter with the lardo in a heavy casserole over low heat, add the garlic and fennel bag and warm for 3 minutes.
Add the diced beef, season, cover tightly and cook on the lowest heat for 1 hour 30 minutes, stirring now and then, so the meat stews in its own juices.
Pour in the wine, cover again and cook gently for 1 hour more until the wine is absorbed and the meat is meltingly tender.
Discard the garlic and fennel bag, adjust the seasoning and serve over hot soft polenta, a specialty of Busto Arsizio and Alto Milanese.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 8 missoltini (salted, air-dried agone shad from Lake Como); substitute salted sardines
steps: Rinse the dried fish quickly under cold water and pat dry.
Grill them over a hot grill pan or embers for 2–3 minutes per side until the skin blisters and they are heated through.
Remove the heads and backbone and lay the fillets on a plate.
Whisk the vinegar, oil, parsley and garlic, pour over the warm fish and leave 5 minutes to soak in.
Serve with slices of grilled polenta.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 600 g small lake fish (alborelle, perch or bleak), cleaned; substitute small sardines or trout fillets
steps: Dust the fish in flour and fry in hot oil at 175 °C for 3–4 minutes until golden and cooked through; drain and salt lightly.
In 3 tbsp of the oil, soften the onions and garlic with the sage for 8 minutes over medium-low heat.
Add the vinegar, wine, peppercorns and salt and simmer for 5 minutes.
Arrange the fish in a deep dish and pour the hot carpione over them so they are covered.
Cool, cover and refrigerate for at least 12 hours; serve cold as an antipasto or summer main.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 pike (luccio), about 1.2 kg, cleaned; substitute zander or hake
1 onion, 1 carrot and 1 celery stick for the court-bouillon
1 tbsp salt and 100 ml white wine vinegar
steps: Simmer the vegetables, salt and vinegar in 3 litres of water for 15 minutes, add the pike and poach gently for 15–20 minutes until the flesh flakes from the bone.
Let the fish cool in the liquid, then lift it out, skin it and remove all bones carefully, as pike has many fine Y-bones.
Finely chop the anchovies, capers, parsley and garlic and stir in the oil and red pepper to make the salsa.
Layer the flaked fish and salsa in a dish, finishing with salsa.
Refrigerate for at least 12 hours and serve with grilled polenta, as on the Mantua lakes.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg mixed beef tripe (busecca), cleaned and pre-cooked
400 g cooked borlotti or white beans
steps: Blanch the tripe in boiling water for 10 minutes, drain and cut into thin strips.
Melt the butter with the pancetta and sage in a large pot and soften the vegetables for 10 minutes over medium heat.
Add the tripe, stir for 5 minutes, then add the tomato paste and stock.
Simmer gently, partly covered, for 2 hours 30 minutes until the tripe is very tender, adding the beans for the last 20 minutes.
Serve in bowls with plenty of Grana Padano and slices of toasted bread; the Milanese are nicknamed busecconi for this soup.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 50 g pancetta or cotenna (pork rind), diced
steps: Gently fry the pancetta in the butter with the sage and onion for 5 minutes in a large pot.
Add all the other vegetables and beans, stir for 5 minutes, then add the water, season and simmer for 1 hour 15 minutes.
Add the rice and cook 15 minutes more until tender and the soup is thick.
Serve hot, or in summer at room temperature as the Milanese do, with Grana Padano on top.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g leftover boiled beef (from bollito), minced
100 g mortadella or salame cotto, minced
50 g stale bread soaked in milk and squeezed
1 garlic clove and 1 tbsp parsley, finely chopped
1 lemon zest and a pinch of nutmeg
steps: Mix the beef, mortadella, egg, bread, Grana Padano, garlic, parsley, zest, nutmeg and a pinch of salt until it holds together.
Shape into slightly flattened balls the size of a walnut and roll them in breadcrumbs.
Fry in the foaming butter over medium heat for 3–4 minutes per side until crisp and golden and hot right through.
Drain on paper and serve hot as an aperitivo snack, as in Milan's osterie.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 pinch salt and 1 pinch bicarbonate of soda
200 g Valtellina Casera cheese, cut into 2 cm cubes; substitute Fontina
200 g chicory leaves (cicorino), dressed with oil and vinegar
steps: Whisk the flours, sparkling water, grappa, salt and bicarbonate to a thick batter and rest for 1 hour in the fridge.
Heat the oil to 180 °C in a deep pan.
Stir the cheese cubes into the batter, then drop them one by one with a spoon into the oil.
Fry for 2–3 minutes until crisp and dark golden, the cheese just melting, and drain on paper.
Serve piping hot on a bed of dressed chicory, the Valtellina way.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g buckwheat flour and 100 g plain flour, or 400 g dried pizzoccheri
300 g Savoy cabbage or chard, cut into strips
200 g Valtellina Casera cheese, thinly sliced; substitute Fontina
steps: Knead the flours and water to a firm dough, roll 3 mm thick and cut into strips 1 cm wide and 7 cm long.
Boil the potatoes and cabbage in plenty of salted water for 5 minutes, add the pasta and cook 10 minutes more until all are tender.
Meanwhile gently fry the garlic and sage in the butter over low heat for 4 minutes until the butter is nutty brown.
Drain, then layer pasta and vegetables in a warm dish with the Casera and Grana Padano.
Pour the hot garlic butter over the top, toss and serve immediately while the cheese melts in strings.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg dense pumpkin (zucca mantovana or delica), in wedges
100 g mostarda di Mantova (mustard-fruit preserve), finely chopped
80 g Grana Padano, grated, plus extra to serve
1 pinch nutmeg and a little lemon zest
300 g 00 flour and 3 eggs for the pasta
steps: Roast the pumpkin at 200 °C for 50 minutes until soft, scoop out the flesh, mash and drain it in a sieve.
Mix the pumpkin with amaretti, mostarda, Grana Padano, nutmeg, zest and salt; rest the filling overnight in the fridge if possible.
Knead the flour and eggs to a smooth dough, rest 30 minutes, roll very thin and cut into 7 cm squares.
Place a teaspoon of filling on each, fold into rectangles and seal the edges well.
Boil in salted water for 4–5 minutes until they float and are tender, then toss in melted sage butter and serve with extra Grana Padano.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g 00 flour and 3 eggs for the pasta
40 g Grana Padano, grated, plus extra to serve
2 amaretti and 1 tbsp raisins, chopped (traditional sweet note)
100 g butter, 50 g pancetta, diced, and 6 sage leaves
steps: Brown the sausage in a pan for 8 minutes until cooked through, then cool and mix with the beef, breadcrumbs, egg, cheese, amaretti, raisins and nutmeg.
Knead the flour and eggs to a smooth dough, rest 30 minutes, roll thin and cut 8 cm rounds.
Put a little filling in each, fold into a half-moon and press the middle down to give the classic curved candy shape.
Boil in salted water for 4–5 minutes until they float.
Meanwhile fry the pancetta and sage in the butter for 4 minutes; toss the casoncelli in it and finish with Grana Padano.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g 00 flour and 4 eggs for the pasta
2 l "brodo dei tre lessi" (beef, chicken and pork stock)
steps: Mix the meats, egg, Grana Padano, breadcrumbs and nutmeg to a firm filling.
Knead the flour and eggs, rest 30 minutes and roll thin; cut into 5 cm rounds with a fluted cutter.
Put a little filling on half of the rounds, cover with the rest and press the edges to seal.
Bring the stock to a gentle boil and cook the marubini for 4–5 minutes until tender.
Serve in their broth with extra Grana Padano, the Christmas dish of Cremona.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g polenta taragna flour (mixed buckwheat and cornmeal)
300 g Valtellina Casera or Bitto cheese, diced; substitute Fontina
steps: Bring the salted water to a boil in a heavy pot (traditionally a copper paiolo).
Rain in the flour while whisking, then cook on low heat for 45 minutes, stirring often with a wooden spoon, until thick and coming away from the sides.
Stir in the butter and cheese for the last 5 minutes until melted and stringy.
Serve very hot as a side to braised meats or as a main with sausages.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg calf's feet and knee cartilage (nervetti)
steps: Simmer the calf's feet with the vegetables and salt in plenty of water for 3 hours until very tender.
Remove the bones, press the meat and cartilage into a loaf tin and refrigerate overnight to set.
Cut the set nervetti into thin strips.
Toss with the red onion, beans, oil, vinegar, parsley and pepper and serve cold as a typical Milanese osteria antipasto.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg mixed firm fruit (cherries, small pears, quinces, apricots, figs, clementines)
10 drops food-grade mustard essential oil (essenza di senape) or 2 tbsp mustard powder
steps: Wash the fruit, leave small fruit whole and halve larger ones, and layer with the sugar in a bowl overnight.
Next day drain the syrup, boil it for 5 minutes and pour back over the fruit; repeat for 3 days so the fruit candies slowly.
On the last day simmer the fruit in the syrup with the water for 15 minutes until glossy and translucent.
Cool to lukewarm, then stir in the mustard oil (use gloves and do not inhale it) or mustard powder.
Jar in sterilised jars and serve with bollito misto and cheeses.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Mix 400 g flour, 180 ml water and 3 g yeast into a firm biga and leave it at 18 °C for 16 hours.
Add the remaining flour, water, yeast, malt and salt and knead 15 minutes to a smooth elastic dough.
Divide into 8 balls of 80 g and stamp each with a michetta (rosetta) stamp or cut a five-petal star with a sharp knife.
Proof upside down for 1 hour, then turn upright and bake at 230 °C with steam for 20–25 minutes until golden and hollow inside.
Cool on a rack; the crust should crackle and the inside be almost empty, ideal for a Milanese panino.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 150 g lievito madre (active stiff sourdough starter); or 10 g fresh yeast
100 g candied orange and citron peel, diced
steps: First dough: mix 250 g flour, the starter, 80 g sugar, 3 yolks, 120 ml water and 70 g butter; leave 12 hours at 24 °C until tripled.
Second dough: add the rest of the flour, sugar, yolks, honey, salt, vanilla and zest, knead until it windowpanes, then add the remaining butter in pieces and finally the fruit.
Shape into a ball, place in a 1 kg paper panettone mould and proof 6–8 hours at 26 °C until the dough reaches 2 cm below the rim.
Cut a cross on top, add a knob of butter and bake at 170 °C for 50–55 minutes until the centre reads 94 °C.
Skewer the base and hang upside down for 12 hours to cool so it does not collapse; serve sliced at Christmas.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 150 g lievito madre; or 10 g fresh yeast
for the glaze: 1 egg white, 60 g sugar, 40 g ground almonds, whole almonds and pearl sugar
steps: Make the first dough with 250 g flour, starter, 80 g sugar, 2 yolks, water and 60 g butter; rise 12 hours until tripled.
Knead in the rest of the flour, sugar, yolks, zest, vanilla, then the butter and candied peel until smooth and silky.
Divide into a body and two wings and lay in a dove-shaped paper mould; proof 6 hours until almost at the rim.
Whisk the egg white, sugar and ground almonds, spread over the top and scatter with whole almonds and pearl sugar.
Bake at 170 °C for 40–45 minutes until deep golden and the centre reaches 94 °C; cool upside down on skewers and serve at Easter.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g whole blanched almonds, toasted warm
steps: Melt the honey in a bain-marie, stirring, for 60 minutes until it thickens; a drop in cold water should form a firm ball.
Whip the egg whites to stiff peaks and fold them into the honey gradually, stirring until the mixture turns white and fluffy.
Boil the sugar and water to 150 °C (hard crack) and pour into the honey mixture while stirring, then add vanilla and the warm almonds.
Spread quickly 2 cm thick between two sheets of wafer paper in a lined tray and press flat.
Cool completely, cut with a large knife into bars and wrap; the classic sweet of Cremona's November torrone fair.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 30 g apricot kernels (armelline); substitute 1 tsp bitter almond extract
2 tbsp pearl or granulated sugar for the tops
steps: Grind the almonds, apricot kernels and half the sugar to a fine powder in short bursts.
Whisk the egg whites with the rest of the sugar to soft peaks and fold in the almond powder to a firm, piping paste.
Pipe or roll walnut-sized balls onto a lined tray, flatten slightly and sprinkle with sugar.
Rest 2 hours to form a skin, then bake at 160 °C for 20 minutes until golden, crisp and cracked.
Cool completely and store airtight; serve with coffee or crumble into pumpkin tortelli.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 150 g almonds, coarsely chopped, plus 30 g whole with skins
150 g cold butter, diced (or half butter, half lard as in Mantua)
steps: Mix the flours, chopped almonds, sugar and zest in a bowl.
Rub in the butter, then add the yolks and vanilla and work with fingertips into large irregular crumbs; do not knead.
Scatter the crumbs loosely into a buttered 26 cm tin without pressing and dot with whole almonds.
Bake at 180 °C for 35–40 minutes until golden and crisp.
Cool, then break into pieces by hand rather than slicing, as is tradition in Mantua.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Cream the butter and icing sugar for 8 minutes until pale and fluffy, then beat in the yolks one at a time with the zest.
Sift the flour, potato starch and baking powder and fold them in.
Whisk the whites with the salt to stiff peaks and fold in gently in three additions.
Pour into a buttered and floured 24 cm tin and bake at 170 °C for 40–45 minutes until a skewer comes out clean.
Cool and dust thickly with icing sugar; the soft cake from Pavia.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 150 g fine cornmeal (farina di mais fioretto)
100 g sugar, plus extra to sprinkle
steps: Cream the butter and sugar, then beat in the eggs and milk.
Add the cornmeal, flour, baking powder and half the elderflowers and mix to a soft dough.
Shape into flat buns about 8 cm across, place on a lined tray and sprinkle with sugar and the remaining elderflowers.
Bake at 180 °C for 20–25 minutes until golden and firm.
Serve with a glass of fresh cream for dipping, as for Saint George's day (23 April) in Milan.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 150 g 00 flour and 100 g fine cornmeal
4 tbsp apricot jam and 2 tbsp rum
60 g dark chocolate, melted, and 2 tbsp yellow sugar
steps: Cream the butter and sugar, beat in the eggs, then fold in the flour, cornmeal and baking powder.
Bake in buttered dome-shaped moulds (zuccotto) at 175 °C for 35–40 minutes until a skewer is clean, then cool.
Brush the domes with apricot jam warmed with rum.
Roll out the marzipan, drape it over each dome and smooth it, then brush lightly with water and roll in yellow sugar to look like polenta.
Top with the chocolate birds fixed with a dab of melted chocolate; this is Bergamo's sweet nod to the savoury dish of polenta with small birds.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 15 g fresh yeast in 200 ml warm milk
steps: Mix the flour, yeast milk, sugar, eggs and salt, then knead in the butter until smooth and elastic.
Rise 2 hours covered in a warm place until doubled.
Knead in the figs, raisins and walnuts and shape into a round loaf on a lined tray; rise 1 hour more.
Bake at 180 °C for 40–45 minutes until deep brown and hollow-sounding.
Cool and slice; the Christmas fruit bread of Valtellina, good with mountain cheeses or a glass of sweet wine.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 100 g dark chocolate, chopped, or 40 g cocoa powder
steps: Melt the chocolate (or cocoa) with the sugar in the milk over low heat, whisking, for 5 minutes until smooth.
Add the hot coffee and whisk vigorously until frothy.
Pour into glasses and top with whipped cream; serve hot in winter, or chilled over ice in summer as in old Milanese cafés.

ingredients: 30 ml chilled spumante brut, from a licensed producer
steps: Fill a rocks glass or tumbler with ice.
Pour in the Campari and red vermouth and stir briefly.
Top with the spumante instead of gin (sbagliato means "mistaken"), stir once gently and garnish with an orange slice; created at Bar Basso in Milan.

ingredients: 800 g veal eye of round (girello di vitello), tied
1 onion, 1 carrot, 1 celery stick, 1 bay leaf
200 g good tuna in olive oil, drained
2 tbsp capers, plus extra to garnish
150 g mayonnaise (or 4 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil for the older, egg-free style)
steps: Put the veal, vegetables, bay leaf and wine in a pot with water just to cover, bring to a gentle simmer and poach for 50–60 minutes until the centre reaches 63 °C.
Cool the meat in its liquid, then lift out and chill for at least 2 hours; keep 150 ml of the strained cooking liquid.
Blend the tuna, anchovies, capers, egg yolks and mayonnaise with enough cooking liquid to make a smooth, pourable sauce; season.
Slice the veal as thinly as possible, overlap the slices on a platter and cover completely with the tuna sauce.
Garnish with capers, cover and rest in the fridge for a few hours or overnight; serve cold as a Piedmontese antipasto.

ingredients: 1.2 kg beef chuck or shoulder clod (cappello del prete), in one piece
1 onion, 2 carrots, 2 celery sticks, roughly chopped
2 garlic cloves, 1 sprig rosemary, 2 bay leaves
50 g butter and 2 tbsp olive oil
steps: Marinate the beef with the wine, vegetables, garlic, herbs and spices in the fridge for 12–24 hours, turning occasionally.
Lift out and dry the meat, dust with flour and brown all over in the butter and oil in a heavy casserole over medium-high heat for 10 minutes.
Add the vegetables from the marinade, cook 5 minutes, then pour in the wine with the spices, season and bring to a simmer.
Cover and braise on very low heat (or at 150 °C in the oven) for 3 hours, turning occasionally, until a fork slides in easily.
Remove the meat, discard the cinnamon and bay, blend the vegetables and liquid into a smooth sauce and reduce if thin; slice the beef and serve under the sauce with polenta or mashed potatoes.

ingredients: 1 kg beef brisket or shoulder (punta di petto)
1 small chicken or capon, about 1.5 kg
2 onions stuck with cloves, 2 carrots, 2 celery sticks
to serve: bagnet verd, bagnet ross (tomato sauce) and mostarda
steps: Bring a very large pot of water with the vegetables, herbs and salt to a boil, add the brisket and simmer gently for 1 hour.
Add the tongue and veal shank and simmer 1 hour 30 minutes more; add the chicken for the last 1 hour, until all meats are tender.
Cook the cotechino separately in simmering water for 2 hours (or as the pack says) so its fat does not cloud the broth.
Peel the tongue while hot, then keep all meats in the hot broth until serving.
Slice at the table onto hot plates with a ladle of broth and serve with bagnet verd, bagnet ross and mostarda; keep the broth for agnolotti.

ingredients: 300 g veal or pork loin, in thin slices
300 g calf's liver and sweetbreads, cleaned and sliced
6 small pork sausages (salsiccia di Bra or similar)
2 apples, cored and sliced into rings
6 squares of semolina pudding (semolino dolce, set and cut)
400 g butter or 1 l sunflower oil for frying
steps: Dip the meats, offal, apple rings, semolina squares and vegetables in egg, then breadcrumbs; leave the sausages and amaretti plain.
Heat the butter or oil to 170 °C in a wide pan.
Fry in batches: meat slices and offal 2–3 minutes per side, sausages 8–10 minutes until cooked through, vegetables 3–4 minutes, and the sweet pieces 1–2 minutes until golden.
Drain each batch on paper, salt the savoury pieces and keep warm in a low oven.
Serve everything together on a large platter, savoury and sweet side by side, as in Piedmontese trattorias.

ingredients: 200 g veal sweetbreads, blanched and sliced
150 g veal brain (traditional) or extra sweetbreads, blanched
150 g chicken or veal fillet, diced
150 g porcini or button mushrooms, sliced
steps: Melt the butter in a wide pan over medium heat and brown the meat, sweetbreads and brain (dusted in flour) for 5 minutes.
Add the mushrooms and cook for 5 minutes until softened.
Add the chicken livers and cook 3 minutes, then pour in the Marsala and vinegar and let them reduce for 2 minutes.
Add the stock, cover and simmer gently for 15–20 minutes until all the offal is cooked through and the sauce is glossy.
Season and serve hot, often inside a puff pastry case (vol-au-vent); a Turin classic once beloved by bankers in frock coats.

ingredients: 400 g very fresh, top-quality Fassone (Piedmontese) beef topside, from a trusted butcher
40 g Parmigiano or aged Bra cheese, shaved, or a few slices of white truffle in season
steps: Buy the beef the day you serve it, specifying it will be eaten raw, and keep it refrigerated until the last moment.
Rub a chilled bowl with the cut garlic, then finely hand-chop the beef with a sharp knife (battuta al coltello); do not mince it in a machine.
Season with oil, a little lemon juice, salt and pepper and mix gently.
Shape onto cold plates and top with shaved cheese or truffle; serve immediately, within 30 minutes of chopping.

ingredients: 1 onion, 1 carrot, 1 celery stick, 1 bay leaf
400 ml extra-virgin olive oil, to cover
steps: Simmer the rabbit with the vegetables, bay and salt in water to cover for 50–60 minutes until the meat falls from the bone.
Drain and cool, then pull the meat off the bones in large flakes, discarding all small bones.
Layer the rabbit in a glass jar with the garlic, sage, peppercorns and a pinch of salt.
Cover completely with olive oil, seal and marinate in the fridge for at least 24 hours (use within 4 days).
Serve at room temperature as an antipasto with bread; the name means "rabbit tuna" because it resembles tuna in oil.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 600 g minced donkey meat (asino), the Borgomanero original; substitute minced beef
steps: Melt the butter with the lardo in a heavy pan over low heat and soften the garlic for 2 minutes.
Add the minced meat and brown for 10 minutes over medium heat, breaking it up well.
Add the bay leaf, cloves and wine, season, cover and simmer gently for 1 hour 30 minutes, adding a little water if dry.
Add the cabbage (if using) for the last 20 minutes; the meat should be soft and saucy.
Serve hot over soft polenta, as in the Novara hills.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 800 g beef chuck, cut into 3 cm cubes (traditionally salt-cured beef)
500 ml full-bodied red wine (Torrette or Nebbiolo)
1 bay leaf, 2 cloves and 1 pinch cinnamon
steps: Dust the beef in flour and brown in the butter in a casserole over medium-high heat for 8 minutes; remove.
Cook the onions in the same pan on low heat for 15 minutes until soft and golden.
Return the beef, add the wine, bay, cloves and cinnamon and season.
Cover and simmer very gently for 1 hour 30 minutes until the beef is tender and the sauce dark and thick.
Serve with polenta, the Aosta Valley classic.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g Fontina DOP from Aosta Valley, rind removed, diced; substitute a good Fontal
1 baguette, cubed and toasted, or boiled potatoes, to serve
steps: Soak the diced Fontina in the milk in the fridge for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Melt the butter in a bain-marie, add the cheese with its milk and stir continuously until melted and smooth, about 8 minutes, without letting it boil.
Off direct heat, stir in the yolks one at a time and keep stirring over the bain-marie for 3–4 minutes until thick, glossy and steaming (about 75 °C).
Season with white pepper and serve at once in warm bowls with toasted bread or potatoes; shave white truffle over it in season.
