ingredients: 400 g 00 flour and 4 eggs (or 12 yolks for a richer dough)
300 g mixed roast meats (veal, pork, rabbit), cooled and minced
100 g cooked Savoy cabbage or spinach, squeezed dry and chopped
50 g Parmigiano, grated, plus extra to serve
100 g butter with 6 sage leaves, or the roasting juices (sugo d'arrosto)
steps: Mix the meats, greens, egg, Parmigiano and nutmeg into a smooth filling and season.
Knead the flour and eggs, rest 30 minutes and roll very thin in long strips 6 cm wide.
Pipe hazelnut-sized dots of filling 2 cm apart along the strip, fold the pasta over, then pinch (plin) the dough between each mound.
Cut along the long edge with a fluted wheel and across between each pinch so each agnolotto folds into a little pocket.
Boil in salted water for 3 minutes until they float, then toss in sage butter or roasting juices and serve with Parmigiano.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 250 g Toma or Fontina cheese, thinly sliced
steps: Boil the potatoes in their skins for 30 minutes until tender, peel while hot and rice them onto a floured board.
Work in the flour and salt quickly to a soft dough, roll into ropes and cut into 2 cm gnocchi.
Boil in salted water for 2 minutes until they float, then lift out with a slotted spoon.
Layer the gnocchi in a buttered baking dish with the Toma, cream and dots of butter and top with Parmigiano.
Bake at 200 °C for 8–10 minutes until the cheese has melted into long strings (bava means drool); serve hot.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 12 egg yolks (traditional 30-tuorli dough uses even more yolks)
30 g white Alba truffle (tartufo bianco d'Alba), cleaned; substitute black truffle or a little truffle butter
steps: Knead the flour and yolks to a firm, deep-yellow dough and rest 30 minutes wrapped.
Roll very thin, dust with flour, roll up loosely and cut into fine 2 mm ribbons with a sharp knife; shake them loose.
Boil in salted water for 1–2 minutes until just tender.
Toss in melted butter with a splash of pasta water and the Parmigiano.
Serve on warm plates and shave the truffle generously over the top at the table.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Soften the shallot in 30 g butter in a wide pan over medium-low heat for 4 minutes.
Toast the rice for 2 minutes until translucent at the edges.
Add half the wine and let it absorb, then add the rest of the wine and the hot stock a ladle at a time, stirring, for 16–18 minutes until al dente.
Off the heat, beat in the remaining cold butter and the cheese, cover 2 minutes and serve; the rice should be a deep purple-red.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 200 g dried borlotti beans, soaked overnight
100 g salam d'la duja (Vercelli salami preserved in lard), crumbled; substitute fresh salami
1 l hot vegetable stock or bean cooking water
for paniscia of Novara: add 1 carrot, 1 celery stick and 150 g Savoy cabbage, diced, to the beans
steps: Simmer the soaked beans (with the extra vegetables for the Novara version) in 1.5 l water for 1 hour until tender; keep the liquid.
Fry the lardo and onion in the butter over medium heat for 5 minutes, add the crumbled salami and cook 3 minutes.
Add the rice and toast 2 minutes, pour in the wine and let it evaporate.
Add the beans and their hot liquid a ladle at a time, stirring, for 18 minutes until the rice is al dente and the risotto thick.
Rest 2 minutes and serve; Vercelli makes panissa, Novara the vegetable-rich paniscia.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g pork rind (cotenna), scraped and cut into strips
2 pig's trotters or 300 g pork ribs
1 onion, 2 carrots, 2 celery sticks, 2 potatoes, diced
2 tbsp olive oil and 30 g butter
salt, black pepper and toasted bread to serve
steps: Blanch the rind and trotters in boiling water for 10 minutes and drain.
Soften the onion, leek, carrots and celery in the oil and butter for 10 minutes in a large pot.
Add the chickpeas, pork, herbs and water and simmer gently for 2 hours 30 minutes.
Add the potatoes and cook 30 minutes more until all is very tender and the soup thick; season.
Serve over toasted bread with olive oil; the soup of All Souls' Day (2 November) in Piedmont.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g stale rye bread (pan ner), sliced
steps: Blanch the cabbage leaves in the stock for 10 minutes and remove.
Toast the bread slices in a dry pan or the oven for 5 minutes.
Layer bread, cabbage and Fontina in a deep earthenware dish, finishing with Fontina.
Pour over enough hot stock to soak everything, dot with butter, sprinkle with cinnamon and bake at 180 °C for 40 minutes until golden and bubbling.
Serve hot, spooned from the dish; the bread soup of Valpelline in the Aosta Valley.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 12 garlic cloves, peeled and germ removed
500 ml whole milk (to soften the garlic, optional)
150 g salted anchovies (acciughe sotto sale), rinsed and filleted
250 ml extra-virgin olive oil (or a mild Ligurian oil)
raw vegetables to dip: cardoons (cardi gobbi), peppers, celery, cabbage leaves, Jerusalem artichokes, fennel
steps: Simmer the garlic in milk for 10 minutes to mellow it (optional), drain and slice thinly.
Warm the garlic in the oil in an earthenware pot over the lowest heat for 10 minutes without colouring.
Add the anchovies and stir until they dissolve into a creamy sauce, about 10 minutes, keeping the heat very low.
Stir in the butter at the end and keep warm over a tea-light burner (fojot) at the table.
Dip the vegetables into the hot sauce; a convivial autumn dish shared around the pot.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 large bunch flat-leaf parsley, leaves only
30 g bread crumb soaked in 2 tbsp red wine vinegar and squeezed
steps: Chop the parsley, anchovies, capers and garlic very finely with a mezzaluna, or pulse briefly in a food processor.
Mash in the soaked bread and the egg yolk if using.
Stir in the olive oil to make a loose, bright green sauce and season with salt.
Rest 30 minutes and serve with bollito misto or boiled eggs.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Rinse the anchovies, soak them in vinegar diluted with an equal amount of water for 10 minutes, then fillet them and remove the spine.
Pat the fillets dry.
Mix the parsley, garlic, chilli and oil to a green sauce.
Layer the anchovies and sauce in a glass dish, finishing with sauce, cover and refrigerate for at least 12 hours.
Serve as an antipasto with bread or grissini.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Bring the salted water to a boil and rain in the cornmeal while whisking.
Cook on low heat for 45 minutes, stirring often, until thick and smooth.
Stir in the Fontina and Parmigiano until melted.
Brown the butter in a small pan for 2–3 minutes until nutty and pour it over the polenta in bowls; serve hot, the Biella and Aosta Valley mountain dish.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 50 ml extra-virgin olive oil (or lard, as traditional)
steps: Dissolve the yeast and malt in the water, mix with the flour, oil and salt and knead 10 minutes to a soft elastic dough.
Shape into a long flat rectangle on semolina, brush with oil and rise 1 hour covered.
Cut into strips 1 cm wide and stretch each by hand to the length of the baking tray (grissini stirati).
Bake at 220 °C for 15–20 minutes until golden and crisp throughout.
Cool on a rack and serve with antipasti or wrapped with cured ham.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 100 g sugar, plus 100 g for the caramel
steps: Melt 100 g sugar in a pan with 2 tbsp water over medium heat until an amber caramel forms, then pour into a 1 l loaf mould and tilt to coat.
Whisk the eggs and sugar, then add the cocoa, crushed amaretti, rum and warm milk and mix until smooth.
Pour into the mould, set it in a roasting tin of hot water and bake at 160 °C for 50–60 minutes until just set and a knife comes out clean.
Cool, then chill for at least 4 hours.
Run a knife round the edge, turn out onto a plate so the caramel runs over and serve in slices.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 g agar-agar powder (vegetarian setting agent; traditional recipes use 8 g gelatine)
for serving: caramel sauce or berry coulis
steps: Heat the cream, milk, sugar and vanilla seeds and pod over medium heat until steaming.
Whisk in the agar and simmer gently for 2 minutes, stirring, so it fully activates.
Remove the pod and pour into 6 small moulds or glasses.
Cool, then refrigerate for at least 4 hours until set with a gentle wobble.
Turn out or serve in glasses with caramel or berry sauce; panna cotta is Piedmont's classic "cooked cream".
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 200 g Piedmont hazelnuts (nocciola Tonda Gentile), toasted and skinned
steps: Grind the warm hazelnuts with the icing sugar in a food processor for 5–8 minutes until they form a smooth, runny paste.
Melt the chocolates in a bain-marie over low heat, then stir in the hazelnut paste and salt.
Cool the mixture, stirring, until it thickens to about 28 °C and holds its shape.
Pipe or shape into small upturned-boat shapes on parchment and leave at cool room temperature for 4 hours to set.
Wrap each in gold foil; Turin's hazelnut-chocolate born in 1865 when cocoa was scarce.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 100 g hazelnuts, toasted and skinned (or almonds)
steps: Grind the nuts with the sugar to a fine powder.
Rub in the flour, salt and butter until a smooth dough forms; chill for 1 hour.
Roll into hazelnut-sized balls (about 8 g each) and place on a lined tray; chill 30 minutes so they keep their dome shape.
Bake at 160 °C for 14–15 minutes until pale golden at the base, then cool completely.
Sandwich pairs with a dab of melted chocolate and let set; the "lady's kisses" of Tortona.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Dissolve the yeast in the water and mix with the flour and salt, then knead in the butter until smooth.
Rise covered for 1 hour 30 minutes until doubled.
Roll pieces into thin ropes 15 cm long, roll them in sugar and twist into teardrop shapes pinched at the base.
Rest 30 minutes on a lined tray, then bake at 190 °C for 15–20 minutes until golden and the sugar caramelised.
Cool and serve with coffee or Moscato; a speciality of Canavese and Aosta Valley.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 250 g Piedmont hazelnuts (Tonda Gentile), toasted and skinned
steps: Grind the hazelnuts with 50 g sugar to a fine, slightly oily flour.
Whisk the eggs with the remaining sugar for 8 minutes until pale and doubled.
Fold in the hazelnut flour, then the flour with baking powder and salt, and finally the melted butter.
Pour into a buttered 24 cm tin and bake at 170 °C for 35–40 minutes until a skewer comes out clean.
Cool and dust with icing sugar; serve with zabaione or a glass of Moscato d'Asti.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 large ripe yellow peaches, halved and stoned
30 g butter, plus extra for the dish
steps: Scoop a little flesh from each peach half to enlarge the hollow and chop the scooped flesh.
Mix the chopped peach with the amaretti, yolk, cocoa and sugar into a thick filling.
Fill the peach halves generously and place in a buttered baking dish; top each with a flake of butter.
Pour the Moscato into the dish and bake at 180 °C for 35–40 minutes until the peaches are tender and the tops crisp.
Serve warm or at room temperature with the pan juices.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 200 g hazelnuts, toasted, skinned and roughly chopped
steps: Whisk the egg whites with the salt to stiff peaks, then gradually beat in the sugar until glossy.
Fold in the hazelnuts and vanilla.
Cook the mixture in a heavy pan over low heat for 10 minutes, stirring constantly, until it comes away from the sides and turns light brown.
Drop rough spoonfuls onto a lined tray and bake at 150 °C for 25 minutes until dry and crisp.
Cool completely; the "ugly but good" biscuits of Borgomanero.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 100 g hazelnuts and 50 g almonds, finely ground
steps: Mix the ground nuts, sugar and flour, then stir in the egg whites, melted butter and vanilla to a thin batter.
Spread teaspoons of batter into very thin 7 cm discs on a lined tray, well spaced.
Bake at 180 °C for 6–8 minutes until golden at the edges.
While still hot, lift each disc and drape it over a rolling pin so it curves like a roof tile (tegola).
Cool until crisp and store airtight; serve with coffee in the Aosta Valley.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 100 ml cold whipping cream, lightly whipped
steps: Melt the chocolate in the milk with the sugar over low heat, whisking, for 5 minutes until thick and smooth.
Pour the hot chocolate into small heat-proof glasses.
Gently pour the espresso over the back of a spoon to form a second layer.
Float the lightly whipped cream on top and serve immediately without stirring, as at Turin's Caffè Al Bicerin since 1763.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 75 ml Vermouth di Torino IGP (rosso or bianco), bought from a licensed producer
steps: Vermouth di Torino is an aromatised fortified wine flavoured with Artemisia (wormwood) and botanicals, created in Turin in 1786; buy it from licensed producers rather than making it.
Serve it chilled in a short glass over ice with a twist of citrus peel as an aperitivo, alongside grissini and olives.
It is also the base of classic cocktails such as the Americano and the Negroni.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Pour the coffee, grappa, sugar, lemon zest and cloves into a wooden grolla or coppa dell'amicizia (friendship cup) with several spouts, or a heat-proof bowl.
Rub sugar around the spouts, then carefully flame the surface with a long match for a few seconds to burn off some alcohol, keeping away from anything flammable, and cover with the lid to extinguish.
Pass the cup around the table so each guest drinks from a different spout without putting it down, a traditional Aosta Valley after-dinner ritual.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 50 g young Genovese basil leaves (Basilico Genovese DOP; substitute small-leaf sweet basil)
20 g Fiore Sardo or Pecorino Sardo, finely grated
80 ml mild Ligurian extra-virgin olive oil (Riviera Ligure DOP)
steps: Pound the garlic with the coarse salt in a marble mortar with a wooden pestle until creamy, then add the pine nuts and pound to a paste.
Add the basil a little at a time, rotating the pestle against the sides rather than striking, until the leaves release a bright green liquid.
Work in the two cheeses, then drizzle in the oil, stirring, until you have a smooth, creamy sauce.
Use at once or cover with a film of oil and refrigerate up to 2 days; never heat it, just loosen with a spoon of pasta water.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g plain or "00" flour (some use part chestnut flour)
150 g waxy potatoes, peeled and diced
150 g green beans, cut into 3 cm pieces
steps: Mix flour, salt and water and knead 10 minutes to a smooth, firm eggless dough; rest 30 minutes covered.
Pinch off chickpea-sized pieces and roll each under the palm on an unfloured board, pushing diagonally to form 3–4 cm twisted spindles; spread on a floured cloth.
Boil the potatoes in well-salted water for 5 minutes, add the green beans and trofie and cook 5–7 minutes more until the trofie are tender.
Drain, reserving a little water, and toss off the heat with the pesto loosened with 2–3 tbsp cooking water; serve immediately.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 350 g trenette (flat narrow dried pasta, like linguine)
2 medium waxy potatoes, peeled and thinly sliced
steps: Bring a large pot of salted water to the boil and cook the potatoes for 4 minutes.
Add the trenette and green beans and cook together until the pasta is al dente, about 9–10 minutes.
Put the pesto in a warm bowl and loosen with 3 tbsp of the cooking water.
Drain the pasta and vegetables, toss with the pesto and serve sprinkled with Parmigiano.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 60 g butter or 5 tbsp olive oil
steps: Knead the flour, eggs, wine and salt into a smooth firm dough and rest 30 minutes.
Roll to 2 mm, cut discs with the cutter end of a carved wooden corzetti stamp (or a 6 cm round cutter) and press each disc in the stamp to emboss both sides; dry 30 minutes.
Toast the pine nuts in the butter or oil over medium-low heat for 3 minutes, then add the marjoram.
Boil the corzetti in salted water 4–5 minutes, drain and toss in the pine nut sauce with Parmigiano (they are also served with pesto or meat tocco).
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Knead the flour, eggs and wine into a smooth dough and rest 30 minutes wrapped.
Roll the dough as thin as possible, almost see-through like silk (the name means "silk handkerchiefs" in Genoese), and cut into 12 cm squares.
Cook the squares a few at a time in a wide pot of boiling salted water for 1–2 minutes until tender.
Lift out gently, layer in warm plates with pesto loosened with a little cooking water, folding the sheets loosely like handkerchiefs, and finish with Parmigiano.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g "00" flour, 1 egg and 100 ml dry white wine for the dough
800 g mixed greens (preboggion: borage, chard, wild herbs; substitute chard and spinach)
200 g prescinsêua or ricotta (prescinsêua is a tangy Genoese curd; substitute ricotta with 2 tbsp yogurt)
1 slice white bread, crusts removed, soaked in milk and squeezed
4 tbsp olive oil and 100 ml milk or cream
steps: Knead the flour, egg, wine and pinch of salt into a soft dough; rest 30 minutes.
Blanch the greens 3 minutes, squeeze very dry, chop and mix with the prescinsêua, Parmigiano, egg, salt and nutmeg.
Roll the dough thin, cut 7 cm squares, fill each with a teaspoon of filling and fold into triangles, sealing well (pansoti means "pot-bellied").
Pound or blend the walnuts, bread and garlic, then add the oil and enough milk to make a creamy sauce; season with salt.
Boil the pansoti 4–5 minutes, drain and toss with the walnut sauce loosened with a little pasta water; serve with Parmigiano.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g "00" flour, 2 eggs and 80 ml water for the dough
200 g veal, cooked in butter until no longer pink
100 g veal brain or sweetbread, poached (optional; use more veal if unavailable)
300 g borage or chard, blanched and squeezed dry
2 eggs and a pinch of marjoram for the filling
500 ml tocco (Genoese meat sauce) or ragù
steps: Knead flour, eggs and water into a supple dough and rest 30 minutes.
Mince the cooked veal, brain if using and greens very finely, then mix with Parmigiano, eggs, marjoram, salt and nutmeg.
Roll the dough thin, place small mounds of filling 4 cm apart, cover with a second sheet, press around each mound and cut 4 cm square ravioli.
Boil in salted water 4–5 minutes, drain and serve layered with hot tocco and Parmigiano.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 200 g fresh borlotti beans (or 400 g can, drained)
150 g green beans and 1/4 savoy cabbage, sliced
150 g short pasta (ditalini or broken trenette) or rice
steps: Put all the vegetables, the fresh beans and the cheese rind in a large pot, cover with 2.5 litres cold water, add the oil and salt and bring to the boil.
Simmer gently, partly covered, for 75 minutes until the vegetables are very soft and the soup is thick.
Add the pasta and cook until tender, about 10 minutes, topping up with boiling water if needed.
Off the heat, remove the rind and stir in the pesto; serve warm or at room temperature with extra olive oil.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg mixed firm fish and seafood (dogfish/palombo, monkfish, gurnard, squid), cleaned and cut in pieces
2 garlic cloves and a handful of parsley, chopped
30 g dried porcini, soaked and chopped
30 g pine nuts and 2 anchovy fillets
steps: Gently fry the onion, garlic, parsley and anchovies in the oil for 8 minutes over medium-low heat.
Add the porcini and pine nuts, then the wine, and let it reduce for 2 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and simmer 15 minutes, then layer in the fish, firmest pieces first, cover and cook very gently for 15–20 minutes without stirring, until the fish is opaque and flakes easily.
Season and serve the stew over toasted bread.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.2 kg small bony rock fish (scorpionfish, gurnard, weever), cleaned (ask your fishmonger)
1 onion, 1 carrot and 1 celery stick, chopped
2 garlic cloves and a handful of parsley
1.5 litres water or light fish stock
4 slices bread, toasted and rubbed with garlic
steps: Sauté the onion, carrot, celery, garlic and parsley in oil over medium heat for 10 minutes.
Add the fish, stir 3 minutes, pour in the wine and let it evaporate, then add the tomatoes and water.
Simmer 45 minutes until the fish falls apart completely, then pass everything through a food mill to a thick velvety soup, discarding bones.
Reheat to a boil, season and serve over garlic toast; this Sestri Levante soup is the ancestor of cioppino.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g strong bread flour ("0" or Manitoba blend)
40 ml olive oil for the dough, plus 50 ml for the pan
Brine: 80 ml water, 40 ml olive oil, 1 tsp salt
steps: Mix flour, water, yeast, malt, salt and oil into a soft dough, knead 8 minutes and rise 1.5 hours.
Press gently into a well-oiled 30 x 40 cm tray, rest 30 minutes, stretch to the corners and rise 1 hour more.
Make deep dimples with your fingertips all over, pour on the emulsified brine so it pools in the holes, sprinkle coarse salt and rise a final 30 minutes.
Bake at 230°C on the lowest rack for 18–20 minutes until golden on top and crisp underneath; eat warm, Genoese-style for breakfast dipped in cappuccino.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 tbsp olive oil, plus extra for the tray and top
400 g crescenza or stracchino (soft fresh cheese; substitute fresh soft goat cheese)
steps: Knead flour, water, oil and salt into a smooth, very elastic dough and rest 30 minutes.
Divide in two and stretch the first half by hand over the knuckles until paper-thin and translucent, laying it on a large oiled round tray.
Dot with walnut-sized pieces of cheese, cover with the second sheet stretched equally thin, trim edges and tear small holes in the top over the cheese.
Drizzle with oil and salt and bake in the hottest oven (250–300°C) for 6–10 minutes until blistered and spotted brown; serve immediately.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 600 g ripe tomatoes, peeled and chopped (or canned)
1 tbsp dried oregano and 1 tsp salt
steps: Mix flour, yeast, water, 2 tbsp oil and salt to a soft dough, knead and rise 1 hour.
Simmer the tomatoes with 1 tbsp oil and salt for 15 minutes until thick.
Press the dough into an oiled 30 x 40 cm tray, rise 30 minutes, then spread with tomato and top with anchovies, olives, whole garlic cloves and oregano; drizzle with the remaining oil.
Bake at 220°C for 25–30 minutes until the base is crisp and golden; the San Remo answer to pizza.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Whisk the chickpea flour into the water until smooth, cover and rest 4 hours (or overnight), skimming off any foam.
Stir in the salt; pour the oil into a large shallow copper or steel pan (about 35 cm) and heat it in the oven at 250°C for 5 minutes.
Pour in the batter, stir lightly to blend with the oil, and bake on the top shelf 12–15 minutes until set with a crisp golden top.
Cut into wedges, grind over plenty of pepper and eat hot from the pan.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: Olive oil for frying and dressing
1 spring onion, thinly sliced, and lemon juice
steps: Whisk the chickpea flour into the cold salted water, then cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, for 30–40 minutes like polenta until very thick.
Pour into an oiled tray or dish to 1.5 cm thick and leave to set until cold.
Either cut into sticks and shallow-fry in hot oil for 3–4 minutes until golden and crisp, or dice it and dress with oil, lemon and spring onion as a salad.
Salt and serve hot or room temperature, as sold in Genoa's friggitorie.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 handful borage or lettuce leaves, finely shredded (optional)
Sunflower or olive oil for deep frying
steps: Whisk flour, yeast, salt and water into a thick, smooth batter, then fold in the greens if using.
Cover and leave to rise in a warm place for 1 hour until bubbly.
Heat the oil to 175°C and drop in teaspoonfuls of batter, frying 2–3 minutes and turning until puffed and golden.
Drain on paper, salt lightly and serve hot in a paper cone.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 3 tbsp olive oil and 120 ml white wine or water
600 g Swiss chard and wild herbs
1 small onion, finely chopped, and fresh marjoram
steps: Knead the flour, oil, wine and a pinch of salt into a smooth elastic dough and rest 30 minutes.
Blanch the greens, squeeze dry and chop, then sauté with the onion in a little oil for 5 minutes; cool and mix with eggs, Parmigiano, marjoram and salt.
Roll the dough thin, cut 10 cm rounds, fill each with a spoonful of filling, fold into half-moons and seal with a fork.
Deep-fry at 175°C for 3–4 minutes until blistered and golden, drain and eat hot, as in Levanto.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g plain flour, 4 tbsp olive oil and 250 ml water for the pastry
steps: Knead the flour, oil, water and salt into an elastic dough, divide into 6–8 pieces and rest 30 minutes under a damp cloth.
Blanch the chard, squeeze dry and chop, sauté with the onion 5 minutes, then cool and mix with the ricotta, half the Parmigiano, 2 eggs and marjoram.

Stretch half the dough balls paper-thin one by one, layering them in an oiled 26 cm tin with oil brushed between; spread in the filling and make 5 hollows, crack an egg into each and sprinkle with the remaining cheese.
Cover with the remaining paper-thin layers, brushing each with oil and blowing a little air between them; seal the edges and prick the top.
Bake at 180°C for 55–60 minutes until deep golden; serve warm or cold at Easter.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg breast of veal, with a pocket cut by the butcher
200 g veal mince and 100 g veal sweetbread or brain (optional)
1 onion, 1 carrot, 1 celery stick for the broth
steps: Brown the mince (and sweetbreads) in a little butter until cooked, cool, then mix with peas, raw eggs, Parmigiano, nuts, marjoram, salt and nutmeg; place the hard-boiled eggs in the middle.
Fill the veal pocket two-thirds full (it swells), sew it closed with kitchen string and prick it with a needle.
Simmer in salted water with the vegetables for 2.5–3 hours, pricking to release steam, until the stuffing reaches 75°C in the centre.
Drain, press between two plates under a weight until cold, then serve in thin slices with salsa verde or a green salad.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 600 g fresh anchovies, heads and bones removed, opened flat
2 slices bread, soaked in milk and squeezed
1 garlic clove and 2 tbsp parsley, chopped
steps: Mix the bread, egg, Parmigiano, garlic, parsley and herbs into a soft filling and season.
Spread a little filling on half the anchovies and cover each with another, skin side out, like a sandwich.
Coat lightly in breadcrumbs and arrange in an oiled baking dish; drizzle with oil.
Bake at 200°C for 15–20 minutes until golden and the fish is cooked through; serve hot or cold with lemon.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 rabbit (about 1.3 kg), cut into pieces (substitute chicken thighs)
2 garlic cloves and 1 sprig rosemary, plus thyme and bay leaf
200 ml dry white wine (Vermentino or Pigato)
steps: Brown the rabbit pieces in the oil with the garlic and herbs over medium-high heat for 10 minutes.
Pour in the wine and let it bubble until reduced by half.
Add the broth, cover and simmer gently 45 minutes, turning occasionally.
Add the olives and pine nuts and cook uncovered 10–15 minutes more until the rabbit is tender and cooked through and the sauce is glossy; serve with roast potatoes or bread.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg presoaked stockfish (stoccafisso ammollato; air-dried cod soaked 3 days in changing water, sold ready-soaked in Italian fish shops; substitute salt cod soaked 48 hours)
600 g waxy potatoes, cut in chunks
1 onion, 2 garlic cloves and 1 celery stick, chopped
60 g Taggiasca olives and 30 g pine nuts
steps: Soak dried stockfish in cold water for 3 days, changing it twice a day, then skin, bone and cut into pieces.
Fry the onion, garlic, celery and anchovies in the oil over medium heat for 10 minutes, add the fish and wine and let it reduce.
Add tomatoes, cover and simmer gently 45 minutes.
Add the potatoes, olives and pine nuts and cook 30 minutes more until the potatoes are tender and the fish flakes; serve hot.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 600 g firm white fish (gurnard, sea bass), poached until opaque and flaked
500 g mixed shellfish (prawns, mussels, a small lobster), cooked through
1 kg mixed vegetables (green beans, carrots, cauliflower, beetroot, celery, potatoes, artichokes), boiled separately
6 ship's biscuits (gallette del marinaio) or rusks, rubbed with garlic and moistened with vinegar water
Salsa verde: 1 bunch parsley, 30 g pine nuts, 3 anchovies, 1 tbsp capers, 2 hard-boiled egg yolks, 1 slice bread, vinegar and 150 ml olive oil
4 hard-boiled eggs and olives, to garnish
steps: Blend all the salsa verde ingredients to a thick green sauce and season.
Dress each vegetable and the fish separately with oil, vinegar and salt.
Line a large platter with the biscuits and build a dome by layering fish, vegetables and salsa verde, finishing with fish and green sauce.
Decorate with prawns, the lobster, mussels, egg halves and olives, chill 1 hour and serve — Genoa's grand Christmas salad.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 courgettes, 2 small aubergines, 2 onions and 2 peppers (or courgette flowers)
1 slice bread, soaked in milk and squeezed
1 garlic clove and a handful of parsley and marjoram, chopped
steps: Halve the courgettes and aubergines and scoop out the flesh; halve the onions and remove the inner layers; blanch the shells 3 minutes.
Chop the scooped vegetable flesh and inner onion, sauté in 2 tbsp oil for 10 minutes, then mix with the potato, bread, eggs, Parmigiano, garlic and herbs.
Fill the shells generously, sprinkle with breadcrumbs and set in an oiled dish; drizzle with the rest of the oil.
Bake at 190°C for 40–45 minutes until golden on top and tender; serve warm or cold.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 garlic clove and 1 tbsp fresh marjoram, chopped
steps: Boil the green beans and potatoes in salted water until very tender, about 20 minutes, then drain well.
Chop the beans finely and mash the potatoes, then mix with eggs, Parmigiano, ricotta, garlic, marjoram and salt.
Spread in an oiled baking dish dusted with breadcrumbs, sprinkle more crumbs on top, and score a diamond pattern with a fork; drizzle with oil.
Bake at 180°C for 40–45 minutes until set and golden; serve warm or cold in squares.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 100 ml milk and 2 tbsp orange-flower water
100 g candied orange and citron, diced
50 g pine nuts and 1 tsp fennel seeds
steps: Cream the butter and sugar, then beat in the eggs, milk and orange-flower water.
Mix in the flour and baking powder, then the raisins, candied fruit, pine nuts and fennel seeds to a firm dough.
Shape into a flat dome about 20 cm across on a lined tray and cut a triangle on top.
Bake at 180°C for 40–45 minutes until golden brown and a skewer comes out clean; this is the low "basso" pandolce, served at Christmas with a sprig of bay on top.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 80 g icing sugar, plus extra to dust
3 hard-boiled egg yolks, pushed through a sieve
steps: Rub the butter into the flour, starch, sugar, zest and salt, then add the sieved yolks and bring together quickly into a soft dough.
Wrap and chill 1 hour.
Roll to 1 cm and cut with a fluted flower cutter, then cut a small hole in the centre.
Bake at 170°C for 12–15 minutes until just set and pale; cool and dust heavily with icing sugar.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 250 g almond flour or finely ground almonds (or hazelnuts)
100 g dark chocolate and 50 ml cream for the ganache
steps: Mix the almonds, sugar and cocoa, then work in the egg whites and honey to a thick piping paste.
Pipe small rosettes with a star nozzle onto a lined tray and leave to dry 1 hour.
Bake at 190°C for 12–15 minutes until firm outside but soft inside, then cool.
Heat the cream, melt in the chocolate, cool to spreading consistency and sandwich the biscuits in pairs.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 egg yolks plus 2 whole eggs for coating
Oil for frying and sugar to dust
steps: Heat the milk with lemon zest; whisk yolks, sugar and flour, add the hot milk and cook over medium-low heat, whisking, for 6–8 minutes until very thick.
Pour into an oiled tray 2 cm deep, smooth and chill at least 3 hours until firm.
Cut into diamonds, dip in beaten egg then breadcrumbs.
Shallow-fry in hot oil at 175°C for 1–2 minutes per side until golden, drain and serve hot dusted with sugar, as part of the Ligurian fritto misto.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg fresh peas in the pod (about 400 g shelled; frozen petits pois as substitute)
1.5 l light meat or vegetable broth
steps: Shell the peas, rinse the empty pods and simmer them in the broth for 20 minutes, then blend or press them through a sieve back into the broth so it tastes intensely of peas; keep it at a bare simmer.
Melt half the butter in a heavy pot over medium-low heat and soften the onion and pancetta for 6–8 minutes until translucent and fragrant but not browned.
Add the peas and a ladle of broth and cook for 5 minutes, then stir in the rice and add broth a ladle at a time, stirring often.
Cook for about 16–18 minutes until the rice is tender; the dish should stay soupy, "all'onda", looser than a risotto and almost spoonable.
Off the heat beat in the remaining butter, the Grana Padano and the parsley, rest for 1 minute and serve in warm bowls.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 600 g whole cuttlefish (seppie) with ink sacs, or cleaned cuttlefish plus 2 sachets (8 g) cuttlefish ink
320 g Vialone Nano or Carnaroli rice
1.2 l light fish broth, kept simmering
1/2 tsp salt and black pepper to taste
steps: Clean the cuttlefish, carefully saving the silvery ink sacs, then cut the bodies into thin strips and the tentacles into small pieces.
Warm the oil in a wide pan over medium heat, soften the onion and garlic for 5 minutes, discard the garlic, then add the cuttlefish and cook for 5 minutes until it turns opaque.
Pour in half the wine, cover and stew gently for 15 minutes until the cuttlefish is tender.
Add the rice, toast it for 2 minutes, splash in the rest of the wine and then add broth a ladle at a time, stirring often; after 5 minutes squeeze in the ink diluted in a little broth.

Cook for 16–18 minutes until the rice is al dente and the risotto is glossy black and wavy; Venetians finish it with oil and parsley rather than cheese, so beat in a final spoon of oil, season and serve at once.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 heads radicchio rosso di Treviso tardivo (about 400 g), sliced into strips; precoce radicchio or red endive as substitute
320 g Carnaroli or Vialone Nano rice
100 ml dry red or white wine
60 g Grana Padano (vegetarian-rennet hard cheese if preferred), grated
50 g Montasio or Asiago cheese, diced (optional)
steps: Melt 30 g butter in a heavy pan over medium-low heat and soften the shallot for 4 minutes until translucent.
Add two-thirds of the radicchio and cook for 4 minutes until wilted and turning deep purple-brown.
Stir in the rice and toast for 2 minutes, then pour in the wine and let it evaporate completely.

Add the hot broth a ladle at a time, stirring often, for 16–18 minutes until the rice is creamy and al dente; add the remaining raw radicchio in the last 3 minutes for colour and a pleasant bitterness.
Off the heat beat in the remaining butter, the grated cheese and the diced Asiago if using, cover for 1 minute and serve.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 320 g Vialone Nano or Carnaroli rice
250 ml Amarone della Valpolicella wine (or another rich Valpolicella red)
1.2 l beef or capon broth, kept simmering
80 g Monte Veronese or Grana Padano cheese, grated
steps: Melt 30 g butter in a heavy pot over medium-low heat and soften the onion for 5 minutes without letting it colour.
Add the rice and toast it for 2–3 minutes, stirring, until the grains are hot and slightly translucent at the edges.
Pour in about two-thirds of the Amarone and stir until it is fully absorbed and the rice turns a deep wine-red.
Continue adding the hot broth a ladle at a time, stirring, for 15–17 minutes; add the remaining wine with the last ladle of broth so its aroma stays fresh.
When the rice is al dente and creamy, take it off the heat and beat in the remaining butter and the cheese; rest for 1 minute, season and serve with a glass of the same wine.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 800 g small lagoon goby fish (gò), gutted; any small rockfish, gurnard or mixed soup fish as substitute
1 onion, half sliced and half finely chopped
1 celery stalk, 1 small carrot and 1 bay leaf
steps: Put the cleaned gò in a pot with the sliced onion, celery, carrot, bay leaf, 1 garlic clove, the salt and the water; bring to the boil and simmer gently for 40 minutes.
Pass everything through a food mill or press hard through a fine sieve to make a thick, cloudy broth, removing every bone; keep it hot.
Warm the oil in a heavy pan over medium-low heat and soften the chopped onion and the second garlic clove for 5 minutes, then discard the garlic.
Toast the rice for 2 minutes, add the wine and let it evaporate, then add the fish broth a ladle at a time, stirring, for about 16–18 minutes until creamy and al dente.
Finish with a drizzle of oil and the parsley (no cheese with fish in Venice), let it rest for 1 minute and serve "all'onda", loose and wavy.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g bigoli (thick whole-wheat spaghetti; wholemeal spaghetti as substitute)
3 large white onions, very thinly sliced
8 salted anchovies, rinsed and filleted (or 16 oil-packed fillets); salted sardines are also traditional
1 tbsp coarse salt for the pasta water
steps: Warm the oil in a wide pan over low heat, add the onions with the water, cover and stew for 20–25 minutes, stirring now and then, until completely soft and golden but not browned.
Add the anchovies and stir over low heat for 3–4 minutes until they melt into a creamy brown sauce; season with pepper.
Meanwhile boil the bigoli in lightly salted water for 10–12 minutes until al dente.
Drain, keeping a cup of the water, and toss the pasta in the sauce over low heat for 1 minute with a splash of water until glossy.
Serve with parsley scattered over; no cheese is added to this Lenten Venetian dish.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 duck (about 1.8 kg), with liver, heart and gizzard
1 onion, 1 carrot and 1 celery stalk, halved
steps: Clean the duck and put it in a large pot with the onion, carrot, celery, bay, rosemary, salt and water; bring to the boil, skim and simmer gently for 1 hour 30 minutes until the meat is tender and the legs pull away easily.
Lift out the duck (serve it as a main course with mostarda) and strain and degrease the broth, keeping it at the boil.
Finely chop the duck liver, heart and gizzard; melt the butter with the sage in a pan over medium heat and fry the giblets for 6–8 minutes until fully cooked and browned.
Cook the bigoli in the boiling duck broth for 10–12 minutes until al dente.
Drain and toss with the giblet butter and a little broth, then serve with grated Grana Padano.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g dried Lamon or borlotti beans, soaked overnight (or 3 x 400 g cans borlotti)
1 small ham hock or 150 g pork rind (cotenna), scraped and cut into strips
1 onion, 1 carrot and 1 celery stalk, finely chopped
4 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, plus extra to serve
200 g short pasta such as maltagliati or ditalini
steps: Drain the soaked beans and put them in a heavy pot with the water, pork rind or hock, potato, bay and rosemary; bring to the boil and simmer gently for 1 hour 30 minutes–2 hours until creamy-soft.
Meanwhile soften the onion, carrot and celery in the oil over medium-low heat for 10 minutes and add them to the beans for the last 30 minutes.
Remove the herbs and bone, blend or pass about half the beans and return the purée so the soup is thick and velvety; dice the rind and meat back in and season.
Add the pasta and simmer for 8–10 minutes, stirring often so it does not stick, until tender.
Let the soup rest for 10 minutes off the heat (Venetians like it warm rather than piping hot) and serve with a thread of raw olive oil and black pepper.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 pigeons (squab), cleaned; guinea fowl or chicken thighs as substitute
12 slices stale country bread, about 1 cm thick
1 onion, 1 carrot and 1 celery stalk, finely chopped
1.5 l rich chicken or capon broth
steps: Melt the butter in a heavy pot over medium heat and brown the pigeons on all sides with the herbs for 10 minutes, then add the chopped vegetables and soften for 5 minutes.

Pour in the wine, let it bubble off, add a ladle of broth, cover and braise gently for 1 hour until the meat is very tender and fully cooked; cool slightly, bone the birds and shred the meat, keeping the pan juices.
Toast the bread slices in the oven at 200 °C for 8 minutes until dry and golden.

In a deep earthenware or ovenproof dish make layers of bread, shredded meat, pan juices and Grana Padano, moistening each layer with hot broth until the bread is soaked but not swimming; finish with bread and cheese.
Bake covered at 140 °C for 2–3 hours, adding a ladle of broth whenever it looks dry, until it is "coada" (brooded) into a soft, set, golden pie; rest 10 minutes and serve in wedges.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 600 g fresh sardines, scaled, gutted and heads removed (butterflied if you like)
100 ml extra-virgin olive oil, plus sunflower oil for frying
40 g raisins, soaked in warm water
steps: Dust the sardines in flour and shallow-fry them in hot sunflower oil (180 °C) for 2 minutes per side until golden and cooked through; drain on paper and salt lightly.
Warm the olive oil in a wide pan over low heat and stew the onions for 20 minutes until very soft and golden, then add the vinegar (and sugar if using) and simmer 3 minutes.
Stir the drained raisins and pine nuts into the onion "saor".
In a glass or ceramic dish layer the sardines with the hot onion mixture, finishing with onions, and pour over all the juices.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 24 hours (up to 3 days) so the vinegar mellows, and serve at room temperature as a cicchetto or with grilled white polenta.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg dried stockfish (stoccafisso, which Vicenza calls "bacalà"), pre-soaked; or dry stockfish soaked yourself for 2–3 days
steps: Soak the stockfish in cold water in the fridge for 2–3 days, changing the water twice a day, until soft and swollen; open it, remove the bones and skin and cut it into pieces about 6 cm.
Soften the onions in a few tablespoons of the oil over low heat for 15 minutes, then add the anchovies and parsley and stir until the anchovies melt.
Stuff a little of the onion mixture into each piece of fish, dust the pieces with flour mixed with the cheese, salt and pepper, and pack them snugly side by side in a heavy pan or earthenware dish.
Spread the remaining onions over, pour in the milk and enough oil to just cover the fish.

Simmer at the lowest possible heat, uncovered and never stirred (only gently shake the pan), for 4–4.5 hours until the fish is meltingly tender and the sauce reduced and creamy; serve with soft or grilled polenta.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 600 g calf's liver, membrane removed, sliced very thin into small strips
600 g white onions, very thinly sliced
steps: Heat the oil and butter in a wide pan over low heat, add the onions with a pinch of salt and stew them gently, covered, for 20 minutes until soft, sweet and pale gold.
Raise the heat to high, push the onions aside, add the liver strips and stir-fry them for 2–3 minutes only, until they lose their raw colour but stay just pink inside.
Pour in the wine (and vinegar if using) and toss for 1 minute more, mixing with the onions.
Season with salt and pepper only at the end (salting liver early toughens it), scatter over the parsley and serve immediately with soft white polenta.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg whole cuttlefish with ink sacs (or cleaned cuttlefish plus 2 sachets ink)
250 g white polenta flour (biancoperla; yellow polenta as substitute)
steps: Clean the cuttlefish, saving the ink sacs in a little water, and cut the bodies into strips and the tentacles into pieces.
Soften the onion and garlic in the oil over medium-low heat for 5 minutes, add the cuttlefish and cook for 5 minutes until opaque, then pour in the wine and let it bubble.

Add the passata if using, cover and simmer gently for 30 minutes, then stir in the ink and cook uncovered for 10–15 minutes more until the cuttlefish is tender and the sauce thick and black; finish with parsley.
Meanwhile bring the salted water to the boil, rain in the polenta while whisking and cook over low heat for 40 minutes, stirring often, until soft and pulling from the sides.
Spoon the soft white polenta onto plates and ladle the black cuttlefish alongside.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g schie (tiny grey lagoon shrimp), rinsed; any very small brown or grey shrimp as substitute
steps: Bring the water to the boil with 1.5 tsp salt, rain in the polenta while whisking and cook over low heat for 40 minutes, stirring often, until soft and creamy.
Meanwhile bring a pan of salted water to the boil, add the schie and cook for 1–2 minutes until they turn pink and float; drain.
Warm the oil with the garlic in a pan over medium heat for 1 minute, add the shrimp and toss for 1 minute, then remove the garlic and finish with parsley, a squeeze of lemon and a pinch of salt.
Pour the soft polenta onto plates and pile the shrimp on top; in Venice the tiny schie are eaten shell and all.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.2 kg horse meat shoulder in one piece (beef chuck or cheek as substitute)
1 l Valpolicella or other robust red wine
2 onions, 1 carrot and 1 celery stalk, chopped
2 garlic cloves, 2 bay leaves, 4 cloves and 1 small cinnamon stick
steps: Put the meat in a bowl with the vegetables, garlic, spices and wine, cover and marinate in the fridge for 24 hours (up to 48), turning it once or twice.
Lift out the meat, pat dry and dust with flour; strain the marinade, keeping wine and vegetables separately.
Melt the lard in a heavy casserole over medium-high heat and brown the meat on all sides for 10 minutes, then add the marinated vegetables and soften for 5 minutes.

Pour in the wine, tomato paste if using, salt and pepper and enough broth to come halfway up the meat; cover and simmer very gently for 3.5–4 hours, turning occasionally, until it is tender enough to cut with a spoon.
Lift out the meat, blend or sieve the sauce and reduce it until thick and glossy, then slice the meat back into it and serve with soft polenta or gnocchi.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg beef brisket or shoulder (bollito cut)
1 cotechino sausage (about 500 g) or 4 chicken legs
steps: Bring the water to the boil with the vegetables and salt, add the beef, reduce to a gentle simmer and cook for 3 hours, skimming, until tender; cook the cotechino separately in simmering water for 2–2.5 hours (or as the pack says), or add chicken legs to the beef for the last hour.
For the pearà, melt the marrow or butter in a heavy pan (traditionally earthenware) over low heat, add the breadcrumbs and stir for 2 minutes until they absorb the fat.
Add hot meat broth a ladle at a time, stirring, and cook very gently for 1.5–2 hours, adding broth as needed, until it becomes a thick, smooth, porridge-like sauce.
Stir in the Grana Padano and plenty of black pepper (pearà means "peppery"), taste for salt.
Slice the meats, moisten them with a little broth and serve with the hot pearà spooned alongside.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g very fresh beef fillet or top round, trimmed, from a trusted butcher (for eating raw)
4 tbsp mayonnaise, made with pasteurised egg yolk
steps: Wrap the beef tightly in cling film and freeze for 30 minutes until firm, which makes slicing paper-thin easy.
Slice it as thinly as possible with a very sharp knife and arrange the slices to cover chilled plates; flatten any thick ones between sheets of cling film with a rolling pin.
Whisk the mayonnaise with the Worcestershire sauce, lemon juice, milk and salt into a thin sauce that drizzles easily.

Drizzle the sauce over the beef in a criss-cross pattern as at Harry's Bar, where the dish was invented, add rocket if you like, and serve immediately; keep the meat refrigerated until serving and do not serve raw beef to pregnant people, young children or the immunocompromised.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g dried stockfish (stoccafisso), soaked 2–3 days, or salt cod soaked 48 hours
200 ml mild extra-virgin olive oil (or half sunflower oil)
12 slices grilled white polenta or toasted bread, to serve
steps: Soak the fish in cold water in the fridge for 2–3 days, changing the water twice daily, until soft.
Put it in a pot of cold water with the bay leaf, bring to a simmer and cook gently for 20 minutes until it flakes; drain, keeping a little cooking water, and remove all skin and bones.

While still warm, beat the fish with a wooden spoon or a mixer paddle, adding the oil in a thin stream as for mayonnaise, until it turns into a white, fluffy, spreadable cream (add a little cooking water if too stiff).
Season with white pepper, salt if needed and parsley (add grated garlic if you like), and serve at room temperature spread on grilled polenta or bread as a classic cicchetto.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 16 moeche (soft-shell green crabs from the lagoon, in spring and autumn); any soft-shell crabs as substitute
1 l sunflower or peanut oil for frying
steps: Beat the eggs with the salt in a bowl; rinse the soft-shell crabs and put them in the egg, cover and refrigerate for 2 hours so they soak it up (traditionally they are put in alive; with bought cleaned soft-shells simply soak them).
Heat the oil in a deep pan to 175–180 °C.
Lift the crabs from the egg, toss them in the flour and shake off the excess.
Fry in batches for 3–4 minutes, turning once, until deep golden and crisp and cooked through.
Drain on paper, salt lightly and serve at once with lemon wedges and a glass of cold white wine.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 baguette or 12 slices grilled white polenta
150 g sarde in saor (see that recipe)
100 g sopressa veneta or other salami, thinly sliced
steps: Slice the baguette on the diagonal into 1 cm slices, brush lightly with oil and toast at 200 °C for 6–8 minutes until crisp at the edges (or grill the polenta slices until marked).
Top some crostini with a spoon of baccalà mantecato and others with a nest of sarde in saor with its onions.
Make more with a fold of sopressa, and half-eggs topped with an anchovy fillet.
Thread the meatballs and pickled onions or olives on toothpicks.
Arrange everything on a board and serve at room temperature as at a Venetian bacaro, with an "ombra" (small glass) of wine or a spritz.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Bring a large pot of water to the boil with the bay leaf, celery, carrot, peppercorns and salt.
Holding each octopus by the head, dip the tentacles into the boiling water three times so they curl, then drop them in.
Simmer gently for 30–40 minutes until a skewer slides easily into the thickest part; leave them to cool in the water for 10 minutes so they stay tender.
Drain and dress while warm with oil, garlic, parsley, lemon juice and a pinch of salt; at Venetian street stalls they are served on toothpicks with a sprinkle of salt and pepper, in a paper cone.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 heads radicchio rosso di Treviso (precoce or tardivo); red endive as substitute
1 tbsp red wine vinegar or aged balsamic vinegar
steps: Trim the root ends and cut each head lengthwise into quarters, keeping the core so the leaves hold together.
Brush with half the oil and season with salt and pepper.
Grill on a hot ridged grill pan or barbecue over medium-high heat for 3–4 minutes per side until wilted, charred at the edges and tender at the core.
Arrange on a plate, drizzle with the remaining oil and the vinegar, and serve warm with grilled meats, Montasio cheese or polenta.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg white asparagus from Bassano del Grappa (any thick white asparagus)
steps: Peel the asparagus from just below the tip downward and trim the woody ends; tie them in a bundle.
Stand the bundle upright in a tall pot of salted boiling water with the tips above the water, cover and cook for 12–15 minutes until the stalks are tender when pierced.
Meanwhile boil the eggs for 9 minutes, cool in cold water and peel.
Mash the yolks with a fork in a bowl, adding the oil, vinegar, salt and pepper, and chop the whites finely into the sauce.
Serve the warm asparagus with the egg sauce; each diner traditionally mixes their own sauce at the table.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 very fresh eggs, separated (use pasteurised eggs if concerned about raw egg)
steps: Make the espresso and let it cool completely in a shallow dish.
Whisk the yolks with the sugar for 5 minutes until pale and thick, then beat in the mascarpone until smooth.
Whisk the whites with the salt to firm peaks and fold them gently into the mascarpone cream in three additions.
Dip the savoiardi one at a time quickly in the coffee (1–2 seconds a side) and lay them in a single layer in a dish; cover with half the cream, then repeat with a second layer of biscuits and cream.
Smooth the top, cover and refrigerate for at least 5 hours, ideally overnight, then dust thickly with cocoa just before serving.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 5 eggs plus 2 yolks, at room temperature
12 g fresh yeast (or 4 g instant dry yeast)
1 vanilla pod, seeds scraped, and grated zest of 1 lemon
steps: Dissolve the yeast in the milk, mix with 100 g flour, 1 egg and 1 tbsp sugar into a soft starter and leave covered for 1 hour until bubbly.
Add 200 g flour, 2 eggs and 50 g sugar, knead 10 minutes until elastic, then leave to double for 2 hours.

Add the remaining flour, eggs, yolks, sugar, salt, vanilla and zest and knead for 15 minutes until silky; work in the butter a little at a time until the dough is smooth, shiny and pulls cleanly from the bowl, then chill it for 1 hour.
Shape into a tight ball and drop it, seam up, into a well-buttered 1 kg star-shaped pandoro mould; cover and leave to rise in a warm place for 6–8 hours until the dough reaches the rim.

Bake at 170 °C for 15 minutes, then at 160 °C for 35 minutes until a skewer comes out clean (cover the top with foil if it browns too quickly); cool in the mould for 1 hour, then unmould and cool fully.
Before serving, put the pandoro in a bag with the icing sugar and shake to coat, as Veronese families do at Christmas.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 15 g fresh yeast (or 5 g instant dry yeast)
100 g raisins, soaked in 2 tbsp grappa or rum
grated zest of 1 lemon and 1 pinch salt
1 l sunflower or peanut oil for frying
60 g icing or caster sugar for rolling
steps: Dissolve the yeast in the milk, then whisk in the flour, eggs, sugar, zest and salt to make a soft, sticky batter-dough; beat for 5 minutes.
Fold in the drained raisins and pine nuts with the grappa, cover and leave in a warm place for 1.5–2 hours until doubled.
Heat the oil to 170 °C in a deep pan.
Drop walnut-sized spoonfuls of dough into the oil (use two wet spoons) and fry in batches for 4–5 minutes, turning, until puffed, deep golden and cooked through.
Drain on paper and roll in sugar while warm; these are the classic Carnival fritters of Venice.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 100 g raisins, soaked in warm water or grappa
grated zest of 1 lemon and 1 pinch salt
steps: Heat the oven to 180 °C and line two trays with baking paper.
Beat the butter with the sugar until creamy, then beat in the eggs one at a time with the zest.
Mix in the cornmeal, flour, baking powder and salt to make a soft dough, then fold in the drained raisins.
Shape the dough into small diamond or oval cookies about 6 cm long and 1 cm thick and set them on the trays.
Bake for 15–20 minutes until golden at the edges; cool on a rack and dust with icing sugar ("zaleti" means "little yellow ones" in Venetian).
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 7 g fresh yeast (or 2 g instant dry yeast)
steps: Dissolve the yeast in the milk, mix with 60 g flour into a soft starter and leave covered for 30 minutes until bubbly.
Add the remaining flour, sugar, butter, egg white and salt and knead for 10 minutes into a smooth, firm dough.
Shape into two thin logs about 4 cm wide, place on a lined tray and leave to rise for about 2 hours until doubled.
Bake at 180 °C for 15–20 minutes until pale golden and set, then cool completely (ideally rest overnight) so they slice cleanly.

Slice the logs on the diagonal as thinly as possible (2–3 mm) and dry the slices on trays at 140 °C for 25–30 minutes until crisp and lightly golden; store airtight and dunk in coffee, hot chocolate or sweet wine.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 vanilla pod, seeds scraped, and grated zest of 1 lemon
steps: Beat the butter with the sugar until creamy, then add the yolks, vanilla, zest and salt.
Work in the flour quickly into a firm, smooth dough, adding milk only if it is crumbly; chill for 15 minutes.
Roll pieces into ropes about 1 cm thick and shape into rings about 8 cm across (the Burano "bussolà") or into S shapes ("esse").
Bake on lined trays at 180 °C for 12–15 minutes until golden around the edges.
Cool completely on a rack; they keep for weeks in a tin and are traditionally dipped in sweet wine.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 15 g fresh yeast (or 5 g instant dry yeast)
grated zest of 1 orange and 1 lemon, and 1 vanilla pod
30 g whole almonds and 2 tbsp pearl sugar, for the top
steps: Dissolve the yeast in the milk, mix with 100 g flour and 1 tbsp sugar into a starter and leave covered for 1 hour until bubbly.
Add the rest of the flour, eggs, yolks, sugar, zests, vanilla seeds and salt and knead for 15 minutes; add the butter in pieces and knead until the dough is glossy and elastic.
Cover and leave to rise in a warm place for 3 hours until doubled, then shape into a ball and set it in a buttered 1 kg panettone or colomba mould (or a deep round tin).
Leave to rise for 4–6 hours until nearly at the rim, brush with egg white and scatter over almonds and pearl sugar.
Bake at 170 °C for 40–45 minutes until deep golden and a skewer comes out clean; cool on a rack and serve at Easter with coffee or sweet wine.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 ripe white peaches (about 300 g), peeled and stoned
1 tsp caster sugar (optional, if the peaches are not very sweet)
600 ml chilled Prosecco, bought from a licensed producer
steps: Purée the peaches in a blender or press them through a sieve to a smooth, pale-pink purée, stirring in the lemon juice and sugar if needed.
Chill the purée for at least 30 minutes, along with the Prosecco and the glasses.
Put about 50 ml peach purée in each flute and slowly top with Prosecco in a ratio of roughly 1 part purée to 3 parts wine.
Stir gently once and serve immediately, as at Harry's Bar in Venice where it was created.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 90 ml Prosecco, bought from a licensed producer
60 ml bitter aperitif (Aperol, Select or Campari), bought
steps: Fill a large wine glass with ice.
Pour in the Prosecco, then the bitter aperitif, then top with the soda water (the classic 3-2-1 ratio).
Stir gently once, garnish with the orange slice and, as in Venice, an olive on a stick; serve at once with cicchetti.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 bottle (700 ml) grappa from a licensed distillery, e.g. from Bassano del Grappa
1 small cup espresso per person, for "caffè corretto" (optional)
steps: Grappa is a strong Italian spirit distilled from grape pomace, the skins and seeds left after winemaking; it is made only by licensed distillers and should be bought, never home-distilled.
Serve young (giovane) grappa chilled to about 9–13 °C and aged (invecchiata) grappa at cool room temperature, pouring about 30 ml into tulip glasses.
Sip slowly after a meal as a digestivo, or add a dash to an espresso to make a "caffè corretto"; drink responsibly.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g floury potatoes, peeled and thinly sliced or coarsely grated
400 g Montasio cheese (a mix of young and medium-aged), grated or cubed; Asiago as substitute
steps: Melt the butter in a 24 cm non-stick or cast-iron pan over medium-low heat and soften the onion for 5 minutes.
Add the potatoes with the salt and a splash of water, cover and cook for 15 minutes, stirring, until soft and partly broken up.
Stir in the cheese and keep stirring for a few minutes until it melts into the potatoes, then press the mixture into an even cake.
Cook without stirring for 8–10 minutes until a deep golden crust forms underneath and fat shows at the edges.
Flip with the help of a plate and cook the other side for 6–8 minutes until crisp and golden; cut into wedges and serve hot with grilled yellow polenta.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 musetto (Friulian cotechino-style pork sausage, about 600 g); cotechino as substitute
800 g brovada (turnips fermented in red grape pomace; or sauerkraut-style sour turnip), drained and grated
steps: Prick the musetto, put it in a pot of cold water, bring slowly to a simmer and cook gently for 2.5–3 hours (or as the pack says) until fully cooked and tender.
Meanwhile rinse the brovada briefly if very sour and squeeze it dry.
Melt the lard in a pan over medium-low heat and soften the onion and garlic for 5 minutes, then add the brovada, bay leaf and caraway.
Cook covered over low heat for 1–1.5 hours, adding broth as needed, until soft and lightly golden; season.
Slice the hot musetto thickly and serve on the brovada, traditionally with polenta, especially at New Year.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.5 kg mixed boiled pork cuts: neck (coppa), shoulder, pork belly, tongue and a cotechino or Kranjska sausage
2 bay leaves and 1 tsp black peppercorns
500 g sauerkraut (capuzi garbi), warmed, to serve
steps: Bring the water to the boil with the onion, carrot, celery, bay, peppercorns and salt.
Add the large cuts of pork and tongue, return to a bare simmer and cook gently for 1.5–2 hours, skimming, until tender; add the sausages for the last 30–40 minutes (or as their packs say).
Peel the tongue while hot and keep everything in the hot broth until serving.
Slice the meats thickly and serve steaming on a board, as in a Trieste buffet, with fresh horseradish, mustard and warm sauerkraut or potatoes.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg beef shin or chuck, cut into 4 cm cubes
60 g lard or 4 tbsp sunflower oil
2 tbsp sweet paprika and 1 tsp hot paprika
1 tsp caraway seeds and 1 tsp dried marjoram
steps: Melt the lard in a heavy casserole over medium-low heat and cook the onions for 20 minutes until soft and golden.
Take the pan off the heat, stir in both paprikas (they burn easily) and the tomato paste, then add the beef and stir to coat.
Return to medium heat, add the garlic, caraway, marjoram, bay, salt and enough broth to almost cover the meat.
Cover and simmer very gently for 2.5–3 hours, stirring occasionally and adding liquid if needed, until the meat is tender and the onions have melted into a thick red sauce.
Serve hot with polenta, boiled potatoes or bread dumplings, as in Trieste's buffets.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g plain flour, 2 eggs and 1 egg yolk for the pasta
80 g Grana Padano or aged Montasio, grated
steps: Knead the flour, eggs and yolk into a firm pasta dough, wrap and rest for 30 minutes.
Wilt the spinach in a pan for 3 minutes, squeeze it very dry and chop finely; mix with the ricotta, half the cheese, the nutmeg and salt.
Roll the dough thinly into a rectangle about 30 x 40 cm, spread the filling evenly leaving a 2 cm border and roll it up tightly like a strudel.
Wrap the roll in a clean cotton cloth, tie the ends with string and simmer it in a fish kettle or wide pan of salted water for 40 minutes.
Unwrap, let it rest for 5 minutes and slice into 2 cm rounds; serve with butter melted with sage until nutty, and the remaining cheese.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 150 ml warm water and 1 tbsp sunflower oil
60 g raisins, soaked in warm water
40 g dark chocolate or 1 tbsp cocoa powder
2 tbsp chopped parsley and mint, 1 tsp cinnamon and grated zest of 1 lemon
80 g smoked ricotta (ricotta affumicata), grated; aged ricotta salata as substitute
steps: Knead the flour, warm water, oil and a pinch of salt into a smooth, soft dough, wrap and rest for 30 minutes.
Mix the potato with the chopped raisins, grated chocolate, herbs, cinnamon, zest, sugar and salt into a sweet-savoury filling typical of Carnia.
Roll the dough thinly, cut into 8 cm rounds, put a teaspoon of filling on each, fold into half-moons and pinch the edges into a pleated border.
Cook in gently boiling salted water for 4–5 minutes until they float and the dough is tender.
Drain and serve with butter melted until golden, a shower of grated smoked ricotta and a pinch of sugar and cinnamon.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 12 small ripe plums (susine or Italian prune plums), stoned
2 tbsp caster sugar and 1/2 tsp salt
steps: Boil the potatoes in their skins for 25–30 minutes until tender, peel while hot and press through a ricer; cool slightly.
Knead in the flour, egg and salt quickly to make a soft, smooth dough.
Fill each plum with a sugar cube and a pinch of cinnamon, wrap it in a flattened piece of dough and roll into a sealed ball.
Cook in gently boiling salted water for 10–12 minutes, until they float and then a further 3 minutes.
Meanwhile toast the breadcrumbs in the butter over medium heat for 4 minutes until golden; roll the drained gnocchi in it and serve dusted with cinnamon sugar.

ingredients: 300 g dried borlotti beans, soaked overnight
150 g smoked pancetta or pork ribs
2 bay leaves and 1 tsp cumin or caraway seeds
2 tbsp plain flour and 3 tbsp lard or olive oil
steps: Simmer the drained beans with the potatoes, pork, 1 bay leaf and the water for 1.5 hours until the beans are soft; mash a few beans and potatoes to thicken.
Meanwhile cook the sauerkraut in a separate pan with a little water, the other bay leaf, the cumin and 1 tbsp lard for 45 minutes until soft.
Make a "pesto": fry the garlic in the remaining lard over medium heat, add the flour and cook for 2 minutes until golden, then stir it into the beans.
Combine the sauerkraut with the beans and simmer together for 20 minutes; dice the meat back in and season.
Rest for 10 minutes and serve hot; jota tastes even better reheated the next day.

ingredients: 40 g Montasio or Grana Padano, grated (optional)
steps: Blanch the spinach in boiling salted water for 2 minutes, drain, squeeze and chop finely.
Melt the butter in a pot over medium heat, sizzle the garlic for 1 minute, then discard it; stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Add the spinach and stir for 2 minutes, then pour in the hot broth and bring to the boil.
Rain in the cornmeal while whisking and simmer over low heat for 30 minutes, stirring often, until it is a creamy, thick green soup.
Season and serve with a little grated cheese if you like.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.2 kg mixed firm fish (turbot, monkfish, scorpion fish, gurnard), cleaned and cut into large pieces on the bone
300 ml water or light fish stock
250 g white polenta, cooked soft, to serve
steps: Warm the oil in a wide pan over medium heat and fry the garlic for 2 minutes until golden, then remove it.
Season the fish with salt and plenty of black pepper and lay it in the oil; cook for 2 minutes per side.
Pour in the vinegar and let it bubble for 2 minutes, then add the water.
Simmer uncovered for 15–20 minutes, shaking the pan rather than stirring, until the fish is cooked through and the sauce is dense and emulsified; this is the fishermen's stew of Grado.
Serve the fish and its peppery sauce over soft white polenta.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 250 g coarse yellow cornmeal (or polenta flour)
50 g fine yellow cornmeal, for the sauce
100 g aged Montasio or smoked ricotta, grated
steps: Bring the salted water to the boil, rain in the coarse cornmeal while whisking and cook over low heat for 40–45 minutes, stirring often, until soft.
Meanwhile mash the fresh ricotta with a few tablespoons of hot polenta water to make it creamy.
Melt the butter in a pan over medium heat, add the fine cornmeal and toast, stirring, for 5–6 minutes until nutty and golden brown.
Spoon the soft polenta into bowls, top with the ricotta cream, pour over the toasted cornmeal butter and grate over the Montasio; "toç in braide" means "sauce in the field" in Friulian.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Boil the potatoes in their skins for 20 minutes until just tender, then peel them.
Melt the lard in a heavy pan (tecia) over medium heat and fry the onion and pancetta for 8 minutes until golden.
Add the potatoes and roughly crush them with a spatula, season with salt, pepper and cumin.
Fry for 10–12 minutes, adding a little broth now and then and scraping the bottom, until you have a mix of soft mash and crunchy golden crust; serve with sausages or boiled pork, Trieste-style.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 tsp sugar or salt, for dusting
steps: Boil the potatoes in their skins for 25 minutes until tender, peel and press through a ricer while hot; let them cool.
Knead in the flour, egg, melted butter and salt quickly into a soft dough.
Roll pieces into finger-thick ropes 10 cm long and bend them into small crescents (kipfel).
Fry in oil heated to 170 °C in batches for 3–4 minutes, turning, until golden and puffed.
Drain on paper and dust with salt to serve with goulash or meats, or with sugar as a sweet snack.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 600 g sardoni (large Adriatic anchovies) or fresh sardines
2 eggs, beaten with a pinch of salt
1 l sunflower or peanut oil for frying
steps: Remove the heads and guts of the fish, open them like a book and pull out the backbone, leaving the tails attached; rinse and pat dry.
Dust each fish in flour, dip in the beaten egg and press into the breadcrumbs.
Heat the oil to 175 °C and fry the fish in batches for 2–3 minutes until golden and cooked through.
Drain on paper, salt and serve hot with lemon, as in the osmizze and buffets of Trieste.
