ingredients: 400 g pitina IGP (smoked meatballs of game or mutton coated in cornmeal, from the Val Tramontina), bought from a specialist producer; smoked salami as substitute
1 small loaf rye or country bread, sliced
steps: Pitina is a traditional cured, smoked meatball from the Pordenone mountains; buy it ready-made and keep it cool.
Slice it thinly and serve raw on a board with bread, Montasio and pickles.
For a warm version, heat the oil in a pan over medium heat, soften the onion for 5 minutes, add thick slices of pitina and fry for 2–3 minutes per side until hot and lightly crisp.
Serve the fried pitina on soft or grilled polenta.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 250 g fresh soft cheese (quark, ricotta or mild sheep's cheese)
steps: Beat the cheese and butter together until smooth and creamy.
Mix in the paprika, caraway, shallot, capers, mustard, salt and pepper until evenly pink.
Chill for at least 30 minutes so the flavours blend.
Shape into a mound, sprinkle with chives and a little more paprika and serve spread on dark rye bread, as in Trieste's buffets.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g plain flour, 2 eggs, 80 g sugar, 80 g butter, 120 ml milk and 10 g fresh yeast for the dough
50 g hazelnuts and 50 g almonds, chopped
100 g raisins, soaked in 4 tbsp grappa or slivovitz
80 g sugar and 50 g dry biscuits or breadcrumbs, crushed
grated zest of 1 lemon and 1 orange, and 1 tsp cinnamon
steps: Dissolve the yeast in the warm milk, then knead with the flour, eggs, sugar, a pinch of salt and soft butter for 10 minutes into a smooth dough; leave to double for 2 hours.
Mix the nuts, drained raisins with their spirit, pine nuts, sugar, biscuit crumbs, melted butter, zests and cinnamon into a moist filling.
Roll the dough into a thin rectangle about 25 x 50 cm, spread with the filling and roll it up along the long side into a tight log.
Coil the log into a snail shape and place it in a buttered 24 cm round tin; leave to rise for 1 hour, then brush with egg.
Bake at 170 °C for 45–50 minutes until deep golden; cool and serve sliced, often sprinkled with a little slivovitz, as in the Natisone valleys.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 100 g walnuts and 50 g almonds, chopped
50 g pine nuts and 50 g raisins (soaked in 2 tbsp rum)
50 g sugar and 30 g dark chocolate, grated
50 g dry breadcrumbs, toasted in 30 g butter
grated zest of 1 lemon, 1/2 tsp cinnamon and 1 pinch clove
steps: Mix the nuts, raisins with rum, peel, sugar, chocolate, buttered crumbs, zest and spices with half the beaten egg into a moist filling.
Roll the puff pastry into a long strip about 15 x 60 cm.
Shape the filling into a log along one long edge, roll the pastry around it and seal the seam.
Coil the roll into a loose spiral on a lined tray and brush with the remaining egg.
Bake at 180 °C for 35–40 minutes until puffed and deep golden; cool before slicing; this is Trieste's Easter pastry.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 20 g fresh yeast (or 7 g instant dry yeast)
grated zest of 1 lemon and 1 orange, and 1 pinch salt
steps: Dissolve the yeast in the milk, mix with 150 g flour into a starter and leave covered for 1 hour until bubbly.
Add the remaining flour, eggs, yolks, sugar, rum, zests and salt and knead for 10 minutes, then knead in the butter until the dough is smooth and elastic.
Let it rise in a warm place for 4–6 hours (or overnight in a cool spot) until doubled.
Divide into two balls, place on lined trays and let rise for 2 hours more; brush with egg and cut a deep three-pointed cross on top with scissors.
Bake at 170 °C for 40–45 minutes until deep brown and a skewer comes out clean; cool and serve at Easter with boiled ham and horseradish or with coffee.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 250 g plain flour, 1 egg, 100 ml lukewarm water, 2 tbsp sunflower oil and 1 pinch salt for the dough
1 kg tart apples (Renetta or Granny Smith), peeled, cored and thinly sliced
60 g raisins, soaked in 2 tbsp rum
60 g breadcrumbs, toasted in 40 g butter
steps: Knead the flour, egg, water, oil and salt for 10 minutes into a very smooth, elastic dough, brush with oil, cover and rest at room temperature for 30 minutes.
Mix the apples with the sugar, cinnamon, drained raisins, pine nuts and zest.
On a floured cloth, roll then stretch the dough with the backs of your hands until it is paper-thin and about 50 x 70 cm; trim the thick edges and brush with melted butter.
Scatter the buttered crumbs over two-thirds of the dough, top with the apple mixture, then lift the cloth to roll the strudel up and slide it onto a lined tray, seam down.
Brush with butter and bake at 190 °C for 40–45 minutes until golden and crisp; cool slightly and dust with icing sugar ("strucolo" is Trieste's word for strudel).
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 150 g walnuts, finely chopped, and 50 g raisins (soaked in grappa)
50 g dry biscuit crumbs and 50 g sugar
grated zest of 1 lemon and 1/2 tsp cinnamon
1 l sunflower oil for frying, and icing sugar for dusting
steps: Knead the flour, butter, sugar, egg, yolk, wine and a pinch of salt into a smooth dough; rest for 30 minutes.
Mix the walnuts, chopped raisins, biscuit crumbs, sugar, zest and cinnamon into a filling, moistening with a little grappa if dry.
Roll the dough thinly, cut into 6 cm rounds, place a teaspoon of filling in the centre, fold into half-moons and seal the edges with a fork.
Fry in oil at 170 °C for 2–3 minutes per side until golden (or bake at 180 °C for 15 minutes for the baked version).
Drain, cool slightly and dust with icing sugar; these little sweet ravioli are made in the Natisone valleys for festivals.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 250 g stale white bread, cut into 1 cm cubes
120 g speck (smoked South Tyrolean ham), finely diced; smoked bacon as substitute
1 small onion, finely chopped, and 20 g butter
steps: Soften the onion in the butter over medium-low heat for 5 minutes, add the speck and fry for 2 minutes; cool slightly.
Beat the eggs with the milk, nutmeg and salt and pour over the bread; add the onion and speck and herbs, mix and leave for 20 minutes to soak.
Sprinkle in the flour and knead lightly until the mixture holds together; with wet hands roll into 8 balls about 6 cm across.
Bring salted water to a gentle simmer and poach the canederli for 15 minutes until they rise and are cooked through (do a test one first).
Serve two per bowl in very hot broth with chives scattered over (cooking them in separate water keeps the broth clear).
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 150 g rye flour and 150 g plain flour
150 ml warm water and 1 tbsp sunflower oil
40 g Parmesan-style hard cheese, grated, plus extra to serve
steps: Knead the rye and wheat flours with the warm water, oil and a pinch of salt into a smooth, firm dough; wrap and rest for 30 minutes.
Blanch the spinach for 2 minutes, squeeze very dry and chop; soften the onion in 20 g butter for 5 minutes and mix both with the quark, cheese, nutmeg and salt.
Roll the dough thin, cut 7 cm rounds, put a teaspoon of filling on each, fold into half-moons and press the edges firmly to seal.
Cook in gently boiling salted water for 4–5 minutes until they float and the dough is tender.
Drain and serve with the remaining butter melted until nut-brown, grated cheese and chives.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g stale white bread, crusts removed, diced
60 g Trentingrana or Grana Padano, grated
steps: Soak the bread in the milk for 20 minutes, then squeeze it lightly.
Blanch the spinach for 2 minutes, squeeze very dry and chop finely.
Mix the bread, spinach, eggs, flour, half the cheese, nutmeg and salt into a soft dough; shape into small oval dumplings with two spoons or floured hands.
Cook in gently boiling salted water for 3–4 minutes until they float and then 1 minute more.
Lift out with a slotted spoon and serve with butter melted with sage until nutty and the remaining cheese.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Blanch the spinach for 2 minutes, squeeze dry and blend with the eggs and water until smooth and bright green.
Beat the purée with the flour, nutmeg and salt for 3 minutes into a thick, sticky batter that drops slowly from a spoon; rest for 10 minutes.
Press the batter through a spätzle grater (Spätzlehobel) or a large-holed colander into a pot of boiling salted water; cook 2 minutes until the little dumplings float, then lift them out.
Soften the shallot in the butter for 3 minutes, add the cream and simmer 2 minutes until slightly thick.
Toss the spätzle in the sauce over medium heat for 1 minute and serve with grated cheese.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 250 g pearl barley, rinsed and soaked for a few hours or overnight
150 g speck or smoked pork rib, diced
1 onion, 1 carrot, 1 celery stalk and 1 leek, finely diced
steps: Melt the butter in a heavy pot over medium-low heat and soften the onion, carrot, celery and leek with the speck for 10 minutes.
Add the drained barley, potatoes, bay leaf and water and bring to the boil.
Simmer gently, partly covered, for 1.5–2 hours, stirring from time to time, until the barley is soft and the soup creamy and thick.
Season, stir in the parsley and serve hot, with a little grated cheese or a thread of oil if you like.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 800 g waxy potatoes, boiled in their skins the day before, peeled and sliced
400 g leftover boiled or roast beef (or pork), cut into strips
steps: Heat the lard in a large cast-iron pan over medium-high heat and fry the potatoes for 10–12 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden and crisp.
Add the onion and fry for 5 minutes until golden, then add the meat and fry for 5 minutes more until heated through and crisp at the edges.
Season with caraway, marjoram, salt and pepper.
Fry the eggs sunny-side up in a separate pan for 3–4 minutes until the whites are set.
Serve the gröstl in the pan topped with fried eggs and chives, with a side of cabbage salad with caraway.

ingredients: 1 kg lean beef topside or rump, in one piece, trimmed of all fat
2 garlic cloves, sliced, and 1 sprig rosemary
steps: Rub the beef all over with the salt, pepper, crushed juniper, bay, garlic and rosemary and pack it tightly in a non-reactive container (traditionally a small wooden tub) with a weight on top.
Refrigerate at 2–4 °C for 10–14 days, turning it every two days in the brine it releases, until it is firm and deep red throughout.
Rinse off the spices, pat dry and slice it as thinly as possible.
Serve raw like carpaccio with oil, lemon and rocket, or, as is more common in Trentino, sear the slices in a hot pan for 30 seconds per side and serve warm with boiled borlotti beans and polenta.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Grate the potatoes coarsely, put them in a cloth and squeeze out as much liquid as possible.
Mix with the onion, flour, salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat and spread spoonfuls of the mixture into thin rounds about 1 cm thick.
Fry for 4–5 minutes per side until crisp and deep golden; drain on paper.
Serve hot with cured meats, mushrooms, cabbage salad or a wedge of Puzzone di Moena cheese, as in the Trentino valleys.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 150 g rye flour and 150 g plain flour
150 ml lukewarm milk, 1 tbsp butter and 1 pinch salt for the dough
300 g spinach, blanched, squeezed dry and chopped
1 small onion, finely chopped and softened in butter
steps: Knead the two flours with the milk, butter and salt for 5 minutes into a smooth, firm dough; cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Mix the spinach, quark, onion, chives, nutmeg and salt into a filling (sauerkraut with caraway is the other classic filling).
Roll the dough very thin, cut into 12 cm rounds, spread filling on half of them, cover with the others and press the edges firmly to seal.
Fry in oil heated to 175 °C for 2–3 minutes per side until puffed with golden bubbles.
Drain on paper and serve warm, often with soup or a glass of new wine at Törggelen time.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g luganega or fresh pork sausage, sliced
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C and grease a 25 x 30 cm baking tin with a little lard.
Whisk the buckwheat flour, cornmeal, milk, salt and pepper into a smooth, pourable batter; stir in the onion and speck.
Pour the batter into the tin and arrange the sausage slices and the remaining lard on top.
Bake for 45–50 minutes until set, crusty and golden on top and the sausage is cooked through.
Cut into squares and serve warm; "smacafam" means "hunger-smasher", a Carnival dish from Trentino.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g rye flour and 100 g plain flour
15 g fresh yeast (or 5 g instant dry yeast) and 100 g rye sourdough (optional)
1 tsp fennel seeds, 1 tsp caraway seeds and 1 tsp fenugreek (or bread clover, Brotklee)
steps: Dissolve the yeast in the water and mix with the flours, sourdough, salt and spices into a soft, sticky dough; cover and let rise for 1 hour.
Divide into 12 pieces, put them on lined trays and let them rest for 15 minutes.
Flatten each piece by shaking the tray back and forth until it spreads into a thin disc about 20 cm across ("schütteln" means to shake), or press flat with wet hands.
Let rise for 30 minutes, then bake at 230 °C for 20–25 minutes until crisp.
Cool on a rack and leave to dry for a day; the crisp flatbread keeps for months and is broken by hand to eat with speck and cheese.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 350 g rye flour and 150 g plain flour
150 g rye sourdough starter (or 15 g fresh yeast)
1 tsp fennel seeds, 1 tsp caraway seeds and 1/2 tsp fenugreek (bread clover)
steps: Mix the flours, water, sourdough (or yeast), salt and lightly crushed spices into a sticky dough and knead for 5 minutes with wet hands.
Cover and leave to rise in a warm place for 2 hours (1 hour if using yeast) until risen and cracked.
Divide into 8 pieces and shape into balls, then put them in pairs, touching, on a lined tray, flatten slightly and dust with rye flour.
Let rise for 30–40 minutes until cracks appear on the surface.
Bake at 230 °C with a tray of water in the oven for 20–25 minutes until the crust is hard and the bottoms sound hollow; serve with speck, butter and cheese.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 250 g plain flour, 120 ml lukewarm water, 3 tbsp sunflower oil and 1 pinch salt for the dough
1 kg tart apples (Renetta or Golden), peeled, cored and thinly sliced
60 g raisins, soaked in 2 tbsp rum
80 g breadcrumbs, toasted in 50 g butter
grated zest and juice of 1 lemon
steps: Knead the flour, water, oil and salt for 10 minutes into a very smooth, elastic, egg-free dough; brush with oil, cover and rest at room temperature for 30 minutes.
Mix the apples with the lemon juice and zest, sugar, cinnamon, drained raisins and pine nuts.
On a floured cloth roll and then stretch the dough with the backs of your hands until it is thin enough to read through and about 50 x 70 cm; trim the thick edges and brush with melted butter.
Spread the buttered crumbs over two-thirds of the dough, top with the apples, then use the cloth to roll it up and slide it onto a lined tray, seam down; brush with butter.
Bake at 190 °C for 40–45 minutes until golden and crisp; cool slightly, dust with icing sugar and serve warm, with vanilla sauce or whipped cream.
