ingredients: 2 tbsp sugar plus 2 tbsp for caramelising
1 pinch salt and 1 tsp vanilla sugar
40 g raisins, soaked in 1 tbsp rum (optional)
200 g cranberry (Preiselbeeren) jam or plum compote, to serve
steps: Whisk the yolks with the milk, flour, vanilla sugar and salt into a smooth batter.
Beat the whites with 2 tbsp sugar to stiff peaks and fold them gently into the batter.

Melt half the butter in a large ovenproof pan over medium heat, pour in the batter, scatter over the raisins and cook for 4–5 minutes until set and golden underneath (or finish in a 200 °C oven for 6 minutes).
Flip in sections, then tear the pancake into bite-size pieces with two forks; add the remaining butter and sugar and toss for 2–3 minutes until lightly caramelised.
Dust with icing sugar and serve hot with cranberry jam or plum compote.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 20 g fresh yeast (or 7 g instant dry yeast)
1 tbsp rum, grated zest of 1 lemon and 1/2 tsp salt
1.5 l sunflower oil for frying, and icing sugar
steps: Dissolve the yeast in the milk with 1 tsp sugar, then knead with the flour, sugar, eggs, yolks, rum, zest and salt for 10 minutes, adding the butter gradually until the dough is smooth and elastic.
Cover and leave to rise in a warm place for 1.5 hours until doubled.
Roll out 1.5 cm thick, cut into 8 cm rounds, place on a floured cloth, cover and let rise for 40 minutes.
Fry in oil at 165–170 °C for 3 minutes per side, covered for the first side so a pale ring forms around the middle, until deep golden and cooked through.
Drain, cool slightly, pipe apricot jam into the side of each krapfen and dust with icing sugar.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 20 g fresh yeast (or 7 g instant dry yeast)
1/2 tsp salt and grated zest of 1 lemon
1.5 l sunflower oil for frying, and icing sugar
steps: Dissolve the yeast in the milk, then knead with the flour, sugar, eggs, butter, zest and salt for 10 minutes into a soft, elastic dough; let rise for 1.5 hours until doubled.
Divide into 12 balls, cover and rest for 20 minutes.
Stretch each ball over your knee or fingertips into a round with a very thin, almost transparent centre and a thick rim ("knee pastries").
Fry in oil at 170 °C for 2 minutes per side until golden, keeping the thin centre pale.
Drain, fill the hollow with a spoon of jam and dust with icing sugar; serve warm.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Whisk the flour, eggs, milk, grappa, sugar and salt into a smooth, thick pouring batter, like a pancake batter.
Heat the oil in a wide pan to 175 °C.
Pour the batter through a funnel (or a piping bag) into the oil in a spiral, moving in circles to form a lacy nest about 15 cm across.
Fry for 1–2 minutes per side until golden and crisp; drain on paper.
Dust with icing sugar and serve warm with cranberry jam, as at South Tyrolean mountain huts and festivals.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 150 g raisins and 100 g dried dates or prunes, chopped
150 g walnuts, 50 g almonds and 50 g pine nuts
100 g candied citron and orange peel, chopped
100 ml grappa or rum, and 100 ml water
300 g rye flour and 100 g plain flour
1 tsp cinnamon, 1/2 tsp ground cloves and 1 tsp baking powder (or 10 g yeast)
blanched almonds and candied cherries, to decorate
steps: Mix the dried fruit, nuts and peel with the grappa and water, cover and leave overnight to soak.
Beat the eggs with the sugar and melted butter, then mix in the flours, spices and baking powder with the soaked fruit and its liquid to make a dense, sticky dough.
Shape into two flat loaves about 3 cm thick on a lined tray (or press into tins), and decorate the tops with almonds and cherries.
Bake at 170 °C for 50–60 minutes until firm and a skewer comes out clean.
Cool completely and wrap; this Christmas fruit bread of Trentino and South Tyrol improves after a few days and is served in thin slices.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Bring the milk with the salt to a gentle boil in a heavy pan.
Rain in the cornmeal (and flour if using) while whisking to prevent lumps.
Cook over low heat for 20–25 minutes, stirring often, until thick and creamy like a soft porridge.
Meanwhile melt the butter in a small pan until golden brown.
Spoon the mosa into bowls, pour the browned butter over and sprinkle with sugar and cinnamon; this simple milk-and-cornmeal dish is a mountain breakfast and supper.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g plain or semolina flour and 200 ml water for the pasta (or 400 g dried strangozzi)
40 g fresh black truffle from Norcia (tartufo nero), or 2 tbsp preserved truffle paste
6 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil (Umbrian if possible)
steps: Knead the flour and water for 10 minutes into a firm dough, rest it 20 minutes, roll it 2 mm thick and cut into thick square-section strips like bootlaces.
Warm the oil with the garlic over very low heat for 3 minutes, then remove the garlic.
Grate three quarters of the truffle into the warm oil off the heat and let it infuse.
Boil the strangozzi in salted water for 4 to 5 minutes (10 to 12 for dried) until al dente, drain, toss with the truffle oil and a splash of pasta water, and shave the remaining truffle on top.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g mixed minced beef and pork
200 g chicken livers and giblets, chopped
1 onion, 1 carrot and 1 celery stick, finely diced
100 ml dry white wine and 400 g tomato passata
3 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil and 30 g butter
1 pinch nutmeg and cloves, 1 tsp salt
steps: Soften the vegetables in the oil and butter for 10 minutes, then brown the minced meat over medium-high heat for 10 minutes.
Add the wine and let it evaporate, then the passata, spices and salt; simmer covered on low for 1.5 hours, adding the chopped livers for the last 20 minutes until cooked through.
Boil the pasta sheets for 1 minute, cool in water and dry on cloths.
Layer pasta, ragù, béchamel and Parmigiano in a buttered dish at least 6 layers deep, finishing with béchamel and cheese.
Bake at 190 C for 40 minutes until bubbling and golden, then rest 15 minutes before slicing.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 3 large eggs (no water, as in Campofilone)
300 g passata or a light meat ragù
steps: Knead the flour and eggs for 10 minutes into a very firm dough and rest it 30 minutes wrapped.
Roll the dough paper-thin (under 1 mm), let it dry 10 minutes, roll it up and cut into very fine threads; spread them out to dry for 20 minutes (good dried egg angel-hair is a substitute).
Soften the onion in the oil for 5 minutes, add the passata or ragù and simmer 10 minutes.
Cook the maccheroncini in boiling salted water for 1 to 2 minutes only, drain gently and toss with the sauce and Parmigiano.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 100 g dried borlotti or cannellini beans, soaked overnight
100 g cicerchia (grass peas), soaked overnight, or dried split fava beans
1 onion, 1 carrot and 1 celery stick, diced
steps: Drain the soaked pulses and simmer the chickpeas, beans and cicerchia in 2.5 litres of fresh water for 1 hour.
Soften the onion, carrot and celery in 4 tbsp oil for 10 minutes, then add the tomatoes and cook 5 minutes.
Add the vegetables, lentils and farro to the pot, season, and simmer 45 minutes until all pulses are tender.
Serve hot with toasted bread and a drizzle of raw olive oil.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.5 kg mixed Adriatic fish and seafood (scorpion fish, gurnard, monkfish, squid, cuttlefish, mantis shrimp, mussels), cleaned
steps: Soften the onion and garlic in the oil over medium heat for 6 minutes, add the squid and cuttlefish and cook 10 minutes.
Add the vinegar and let it reduce for 2 minutes, then add the passata, chilli and salt and simmer 10 minutes.
Layer the firm fish first, then the delicate fish and shellfish on top without stirring, add water just to cover, and simmer 15 minutes, shaking the pot, until the fish flakes and mussels open.
Sprinkle with parsley and serve over toasted bread.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g Castelluccio di Norcia lentils (or small green lentils)
1 onion, 1 carrot and 1 celery stick, finely diced
steps: Soften the vegetables, garlic and rosemary in the oil for 10 minutes over medium-low heat, stir in the tomato paste and add the rinsed lentils and water.
Simmer 25 to 30 minutes until the lentils are tender but whole, seasoning at the end.
Meanwhile prick the sausages and brown them in a pan over medium heat for 10 minutes, then nestle them into the lentils and simmer 10 minutes more until cooked through.
Serve hot with crusty bread and a drizzle of olive oil.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 wood pigeons (palombacci) or squab, cleaned, livers reserved
4 black olives, 1 tbsp capers and 2 sage leaves
steps: Season the pigeons inside and out and roast them on a spit or in a 200 C oven for 45 to 60 minutes, basting often, until the juices run clear.
Set a pan underneath (the ghiotta) holding the wine, vinegar, oil, prosciutto, olives, capers, sage, zest and chopped livers to catch the dripping juices.
Simmer the ghiotta sauce on the hob for 15 minutes until the livers are cooked, then blend or chop finely.
Joint the birds, pour the sauce over and serve on toasted bread.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 whole rabbit (about 1.5 kg), boned, liver reserved
2 bunches wild fennel fronds (finocchietto), or dill plus 1 tsp fennel seeds
2 tsp salt and 1 tsp black pepper
steps: Blanch the wild fennel for 2 minutes, squeeze, chop and mix with garlic, chopped liver, salt and pepper.
Lay the boned rabbit flat, line it with pancetta, spread with the fennel filling, roll tightly and tie with string.
Brown in a roasting tin with the oil on the hob, then roast at 180 C for 1.5 hours, adding wine halfway and basting, until the internal temperature reaches 71 C.
Rest 10 minutes, slice and serve with roast potatoes.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg soaked stockfish (stoccafisso, dried cod), skinned and cut in pieces
1 onion, 1 carrot and 1 celery stick, finely diced
3 garlic cloves and 1 handful parsley, chopped
steps: If buying dried stockfish, soak it in cold water in the fridge for 3 to 5 days, changing the water daily, or buy pre-soaked; drain and bone it.
Make a soffritto of onion, carrot, celery, garlic, parsley and anchovies in some of the oil for 10 minutes.
Layer a heavy pan with wooden spoons or a rack, then layers of potatoes, fish, tomato and soffritto, seasoning as you go.
Pour over the wine and remaining oil, cover and simmer very gently for 2.5 to 3 hours, shaking the pan rather than stirring, until the fish is creamy and flakes.
Rest 15 minutes and serve warm.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 24 olive all'Ascolana (stuffed green olives, see that recipe), breaded
200 g crema fritta (set custard cut in cubes)
200 g plain flour and 200 g fine breadcrumbs
1.5 litres olive or sunflower oil for frying
steps: Flatten the lamb chops slightly and season them; cut the custard and vegetables into pieces.
Dredge everything in flour, then beaten egg, then breadcrumbs.
Fry in batches in oil at 175 C: lamb 4 to 5 minutes until cooked through, olives 3 to 4 minutes, custard and vegetables 2 to 3 minutes, until all are golden.
Drain on paper, salt and serve immediately with lemon wedges.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 40 large green olives (Ascolana Tenera, or large Spanish green olives), pitted
150 g minced pork, 100 g minced beef and 50 g minced chicken
1 onion, 1 carrot and 1 celery stick, finely chopped
50 g Parmigiano, grated and 1 pinch nutmeg
150 g plain flour and 200 g fine breadcrumbs
steps: Soften the vegetables in the olive oil for 5 minutes, add the meats and brown 10 minutes, add the wine and cook 20 minutes until fully cooked; cool and mince finely with Parmigiano, nutmeg and 1 egg.
Cut each olive in a spiral around the stone, remove it, fill with the meat mixture and reshape into an olive.
Roll each olive in flour, then beaten egg, then breadcrumbs.
Fry in oil at 175 C for 3 to 4 minutes until golden, drain and serve hot.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 tsp baking soda (or 7 g dried yeast)
200 g sautéed greens or pecorino, to fill
steps: Mix the flour, baking soda, salt, oil and water and knead 10 minutes into a soft smooth dough; rest 30 minutes.
Roll into a disc about 1.5 cm thick and 30 cm wide and prick all over with a fork.
Cook on a preheated testo (stone griddle) or cast-iron pan over medium heat for 6 to 7 minutes per side until speckled and cooked through.
Cut into wedges, split them open and fill with sautéed greens or pecorino.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Whisk the flour, salt, baking soda and sparkling water into a thick, soft batter and rest 15 minutes.
Heat 1 cm of oil in a pan to 175 C.
Spread ladlefuls of batter into thin discs in the oil and fry 2 to 3 minutes per side until golden and puffed.
Drain on paper and eat hot, with cheese or sautéed greens, as in Gubbio.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 200 g prosciutto or sautéed greens, to fill
steps: Knead the flour, egg, water and salt into a smooth dough and rest 20 minutes.
Roll the dough into a thin large rectangle, spread with the lard, sprinkle with pepper, roll up tightly like a rope, then coil into a spiral and rest 30 minutes.
Flatten each coiled piece into a 20 cm disc about 5 mm thick.
Cook on a hot dry griddle or heavy pan over medium heat for 4 to 5 minutes per side until flaky and spotted gold, then fill with prosciutto or greens.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 100 g pecorino, grated, plus 100 g pecorino, cubed
1 tsp salt and 1 tsp black pepper
steps: Dissolve the yeast in the milk with 100 g flour and let it bubble for 30 minutes.
Beat the eggs with the cheeses, oil, salt and pepper, add to the starter with the remaining flour and knead 15 minutes into a soft sticky dough, then mix in the cheese cubes.
Put into a tall oiled panettone mould only half full and let rise in a warm place for 4 to 8 hours until it reaches the rim.
Bake at 180 C for 50 to 60 minutes until deep golden and a skewer comes out clean; serve at Easter breakfast with salami and boiled eggs.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g plain flour, 80 ml extra-virgin olive oil, 100 ml white wine and 1 pinch salt for the pastry
40 g dried figs and prunes, chopped
3 tbsp Alchermes liqueur (or cherry brandy) and 2 tbsp icing sugar
steps: Knead the flour, oil, wine and salt into a smooth elastic dough and rest 20 minutes.
Mix the apples, nuts, raisins, figs, prunes, sugar and cinnamon.
Roll the dough paper-thin into a rectangle, spread with the filling, roll up and curl into a spiral on a lined tray.
Brush with Alchermes for its red colour and bake at 180 C for 35 to 40 minutes until golden; dust with icing sugar.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g dried figs, chopped and soaked overnight
150 g walnuts and 100 g almonds, chopped
50 g dark chocolate or cocoa, chopped
100 ml cooled espresso and 50 ml mistrà or anise liqueur
1 tsp cinnamon, grated nutmeg and orange zest
steps: Soak the figs overnight, then simmer them in their water for 10 minutes until soft and mash them.
Mix in the raisins, nuts, chocolate, honey, sugar, coffee, liqueur, spices and zest, then the flour and 3 tbsp oil into a dense dark batter.
Spread 2 cm thick in an oiled tin and brush the top with the remaining oil.
Bake at 170 C for 50 to 60 minutes until firm and dark; cool completely before slicing, as eaten at Christmas in the Marche.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 80 g raisins and 50 g pine nuts
steps: Make a dough with flour, yeast, water, sugar, eggs and fat, knead 10 minutes and let rise 1.5 hours.
Knead in the aniseed, zest, citron, raisins and pine nuts.
Shape into a ring, place on a lined tray and make 5 cuts on top (for the five gates of Perugia); let rise 45 minutes.
Brush with egg and bake at 180 C for 35 to 40 minutes until golden; serve with Vin Santo on 29 January.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 60 ml Alchermes liqueur (or raspberry syrup with red food colouring)
100 g caster sugar for the meringue
steps: Beat the yolks with the sugar until pale, then add the butter, zest, Alchermes, flour and baking powder for a red batter.
Pour into a buttered ring tin and bake at 180 C for 35 minutes until a skewer comes out clean.
Whisk the remaining egg whites with caster sugar to stiff glossy peaks.
Turn out the cake, cover it with the meringue, scatter with sprinkles and bake at 140 C for 15 minutes until the meringue is dry; this is Perugia's Easter cake.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 30 g dark cocoa or melted chocolate (optional, for the dark version)
steps: Cook the sugar and water over medium heat, without stirring, to the soft-ball stage (115 C).
Whisk the egg white to stiff peaks and pour in the hot syrup in a thin stream, beating constantly.
Fold in the pine nuts and lemon zest; for dark pinoccate, fold cocoa into half the mixture.
Spoon small diamonds onto wafer paper, let set for 20 minutes, then trim the paper; serve at Christmas in Perugia.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Mix the almonds, sugar, flour, zest and cinnamon, then work in the butter, rum and egg whites to a soft dough.
Roll into thin ropes and cut into small pieces shaped and pressed like broad beans (fave).
Place on a lined tray and bake at 170 C for 15 to 20 minutes until lightly golden but still soft inside.
Cool and serve for All Souls' Day on 2 November.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 800 g boneless mutton or lamb leg (castrato), with some fat
30 thin wooden skewers, soaked in water 30 minutes
steps: Cut the meat into 1 cm cubes, keeping small pieces of fat, and thread them tightly onto the soaked skewers, alternating lean and fat.
Light a charcoal grill (in Abruzzo a long narrow "fornacella") and let it burn down to very hot embers with no flame.
Lay the skewers in a single row across the grill and cook 2 to 3 minutes per side, brushing with oil using the rosemary sprig, until browned outside and just pink inside (lamb to at least 63 C).
Salt generously right off the grill and serve at once with bread drizzled with olive oil and a glass of Montepulciano d'Abruzzo for adults.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g durum semolina and 00 flour mix (half and half)
30 g grated pecorino, plus extra to serve
steps: Knead the flour with 4 eggs into a firm dough, rest 30 minutes covered, roll into 3 mm sheets and press through a chitarra (string-cut pasta frame) to make square spaghetti; substitute fresh tonnarelli or spaghetti if you have no chitarra.
Mix the mince with 1 egg, pecorino, salt and pepper and roll into tiny pallottine (meatballs) the size of a chickpea.
Soften the onion in olive oil over medium-low heat for 6 minutes, add the passata and a pinch of salt and simmer 30 minutes.
Drop the pallottine into the sauce raw and simmer gently 20 minutes until cooked through.
Boil the pasta in well-salted water 3 to 4 minutes until al dente, drain and toss with the sauce and meatballs; serve with grated pecorino.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 600 g broccoli, cut into small florets
40 g grated pecorino or toasted breadcrumbs
steps: Bring a large pot of well-salted water to the boil and cook the broccoli florets for 5 minutes.
Add the cavatelli to the same pot and cook together until the pasta is al dente and the broccoli very soft, about 10 to 12 minutes for dried pasta.
Meanwhile warm the olive oil over low heat with the garlic and chilli for 2 minutes until fragrant but not browned.
Drain the pasta and broccoli, reserving a cup of water, and toss in the garlic oil over medium heat, crushing some broccoli into a creamy sauce with a splash of water.
Serve with pecorino or toasted breadcrumbs scattered on top.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg chicken pieces (or a boiling hen) for broth
1 tbsp lard or oil, for the pan
steps: Simmer the chicken with the onion, carrot, celery and 2.5 litres salted water for 1 hour 30 minutes, skimming, then strain into a clean pot and keep at a boil.
Whisk the eggs, flour, water, parsley and a pinch of salt into a thin, smooth batter and rest 15 minutes.
Grease a 20 cm pan lightly, pour in a thin layer of batter and cook over medium heat for 1 minute per side to make thin scrippelle (crepes); repeat.
Sprinkle each scrippella with grated cheese and pepper, roll up tightly and place 3 or 4 in each warm bowl.
Ladle the boiling broth over them so they are "mbusse" (soaked) and serve immediately.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 100 g each dried chickpeas, cannellini beans, lentils and split fava beans, soaked overnight
200 g pork rind and pig's trotter, cleaned
100 g prosciutto end or pancetta, diced
500 g mixed spring greens (chard, spinach, endive, wild fennel)
300 g mixed dried pasta shapes plus fresh egg pasta pieces
steps: Soak the dried legumes overnight in separate bowls, then simmer each in fresh water until tender, 1 to 2 hours depending on type, and drain.
Boil the pork rind and trotter in water for 2 hours until soft, then cut into strips and keep some of the stock.
Fry the pancetta in olive oil, add the onion, carrot and celery and cook 10 minutes over medium heat, then add the tomatoes and simmer 15 minutes.
Add the legumes, pork, greens and 2 litres of the cooking liquids and simmer 30 minutes, seasoning with salt and chilli.
Add the mixed pasta, starting with the dried shapes, and cook until all is tender; serve thick and hot, traditionally on 1 May.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.5 kg mixed fish and shellfish (scorpionfish, gurnard, mullet, squid, mantis shrimp, mussels), cleaned
1 dried sweet red pepper or 1 tsp hot chilli flakes
steps: In a wide terracotta pan warm the olive oil with the garlic and chilli over low heat for 2 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and green peppers and cook 10 minutes until saucy.

Lay in the squid and firm whole fish first, without stirring, then the smaller fish and shellfish on top; cover and cook over low heat for 15 to 20 minutes, shaking the pan rather than stirring, until the fish flakes and mussels open.
Scatter with parsley, discard unopened mussels, and serve in the pan with toasted bread.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.5 kg mixed Adriatic fish (cuttlefish, gurnard, scorpionfish, mullet, skate), cleaned
steps: Gently fry the garlic, chilli and green peppers in the olive oil in a wide shallow pan over medium-low heat for 5 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and a pinch of salt and cook 8 minutes until they collapse.
Arrange the cuttlefish at the bottom, then the larger fish and finally the delicate fish on top; add a ladle of water if dry.
Cover and simmer 15 minutes, swirling the pan occasionally, until all fish is opaque and cooked through.
Finish with parsley and serve with bruschetta to soak up the broth.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 12 scrippelle (thin crepes made from 4 eggs, 120 g flour, 300 ml water)
400 g minced beef, rolled into tiny meatballs with 1 egg and 30 g pecorino
1 litre meat ragù (beef and pork simmered in tomato sauce)
300 g scamorza or fior di latte, diced
2 tbsp olive oil, for frying and greasing
steps: Make the ragù ahead and simmer it 1 hour 30 minutes; fry the tiny meatballs in oil for 5 minutes until browned and cooked through.
Cook thin scrippelle in a lightly greased pan, 1 minute per side.
Grease a deep baking dish, line the bottom with scrippelle and spread with ragù, meatballs, spinach, scamorza, egg slices and Parmigiano.
Repeat the layers, finishing with scrippelle, ragù and Parmigiano.
Bake at 180 C for 45 minutes until bubbling and set, rest 20 minutes and cut into squares.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 kg mature mutton on the bone, cut into large pieces
steps: Rinse the mutton, place it in a large pot (a copper "cottora" is traditional) and cover with cold water; bring to the boil and skim off the foam for 10 minutes.
Add the onions, celery, tomatoes, chillies, herbs and salt.
Simmer very gently, partly covered, for 3 to 4 hours, topping up with hot water, until the meat falls from the bone.
Serve the meat with its broth and plenty of bread, as at shepherd festivals.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg lamb shoulder or leg on the bone, cut into pieces
steps: Brown the lamb in olive oil with the garlic and rosemary in a heavy pan over medium-high heat for 10 minutes.
Pour in the wine, let it evaporate, then season, cover and cook over low heat for 45 minutes, adding splashes of water, until tender.
Beat the eggs with the pecorino, lemon juice and pepper.
Take the pan off the heat, pour in the egg mixture and stir constantly for 1 to 2 minutes so it sets into a creamy coating without scrambling; serve hot.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 600 g lamb offal (lungs, heart, liver), cleaned
1 kg large chard or romaine lettuce leaves
300 g lamb intestines (budelline) or kitchen string, for tying
1 bunch parsley and 2 garlic cloves, chopped
steps: Blanch the chard or lettuce leaves 30 seconds and spread them flat on a cloth.
Cut the offal into strips, season with garlic, parsley, chilli and salt, and wrap a small bundle tightly in each leaf.
Tie each parcel with cleaned lamb intestine (traditional) or kitchen string.
Brown the parcels in olive oil over medium heat for 5 minutes, add the wine and a little water, cover and cook gently for 50 minutes until the offal is fully cooked; serve hot with bread.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 250 g grated pecorino and caciotta mix
150 g stale bread, crusts removed, soaked in milk and squeezed
1 garlic clove and 1 tbsp parsley, minced
Vegetable or olive oil, for frying
steps: Mix the cheese, eggs, bread, garlic and parsley into a soft, mouldable dough; rest 10 minutes.
Shape into walnut-sized balls and shallow-fry in hot oil at 170 C for 3 to 4 minutes until golden; drain.
Simmer the passata with olive oil, basil and salt for 15 minutes.
Slide the pallotte into the sauce and simmer gently 10 minutes so they absorb it; serve warm with bread.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg pork loin or shoulder, cut into thick slices
steps: Rub the pork thoroughly with salt, garlic, paprika and chilli so it is coated red, then cover and refrigerate overnight.
Lay the slices in an oiled terracotta baking dish and drizzle with olive oil.
Roast at 180 C for 50 to 60 minutes until tender and well cooked, turning once.
Pour the vinegar over in the last 5 minutes and let it sizzle away; serve hot or at room temperature, as in San Salvo.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.5 kg mutton on the bone, cut into large pieces
steps: Rinse the mutton and put it in a large pot with cold water to cover; bring to the boil and skim.
Add the onions, celery, tomatoes, chilli, herbs and salt and simmer gently for 2 hours 30 minutes.
Add the potatoes for the last 30 minutes and cook until the meat is falling-tender.
Serve the meat in deep bowls with broth and bread, the Molisan shepherds' feast dish.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Mix the flour and salt, then add the olive oil and wine and knead into a smooth, firm dough with no yeast, adding water only if needed.
Press into an oiled 30 cm round tin to about 2 cm thick.
Score the top deeply into a diamond grid with a knife.
Bake at 200 C for 30 to 35 minutes until golden; serve warm with cured meats, cheese or greens.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 6 egg yolks and 150 g sugar, for the custard
150 ml alchermes liqueur mixed with 150 ml water (or sweetened coffee)
steps: Whisk the eggs and sugar for 10 minutes until pale and tripled, fold in the flour and bake in a 24 cm tin at 170 C for 35 to 40 minutes; cool and slice into three discs.
Cook the milk, yolks, sugar and cornstarch over medium heat, whisking, until thick, 6 to 8 minutes; divide in half and stir the chocolate into one half.
Brush each disc with the alchermes syrup.
Layer sponge, plain custard, sponge, chocolate custard, and the last sponge; cover with remaining custard and almonds.
Chill at least 3 hours before slicing.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 200 g blanched almonds plus 6 bitter almonds (or 1/4 tsp almond extract)
200 g dark chocolate, for the glaze
steps: Grind the almonds with 2 tbsp of the sugar to a fine flour.
Beat the yolks with the remaining sugar until pale, then mix in the almond flour, semolina, starch and lemon zest; fold in the egg whites whisked to stiff peaks.
Pour into a buttered dome-shaped mould and bake at 170 C for 40 minutes until a skewer comes out clean.
Cool, unmould and coat with melted dark chocolate, which imitates the burnt crust of the shepherds' bread it is named after.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 120 ml extra-virgin olive oil or 150 g butter
300 g grape jam (scrucchiata) or chocolate-almond filling
steps: Mix the flour, sugar, baking powder and zest, then add the eggs and oil and knead briefly into a soft shortcrust.
Roll out to 3 mm and line small fluted tartlet moulds.
Fill each with a spoonful of grape jam, or with a mix of chocolate, ground almonds and cinnamon, and cover with a pastry lid, sealing the edges.
Bake at 180 C for 20 to 25 minutes until golden, cool and dust with icing sugar.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 100 ml extra-virgin olive oil or melted butter
1 tsp anise seeds or grated lemon zest
steps: Beat the eggs and sugar until smooth, then mix in the oil and anise.
Stir in the flour and baking powder to a thick, spoonable batter.
Heat a pizzelle iron (ferratelle press) over the flame or electrically and grease lightly.
Place a tablespoon of batter in the centre, close and cook 30 to 60 seconds each until pale gold; cool flat on a rack so they crisp.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 50 g toasted almonds and coloured sprinkles
steps: Knead the flour, eggs, olive oil, sugar and zest into a smooth dough and rest 20 minutes.
Roll into thin ropes and cut into chickpea-sized pieces (cicerchie).
Deep-fry in batches at 175 C for 2 to 3 minutes until golden, then drain.
Warm the honey in a wide pan until fluid, tip in the fried balls and almonds and stir to coat.
Shape into a ring on a wet plate, decorate with sprinkles and let set before serving at Carnival.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil and 3 tbsp white wine
400 g fresh semi-aged pecorino or caciotta, grated
steps: Knead the flour, 3 eggs, oil and wine into a smooth dough and rest 20 minutes.
Mix the grated cheese with 6 eggs and pepper into a thick filling.
Roll the dough thin, cut into 12 cm rounds, spoon filling on one half and fold into half-moons, pressing the edges; cut a small slit on top so the filling puffs.
Brush with yolk and bake at 190 C for 25 to 30 minutes until golden; serve at Easter.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 80 ml extra-virgin olive oil and 100 ml white wine
300 g boiled chestnuts or cooked chickpeas, mashed
steps: Knead the flour, eggs, olive oil and wine into a smooth dough and rest 30 minutes.
Mix the chestnuts or chickpeas with almonds, chocolate, honey and cinnamon into a thick filling.
Roll the dough thin, place spoonfuls of filling and fold over to make large ravioli, sealing with a fork.
Deep-fry at 175 C for 3 minutes per side until golden; drain and dust with icing sugar, a Molisan Christmas sweet.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Toast the almonds at 150 C for 10 minutes and let them cool.
Boil the sugar, water and glucose to a light syrup (about 105 C) and add the vanilla.

Put the almonds in a large bowl or pan set over low heat and add a spoonful of syrup at a time, tossing continuously so each layer dries before the next; continue 40 to 50 minutes until thickly coated and smooth (Sulmona makers use rotating copper pans).
Spread to dry for several hours, then shape into flowers with ribbon or serve at weddings in five-piece bags.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 bottle Centerbe liqueur, from a licensed producer
steps: Centerbe (also "Centerba") is a strong emerald-green herbal liqueur from Tocco da Casauria in Abruzzo, flavoured with around a hundred mountain herbs; buy it from licensed producers rather than making it at home.
Serve it in small measures, chilled or neat, as a digestif after a heavy meal; it is very high in alcohol, so sip slowly.
Locals also add a few drops to espresso as "caffè corretto" or drizzle it over ice; enjoy responsibly.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Orecchiette con le Cime di Rapa

ingredients: 1 kg cime di rapa (turnip tops; substitute broccoli rabe or rapini)
steps: Trim the cime di rapa, keeping the tender leaves and florets, and wash well.
Boil them in plenty of salted water for 4 minutes, then add the orecchiette and cook together until the pasta is al dente.
Meanwhile warm the olive oil over low heat with the garlic, chilli and anchovies, stirring until the anchovies melt, about 3 minutes.
Drain the pasta and greens, toss in the anchovy oil over medium heat for 1 minute, and serve topped with toasted breadcrumbs.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 ml thin tomato broth (100 g tomato paste dissolved in 500 ml hot salted water)
steps: Warm the passata briefly with a pinch of salt; keep the tomato broth hot in a separate pan.
In a large heavy iron pan, heat the olive oil with the garlic and chilli over medium heat for 1 minute, then add the passata and fry 2 minutes.
Add the raw spaghetti in a single layer and let it sear without stirring until it starts to char, then turn it.
Add tomato broth a ladle at a time, risotto-style, letting each addition evaporate and the pasta crisp and blacken in places, for about 18 minutes until al dente.
Serve straight from the pan, crunchy, smoky and very spicy, as in Bari.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g semolina and 00 flour mix, plus water for the tria
1 onion, 1 celery stalk, 1 carrot, finely chopped
Salt and black pepper, to taste
steps: Simmer the soaked chickpeas with bay leaves, garlic, vegetables and plenty of water for 2 hours until creamy and tender; salt at the end.
Knead the flour with warm water into a firm dough, roll to 2 mm and cut into short ribbons (tria) about 1 cm wide and 8 cm long.
Fry one third of the tria in hot olive oil at 170 C for 2 minutes until golden and crisp; drain.
Boil the remaining tria directly in the chickpea pot for 3 to 4 minutes, adding hot water if too thick.
Serve in bowls topped with the fried tria, a drizzle of olive oil and black pepper.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 80 g cacioricotta, grated (substitute ricotta salata or pecorino)
steps: Knead the semolina with water and a pinch of salt for 10 minutes into a firm dough; rest 30 minutes.
Roll out thinly, cut into ribbons 1.5 cm wide and twist each around itself into long corkscrew spirals; let dry 20 minutes.
Fry the onion in olive oil 5 minutes, add the passata, basil and salt and simmer 30 minutes.
Boil the sagne in salted water 5 to 7 minutes until al dente, toss with the sauce and finish with grated cacioricotta.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg fresh mussels, scrubbed and debearded
800 g waxy potatoes, peeled and thinly sliced
2 garlic cloves and 1 bunch parsley, chopped
steps: Open the mussels raw with a small knife over a bowl to catch their liquid, leaving the meat on the half-shell (or steam them open 2 minutes); strain the liquid.
Oil a deep baking dish (tiella) and layer onions, potatoes, tomatoes, garlic, parsley and pecorino.
Add a layer of mussels on the half-shell, scatter over the raw rice, then repeat the layers, finishing with potatoes, tomatoes and pecorino.
Pour in the mussel liquid plus enough water to just reach the top layer, drizzle with oil.
Bake at 200 C for 50 to 60 minutes until the rice and potatoes are tender and the top is golden; rest 10 minutes before serving.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g dried split peeled fava beans, soaked overnight
1 kg wild chicory or dandelion greens (cicoria; substitute escarole or puntarelle)
1 red onion, thinly sliced (optional, to serve)
steps: Simmer the soaked fava beans with the potato, bay leaf and water to cover in a terracotta pot over low heat for 1 hour 30 minutes, stirring often, until they collapse.
Beat with a wooden spoon and 4 tbsp olive oil into a smooth puree, seasoning with salt.
Boil the chicory in salted water for 8 minutes until tender, drain and toss with olive oil.
Serve the warm puree beside the chicory, drizzled generously with oil, with raw onion and bread on the side.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 8 thin slices beef or horse meat (about 600 g), pounded
60 g pecorino, cut into small sticks
steps: Lay the meat slices flat, season with salt and pepper and top each with pecorino, garlic, parsley and lardo.
Roll up tightly and secure with toothpicks or string.
Brown the braciole in olive oil with the onion over medium heat for 8 minutes, then add the wine and let it evaporate.
Pour in the passata and a cup of water, cover and simmer gently for 2 hours 30 minutes until very tender.
Use the sauce to dress orecchiette as a first course and serve the braciole as the main course.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.2 kg octopus, cleaned (previously frozen is more tender)
steps: Rinse the octopus and cut into large pieces.
Put everything into a terracotta pignata (pot) or heavy casserole without adding water.
Seal the lid with foil or a flour paste and cook over very low heat for 1 hour 30 minutes, letting the octopus stew in its own juices until a fork slides in easily.
Rest 10 minutes, then serve with its juices and crusty bread.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.5 kg large fresh mussels, scrubbed and debearded
2 garlic cloves and 1 bunch parsley, minced
steps: Steam the mussels in a covered pan over high heat for 3 minutes until they just open; discard any that stay closed and keep the strained liquid.
Remove the empty half-shells and arrange the mussels on the half-shell in a baking tray.
Mix the breadcrumbs, pecorino, garlic, parsley, oregano, tomatoes, pepper, oil and 3 tbsp mussel liquid into a moist crumb.
Top each mussel generously, drizzle with oil and bake at 220 C for 10 to 12 minutes until golden and crisp.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg small whole fish (picarel, bogue or anchovies), cleaned
Olive or sunflower oil, for frying
1 tsp saffron threads (zafferano), steeped in 2 tbsp warm water
steps: Dust the fish in flour and fry in hot oil at 180 C for 3 to 4 minutes until crisp and cooked through; drain and salt.
Soak the breadcrumbs in the vinegar with the saffron and its water until they turn yellow and soft.
In a wooden tub or glass dish, alternate layers of fish and saffron breadcrumbs, finishing with breadcrumbs.
Press down, cover and leave in the fridge at least overnight; serve cold in paper cones, as at the fairs of Gallipoli.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g sashimi-grade red prawns (gamberi rossi) or scampi
300 g sashimi-grade sea urchin roe (ricci di mare) or tuna
steps: Buy only sashimi/sushi-grade fish and shellfish from a certified fishmonger on the day, keep everything on ice, and use live oysters with tightly closed shells.
Shuck the oysters, peel the prawns leaving the heads, and cut the cuttlefish into thin ribbons.
Arrange everything on a platter of crushed ice with the sea urchin in its shell.
Serve immediately with lemon wedges, a drizzle of olive oil and a pinch of salt, as on the Bari seafront; skip it if you are pregnant or immunocompromised.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 600 g pork neck (capocollo), cut into thin slices
150 g caciocavallo, cut into small cubes
steps: Pound the pork slices thin, season with salt, pepper and parsley.
Place a cube of caciocavallo and a little pancetta on each slice and roll into a tight parcel the size of a walnut.
Thread 3 or 4 bombette onto each skewer and brush with olive oil.
Cook in a hot oven at 220 C or over embers for 12 to 15 minutes, turning, until the pork is cooked through and the cheese oozes; serve hot as in the butcher-grills of the Valle d'Itria.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 600 g lamb offal (liver, lungs, heart, sweetbreads), cleaned
400 g cleaned lamb intestines (or caul fat as a substitute)
60 g pecorino, cut into small sticks
steps: Cut the offal into small strips and season with parsley, garlic, salt and pepper.
Make small bundles of mixed offal with a stick of pecorino and wrap tightly with the cleaned intestine (or caul fat) into small rolls.
Thread onto skewers, alternating with bay leaves, and brush with olive oil.
Grill over medium embers or roast at 200 C for 25 to 30 minutes, turning, until well browned and cooked through; serve hot.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 200 g tomato pulp, seasoned with salt and oregano
Sunflower or peanut oil, for frying
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar, water and olive oil, add the salt and knead 10 minutes into a soft dough; let rise 1 hour 30 minutes until doubled.
Divide into 12 balls, rest 15 minutes, then roll each into a 15 cm disc.
Place a spoonful of tomato and mozzarella on one half, fold into a half-moon and seal the edges well by pressing and pinching.
Deep-fry at 175 C for 2 to 3 minutes per side until puffed and golden; drain and eat hot.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 100 g cauliflower florets, blanched and chopped (optional)
Olive or sunflower oil, for frying
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, salt and water into a very soft, sticky batter-like dough, beating with your hand for 10 minutes.
Cover and leave to rise in a warm place for 1 hour until bubbly; stir in the cauliflower if using.
Wet two fingers or a spoon and drop walnut-sized pieces of dough into hot oil at 175 C.
Fry 3 to 4 minutes, turning, until golden and puffy; drain and salt, as eaten on 7 December in Salento.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: Peanut or sunflower oil, for frying
steps: Bring the salted water to a boil, whisk in the polenta in a thin stream and cook over low heat for 40 minutes, stirring often, until very thick.
Spread on an oiled tray to 1 cm thick and let cool until firm, about 3 hours.
Cut into rectangles or diamonds.
Deep-fry at 180 C for 4 to 5 minutes until crisp and golden; drain, salt and serve hot in paper, as sold in Bari Vecchia.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 25 g butter and 25 g flour, for the bechamel
150 g tomato pulp, seasoned with salt and pepper
steps: Melt the butter, stir in the flour and cook 1 minute, then whisk in the milk and cook over medium heat for 5 minutes until thick; season with nutmeg and salt and cool.
Cut the pastry into 10 cm fluted rounds.
Put a spoonful of bechamel, a little tomato and some mozzarella on half the rounds, cover with the remaining rounds and seal the edges.
Brush with milk and bake at 200 C for 20 to 25 minutes until puffed and deep golden; serve warm.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 350 g 00 flour and 150 g durum semolina (semola rimacinata)
1 medium potato (150 g), boiled and mashed
300 g cherry tomatoes, halved and squeezed
steps: Mix the flours, mashed potato, yeast and water, add the salt and knead into a very soft dough; let rise 2 hours until doubled.
Pour 5 tbsp olive oil into a 30 cm round tin, tip the dough in and stretch it gently with oiled fingers; rest 30 minutes.
Press the tomatoes and olives into the dough, sprinkle with oregano and salt and drizzle with the remaining oil.
Bake at 250 C on the lowest shelf for 25 to 30 minutes until crisp-bottomed and golden.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 friselle (twice-baked durum wheat or barley rings, bought)
steps: Dip each frisella in cold water (or seawater, as in Salento) for a few seconds until slightly softened but still crunchy.
Rub with garlic if you like.
Crush the tomatoes over the top so the juices soak in, then season with salt, oregano and basil.
Drizzle generously with olive oil and eat immediately.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 150 g black olives, pitted (for olive puccia)
steps: Mix the semolina, yeast, water and oil, add the salt and knead 10 minutes into a smooth dough; work in the olives if using.
Let rise 1 hour 30 minutes until doubled.
Divide into 6 balls, flatten into rounds 2 cm thick and rest 30 minutes.
Bake at 240 C for 20 to 25 minutes until golden and hollow-sounding; split and fill with grilled vegetables and cheese.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg remilled durum semolina (semola rimacinata di grano duro)
steps: Dissolve the starter in the water, add the semolina and knead 15 minutes, then add the salt and knead until smooth and elastic.
Cover and let rise 3 to 4 hours, then fold and shape into the traditional tall folded-over "scuanéte" loaf and prove covered overnight in the fridge or 2 more hours at room temperature.
Bake in a very hot oven at 250 C with a tray of water for 20 minutes, then lower to 200 C and bake 40 more minutes until the thick crust is dark golden.
Cool fully on a rack; the yellow crumb keeps for days.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g 00 flour, 7 g dried yeast, 10 g salt and 300 ml water
1 kg sponsali (long sweet onions) or spring onions, sliced
steps: Knead the flour, yeast, water, 3 tbsp oil and salt into a soft dough and let rise 1 hour 30 minutes.
Stew the onions in 3 tbsp oil over low heat for 25 minutes until soft and sweet, then add the tomatoes, anchovies, olives and capers and cook 5 minutes more; cool and stir in the pecorino.
Divide the dough in two, line an oiled 28 cm tin with half, add the filling and cover with the other half, sealing the edges and pricking the top.
Brush with oil and bake at 200 C for 35 to 40 minutes until deep golden.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 tsp fennel seeds or black pepper
steps: Mix all the ingredients and knead 10 minutes into a smooth, firm dough; rest 20 minutes.
Roll small pieces into pencil-thin ropes 10 cm long and press the ends together into rings.
Drop the rings into boiling water in batches; lift them out as soon as they float and dry on a cloth.
Bake at 190 C for 25 to 30 minutes until crisp and pale golden; cool completely before storing in a jar.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g stale country bread, cut into 2 cm cubes
500 g cime di rapa or chicory, trimmed
250 g cooked chickpeas or fava beans
steps: Boil the greens in salted water for 6 minutes, drain and chop roughly.
Fry the bread cubes in 5 tbsp olive oil over medium heat for 5 minutes until golden and crisp; set aside.
In the same pan warm the remaining oil with garlic and chilli, add the greens and legumes and cook 5 minutes.
Toss in the fried bread just before serving so it stays crunchy, the Salentine "muersi" (bites).
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 tsp baking ammonia or baking powder
500 ml milk, 4 egg yolks, 120 g sugar and 50 g cornstarch, for the custard
steps: Make the custard: heat the milk with lemon zest, whisk the yolks with sugar and cornstarch, combine and cook over medium heat for 5 minutes until thick; cool covered.
Rub the lard into the flour, sugar and baking powder, then add eggs and yolks and knead briefly into a shortcrust; chill 30 minutes.
Line greased oval pasticciotto moulds with pastry, fill with custard and cover with a pastry lid, sealing well.
Brush with beaten egg and bake at 220 C for 20 to 25 minutes until dark golden; eat warm for breakfast in Lecce.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 ml vincotto (cooked grape must; substitute honey)
steps: Knead the flour, warm oil, wine and salt into a smooth, firm dough; rest 30 minutes.
Roll paper-thin, cut into strips 3 cm wide with a fluted wheel, pinch every 3 cm and coil each strip into a rose shape, pressing the pinched points together.
Let them dry for a few hours, then deep-fry at 175 C for 2 to 3 minutes until golden; drain well.
Warm the vincotto with cinnamon, dip each cartellata to fill the pockets, and finish with sprinkles; a Christmas sweet across Puglia.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Cook the milk, yolks, sugar, cornstarch and lemon zest over medium heat, whisking, for 5 to 6 minutes until thick; cool covered.
Cut the puff pastry into 8 cm squares and bake at 200 C for 12 to 15 minutes until puffed and golden.
Split each square in half horizontally and fill with a thick layer of custard.
Dust heavily with icing sugar and serve warm; the name means "dirty mouth" because of the sugar.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 tbsp almond milk syrup (latte di mandorla; substitute orgeat syrup)
steps: Brew a strong espresso.
Put the ice cubes in a short glass and pour in the almond syrup.
Pour the hot espresso over the ice, stir and drink at once, the summer coffee of Lecce.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g durum wheat semolina (semola rimacinata), plus 150 ml warm water for fresh fileja (or 350 g dried fileja)
100 g 'nduja di Spilinga (spicy spreadable pork salume; or chorizo paste)
1 small red onion of Tropea, finely chopped
60 g grated pecorino crotonese or ricotta salata
steps: For fresh fileja, knead semolina and water 10 minutes, rest 30 minutes, then roll thin ropes around a skewer (ferretto) into 10 cm hollow spirals and slide off.
Soften the onion in oil over medium heat 6 minutes, add the 'nduja and stir until it melts into the oil.
Add passata and salt and simmer 15 minutes until thick.
Boil the fileja in salted water 6–8 minutes (fresh) until tender, toss in the sauce with basil, and serve with grated pecorino.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 400 g goat or pork meat (or pork ribs), in pieces
steps: Brown the meat in oil with the onion for 10 minutes, add the wine and let it evaporate.
Add passata, chilli and salt and simmer gently 1 1/2 hours until the meat is tender and the ragù is thick.
Meanwhile knead the semolina and water into a firm dough, rest 30 minutes, then roll small pieces around a ferretto (thin iron rod or skewer) into 8 cm hollow tubes.
Boil the maccheroni 6–8 minutes until tender, dress with the ragù and pecorino, and serve the meat as a second course, Lucanian style.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 350 g struncatura (rough wholewheat linguine from Gioia Tauro; or wholewheat linguine)
steps: Toast the breadcrumbs in a dry pan over medium heat until golden, stirring, and set aside.
Warm the oil with garlic, chilli and anchovies over low heat until the anchovies dissolve; add olives and capers.
Cook the struncatura in lightly salted water until al dente, then toss in the sauce with a splash of cooking water.
Serve sprinkled with the toasted breadcrumbs instead of cheese.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g durum wheat semolina and 150 ml warm water (lagane), or wide dried tagliatelle
2 peperoni cruschi (crisp dried sweet peppers) or 1/2 tsp paprika
steps: Simmer the soaked chickpeas with bay, rosemary and 1 garlic clove in 2 litres of water for 1 1/2–2 hours until tender; salt at the end.
Knead the semolina and water, rest 30 minutes, roll thin and cut into 2 cm wide ribbons (lagane).
Cook the lagane directly in the chickpeas with their broth for 4–5 minutes until tender and the dish is thick and soupy.
Fry the remaining garlic and the crumbled peppers briefly in oil and pour over each bowl; this is the Lucanian "lagane e ciciri".
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

dishes.name: Strascinati con Mollica e Peperoni Cruschi

ingredients: 400 g durum wheat semolina and 200 ml warm water (or 400 g dried cavatelli/orecchiette)
6 peperoni cruschi (Senise dried sweet peppers; or mild dried Hungarian peppers)
steps: Knead semolina and water into a firm dough, rest 30 minutes, cut into small pieces and drag (strascinare) each across a board with two or three fingers into a hollow shell.
Fry the peppers in hot oil for 5–10 seconds per side until crisp and bright red; drain and crumble, keeping the red oil.
Toast the breadcrumbs with the garlic in a little of the pepper oil until golden.
Boil the pasta 5–7 minutes, drain, toss with the pepper oil, breadcrumbs and crumbled peppers, and serve with cheese if liked.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg veal tripe and offal (heart, lung, spleen), cleaned
2 bay leaves and 1 tsp dried oregano
steps: Wash the tripe and offal well, boil 30 minutes in plenty of water, drain and dice.
Brown in oil in a terracotta or heavy pot for 10 minutes, then add tomato paste, passata, chillies, bay, oregano and salt.
Add hot water, cover and simmer 2–2 1/2 hours, stirring occasionally, until very tender and thickly sauced.
Split each pitta, stuff generously with the stew and eat hot, as in the morning street stalls of Catanzaro.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Whisk the lemon juice, oil, garlic, capers, oregano, parsley and salt into a salmoriglio sauce.
Lay the swordfish in an oiled baking dish and spoon over half the sauce.
Bake at 200°C for 10–12 minutes until the fish is opaque and flakes at the centre.
Spoon over the remaining sauce and serve with crusty bread, as in Bagnara Calabra.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 6 peperoni cruschi (Senise dried sweet peppers; or mild dried peppers)
steps: Soak the baccalà 48 hours in cold water in the fridge, changing the water 3 times a day, then cut into pieces.
Poach the cod in barely simmering water 10 minutes until it flakes; drain.
Fry the peppers in hot oil for a few seconds until crisp, remove and crumble; fry the garlic in the same oil.
Arrange cod and potatoes on a platter, pour over the red pepper oil, top with crumbled peppers, olives and parsley, and serve warm.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.2 kg lamb or kid (shoulder and neck), in pieces
steps: Brown the lamb in oil in a heavy pot (traditionally a terracotta pignata) over medium-high heat for 10 minutes.
Add onion, celery, tomatoes, herbs, chilli and salt, and enough water to half cover.
Cover and cook very gently 1 1/2 hours, then add the potatoes and cook 40 minutes more until meat and potatoes are tender.
Serve hot with country bread, a Lucanian shepherds' dish.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg red onions of Tropea, thinly sliced
steps: Gently sweat the onions in oil with salt for 15 minutes until soft and sweet without colouring.
Add potatoes, chilli and stock and simmer 25 minutes until the potatoes are tender.
Toast the bread and place a slice in each bowl.
Ladle the soup over, sprinkle with pecorino and drizzle with oil.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 100 g cicerchia (grass peas) or dried peas
steps: Soak all the legumes (except lentils) and the wheat overnight in separate bowls.
Drain, place in a large pot with garlic and bay, cover with 4 litres of water and simmer 2 hours, skimming.
Add lentils and potatoes and simmer 45 minutes more until everything is tender and creamy.
Season with salt, drizzle with oil and serve hot; it is cooked in Matera on 1 August to celebrate the harvest.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g salted anchovies or whitebait (traditional bianchetti/neonata are now restricted), rinsed and boned
3 tbsp crushed Calabrian chilli (or hot paprika plus chilli flakes)
steps: Rinse and fillet the salted fish, pat dry and chop finely or mash with a fork.
Mix with the chilli, paprika and fennel seeds into a thick red paste.
Pack into a clean jar, cover with olive oil and refrigerate at least 2 days (up to 2 weeks), keeping it under oil.
Spread on toasted bread or crackers as an antipasto; this is "Calabrian caviar".
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 150 g stale bread, soaked in water and squeezed
2 tbsp chopped parsley and 6 basil leaves
1/2 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp black pepper
500 ml sunflower or olive oil, for frying
steps: Peel and dice the aubergines and boil 10 minutes until soft; drain and squeeze out all the water.
Mash with the bread, eggs, pecorino, garlic, herbs, salt and pepper, adding breadcrumbs until firm.
Shape into walnut-sized balls and roll in breadcrumbs.
Fry at 170°C for 3–4 minutes until deep golden; serve warm or with tomato sauce.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 500 g floury potatoes, boiled and riced
10 g fresh yeast (or 4 g instant yeast)
1 l sunflower or olive oil, for frying
steps: Mix flour, potato, yeast, water and salt into a very soft, sticky dough and let rise 1 1/2 hours until doubled.
Heat the oil to 175°C.
With oiled hands, stretch a piece of dough into a 12 cm finger, wrap it around a piece of anchovy and drop into the oil.
Fry 3–4 minutes, turning, until golden and puffed; drain and serve hot, a Calabrian Christmas Eve treat.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Fry the potatoes, aubergines and peppers separately in oil in batches until golden and tender; drain.
Soften the onion in the same pan, add the tomatoes and salt and cook 10 minutes.
Return all the vegetables with the courgettes and simmer 15 minutes until melded.
Add basil and serve warm or at room temperature with bread.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 12 dried peperoni di Senise (mild dried sweet peppers; or dried ancho/Hungarian peppers)
steps: Wipe the peppers with a damp cloth, cut off the stems and shake out the seeds; dry well.
Heat the oil to about 170°C in a small pan.
Fry the peppers one or two at a time for 5–10 seconds, just until they puff and turn bright red; do not let them darken or they turn bitter.
Drain on paper, salt lightly and eat as a crunchy snack or crumble over pasta and baccalà.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 kg potatoes (Sila potatoes if possible), thinly sliced
steps: Heat the oil in a wide cast-iron pan over medium-high heat and add the potatoes in an even layer.
Cook 10 minutes without stirring until a sticky golden crust forms on the base, then turn in sections.
Add the onions, peppers, salt and chilli and cook 15 minutes more, turning occasionally, until tender and caramelised; the potatoes should stick together ("mpacchiuse").
Serve hot as a side.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 150 g fresh horseradish root (rafano), peeled and finely grated
1/2 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp black pepper
steps: Beat the eggs with the horseradish, pecorino, breadcrumbs, parsley, salt and pepper into a thick batter.
Heat the oil in a 24 cm ovenproof frying pan, pour in the mixture and cook on low 8–10 minutes until the base is set.
Transfer to an oven at 180°C for 15–20 minutes until puffed, golden and set through.
Serve warm or cold in wedges; it is the Lucanian Carnival frittata ("poor man's truffle").
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

steps: Mix semolina, starter and most of the water, rest 30 minutes, then add salt and remaining water and knead 15 minutes until smooth and strong.
Leave to rise 4–6 hours until doubled, then shape into the traditional high "cornetto" loaf by folding and cutting three notches across the top.
Cover and proof 2–3 hours until puffy (or overnight in the fridge).
Bake at 240°C with steam for 20 minutes, then at 200°C for 40 minutes until the crust is dark and hollow-sounding; cool completely before slicing.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 150 ml sweet white wine (Moscato) plus 100 ml warm water
300 g raisins, soaked in a little brandy
2 tsp cinnamon and 1/2 tsp ground cloves
steps: Knead the flour, oil, wine, water and zest into a smooth dough and rest 30 minutes.
Mix the walnuts, raisins, almonds, spices, orange juice and half the honey.
Roll the dough thin, cut into 6 cm strips, spread filling along each and roll up loosely into rosettes; pack the rosettes side by side in an oiled 26 cm tin.
Bake at 180°C for 40–45 minutes until golden, then brush with the remaining warm honey; a Christmas sweet from San Giovanni in Fiore.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g honey (or fig syrup, vino cotto di fichi)
1/2 tsp baking ammonia or baking powder
1 tbsp olive oil, for the tray
steps: Warm the honey with the water until fluid, then mix with flour, anise, zest and raising agent into a firm dough.
Rest 30 minutes, roll 1 cm thick and cut into figures (fish, hearts, horses, dolls), decorating with pressed patterns and whole almonds.
Bake on an oiled tray at 180°C for 15–20 minutes until firm and golden brown.
Cool; they are hard, keep for months and are sold at Soriano and village fairs.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 3 eggs for the dough, plus 1 beaten for glazing
12 g fresh yeast (or 5 g instant yeast)
1 lemon, zested and 1/2 tsp ground anise
steps: Knead flour, eggs, sugar, milk, yeast, zest and anise, then work in the butter until smooth; let rise 2 hours.
Shape into braids, rings or dolls, and press a raw egg in its shell into each, holding it with a cross of dough.
Rise 1 hour, glaze with beaten egg and sprinkle with coloured sprinkles if liked.
Bake at 180°C for 30–35 minutes until golden (the eggs bake hard through); a Calabrian Easter bread.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 100 g dark chocolate, melted (for the core)
steps: Soften the hazelnut gelato slightly; line 6 cups with cling film and press in a layer to make half-spheres, then freeze 1 hour.
Fill the centre with a spoon of melted chocolate and a little chocolate gelato, then cover with more hazelnut gelato to close into a ball; freeze 3–4 hours until hard.
Mix the cocoa and sugar, unwrap each ball and roll it in the cocoa sugar.
Serve straight from the freezer; the original is from Pizzo Calabro.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 suckling pig (porceddu), 5-6 kg, split and cleaned
2 tbsp pork lard or olive oil
steps: Light a wood fire with juniper, olive or holm-oak wood and let it burn down to strong embers; alternatively heat the oven to 160 C.
Skewer the pig lengthwise, rub with lard and set it vertically or at an angle near (not over) the embers, skin side away at first.
Roast slowly for 3.5-4 hours, turning, salting the skin halfway and basting with lard, until the skin crackles and the meat reaches at least 70 C at the thickest part.
Lay the hot pig on a bed of myrtle branches, cover with more myrtle and rest 20 minutes so it takes the scent.
Cut into pieces and serve on cork boards with pane carasau.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 kg mutton (pecora), on the bone, cut in large pieces
steps: Put the mutton in a large pot of cold water, bring to a simmer and skim off the foam.
Add onions, carrots, celery, tomatoes, parsley and salt and simmer gently for 2.5 hours until the meat is very tender.
Add the potatoes for the last 30 minutes and cook until soft.
Serve the meat and vegetables on a platter; use the broth to moisten pane carasau or cook pasta.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1.2 kg lamb shoulder or leg on the bone, cut in pieces
500 g wild fennel (finocchietto selvatico), stalks and fronds (substitute: 2 fennel bulbs with fronds plus 1 tsp fennel seed)
2 tbsp tomato paste or 3 ripe tomatoes, chopped
125 ml Vermentino or other dry white wine
steps: Blanch the wild fennel in salted water for 5 minutes, drain and chop roughly.
Brown the lamb in oil over medium-high heat for 10 minutes, add onion and garlic and cook 5 minutes.
Pour in the wine and let it evaporate, add tomato and a glass of water, cover and simmer 45 minutes.
Add the fennel and cook 15 minutes more until the lamb is tender and cooked through; serve hot.

ingredients: 1 kg dogfish or small shark (gattuccio) steaks (substitute: monkfish)
steps: Poach the fish in salted water with the bay leaf for 12-15 minutes until fully cooked; drain, skin and cut in pieces.
Fry the garlic in the oil for 1 minute, add walnuts and vinegar and simmer 3 minutes.
Layer the fish in a glass or earthenware dish and pour the hot marinade over it.
Cool, cover and refrigerate overnight; serve cold with parsley.

ingredients: 2 live spiny lobsters (aragosta), about 800 g each
steps: Chill the lobsters in the freezer 20 minutes to stun them, then plunge into a large pot of boiling salted water and cook 12-15 minutes until bright red and the flesh is opaque.
Cool, split, remove the meat and cut into medallions; keep any coral.
Toss tomatoes, onion and celery in a bowl with oil, lemon, salt and pepper.
Add the lobster and its juices, mix gently and serve at room temperature, as in Alghero.

ingredients: 1 kg lamb intestines (cordula), cleaned by the butcher
2 tbsp tomato paste or 3 tomatoes, chopped
steps: Rinse the intestines repeatedly in salted water, then braid three strands together into long plaits and parboil 10 minutes.
Brown the plaits in oil over medium heat for 10 minutes, add the onion and cook 5 minutes.
Add tomato, peas and a little water, cover and simmer 40 minutes until fully cooked and tender (or grill them over embers for 25 minutes).
Season and serve hot with parsley.

ingredients: 100 g lard (strutto) and 250 ml warm water
500 g lamb or pork, cut in small dice
300 g potatoes, diced (or peas or artichokes)
2 garlic cloves and 2 tbsp parsley, chopped
1 tsp sun-dried tomato paste or saffron (optional)
steps: Knead semolina, lard, water and salt into a smooth firm dough; rest 30 minutes.
Mix the raw meat with potatoes, garlic, parsley, oil, salt and pepper.
Roll out the dough; line small round moulds or shape by hand into cups with high sides, fill and close with a lid, crimping the edges into a decorative braid.
Bake at 180 C for 60 minutes until golden and the filling is cooked through (75 C inside); serve warm.

ingredients: 1 l hot vegetable broth, well salted
1 garlic clove and a few basil leaves
steps: Cook the passata with garlic, basil and oil for 20 minutes until thick.
Poach the eggs in simmering water with vinegar for 3-4 minutes until the whites are set.
Dip each carasau sheet briefly in hot broth and layer on plates with tomato sauce and pecorino, making 2 layers per plate.
Top each with a poached egg, more sauce and pecorino and serve at once.

ingredients: 300 g fresh Sardinian pork sausage, skinned and crumbled
0.2 g saffron dissolved in 2 tbsp warm water
steps: Soften the onion in oil for 5 minutes, add the sausage and brown well for 8 minutes.
Add passata, saffron and basil and simmer 30 minutes.
Boil the malloreddus in salted water for 12-15 minutes until al dente, drain and toss with the sauce.
Serve with plenty of pecorino.

ingredients: 350 g lorighittas (braided ring pasta from Morgongiori; substitute: busiate or casarecce)
1 free-range chicken leg and thigh, about 500 g, cut in pieces
steps: Brown the chicken in oil for 10 minutes, add onion and garlic and cook 5 minutes.
Add wine, let it evaporate, then add passata and simmer covered for 45 minutes until the chicken is cooked through; shred the meat into the sauce.
Cook the lorighittas in salted water until al dente.
Toss with the sauce and serve with pecorino.

ingredients: 300 g fregola (toasted Sardinian semolina pearls; substitute: giant couscous)
1 kg arselle clams, purged in salted water for 2 hours
125 ml Vermentino or dry white wine
1 l light fish stock or water
5 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil and 1 pinch chilli
steps: Cook the clams with 1 tbsp oil and the wine in a covered pan over high heat for 3-4 minutes until they open; discard any closed ones, strain and keep the liquor.
Fry garlic and chilli in the remaining oil, add tomatoes and cook 5 minutes.
Add the fregola and toast 1 minute, then add the clam liquor and stock gradually, risotto style, for 15 minutes until tender and creamy.
Return the clams, add parsley and serve slightly soupy.

ingredients: 60 g bottarga di muggine (cured grey mullet roe), grated, plus a few thin slices
steps: Boil the spaghetti in lightly salted water (bottarga is salty) until al dente.
Warm the oil with garlic over low heat for 2 minutes and remove the garlic.
Toss the drained pasta in the oil with a splash of cooking water, then off the heat add most of the grated bottarga, zest and parsley.
Serve with the remaining bottarga and thin slices on top.

ingredients: 400 g semola rimacinata and 200 ml warm water with 1 tsp salt
600 g floury potatoes, boiled and mashed
200 g aged pecorino sardo, grated (and/or fresh casizolu)
400 g tomato passata cooked with basil
steps: Knead semolina and salted water to a smooth firm dough; rest 30 minutes.
Mix the potatoes with pecorino, garlic, mint and oil to a firm filling.
Roll the dough thin, cut 8 cm rounds, add a ball of filling and close with the traditional wheat-ear pleat (spighitta), pinching from bottom to top.
Boil in salted water for 5-6 minutes until they float and the pasta is tender.
Serve with the tomato sauce and extra pecorino.

ingredients: 150 g dried su filindeu (hand-pulled pasta threads; substitute: thin angel-hair nests broken up)
1.5 kg mutton or lamb on the bone for broth
200 g fresh sour pecorino (casu fiscidu or fresh pecorino; substitute: feta)
steps: Simmer the mutton with the vegetables and salt in the water for 2 hours, skimming, until the meat is tender; strain the broth and keep it boiling.
Break the filindeu into pieces into the boiling broth and cook 3-4 minutes.
Add the fresh pecorino, cut in small pieces, and stir until it softens.
Serve in bowls with grated pecorino, and the mutton on the side.

ingredients: 600 g stale country bread, sliced 1 cm thick
1.5 l rich beef or mutton broth, hot
400 g fresh cow's milk cheese (casizolu or fiore sardo young), sliced (substitute: fontina)
1 tsp ground cinnamon and 1 pinch nutmeg
steps: Butter a deep baking dish and layer bread, cheese slices, grated pecorino, herbs and a pinch of spice, repeating to fill the dish.
Pour hot broth over slowly until the bread is soaked but not floating.
Rest 15 minutes, top with grated pecorino and butter.
Bake at 180 C for 45 minutes until a golden crust forms; serve hot.

ingredients: 500 g dried broad beans, soaked overnight
500 g pork ribs and 300 g pork rind or trotter
steps: Drain the beans and put them in a large pot with the pork ribs, rind, lardo, onions, tomatoes and water to cover by 5 cm.
Simmer gently for 2 hours, skimming occasionally.
Add the sausage, cabbage and fennel and simmer 1 hour more until meat is tender and fully cooked.
Season and serve as a thick soup with toasted bread; it is traditional for Carnival.

steps: Whisk the flour into the water until smooth and rest 4 hours, skimming any foam.
Heat the oven as hot as possible (250 C) with a large round copper or steel pan inside, oiled with 4 tbsp oil.
Stir salt into the batter and pour it into the hot pan about 5 mm deep; scatter onion if using and drizzle with oil.
Bake 20-25 minutes until crisp and golden on top; serve hot with black pepper, as in Sassari.

steps: Knead flour, water, yeast and salt to a firm smooth dough; rise 1 hour.
Divide into 10 balls, rest 15 minutes, and roll each into a very thin 30 cm disc; rest 20 minutes between cloths.
Bake one at a time at 260 C on a hot stone for 1-2 minutes until it puffs up like a balloon.
While hot, split each puffed disc into two thin sheets with a knife.
Stack the sheets under a weight and bake again briefly at 200 C for 1-2 minutes until crisp and dry; store airtight.

Brush or drizzle with olive oil and sprinkle with salt and rosemary.
Bake 3-5 minutes until golden and crisp; serve warm with wine or cured meats.

ingredients: 300 g semola rimacinata and 40 g lard
120 ml warm water and 1 pinch salt
300 g fresh, slightly sour pecorino (substitute: young pecorino or a mix of mozzarella and pecorino)
6 tbsp bitter strawberry-tree or chestnut honey (miele di corbezzolo)
steps: Knead semolina, lard, water and salt into a smooth elastic dough; rest 30 minutes.
Grate or slice the cheese, melt it gently in a pan with a spoon of water and the lemon zest until stringy, then spread 1 cm thick, cool and cut into 8 cm rounds.
Roll the dough thin, sandwich each cheese disc between two pastry rounds and seal with a fluted cutter.
Fry at 175 C for 2-3 minutes per side until golden and blistered.
Serve hot drizzled with honey.

ingredients: 300 g semola rimacinata, 30 g lard, 120 ml water, pinch salt
500 g sheep's milk ricotta, drained overnight
0.2 g saffron dissolved in 1 tbsp warm water
honey or icing sugar to finish
steps: Make a smooth dough with semolina, lard, water and salt; rest 30 minutes.
Mix the ricotta with sugar, eggs, semolina, zests and saffron.
Roll the dough thin, cut 10 cm rounds, put a spoonful of filling in the middle and pinch the edges up into a star-shaped open cup.
Bake at 180 C for 25-30 minutes until the filling is puffed and golden; finish with honey or icing sugar.

ingredients: 200 g sugar and 150 g lard or butter
150 g raisins (papassa) and 150 g chopped walnuts or almonds
200 g icing sugar mixed with 1 egg white and coloured sprinkles
steps: Rub flour, sugar and lard together, then knead in eggs, raisins, nuts, zest, aniseed and baking powder.
Roll 1 cm thick and cut into diamonds.
Bake at 180 C for 15-20 minutes until lightly golden; cool.
Spread with white icing and add sprinkles; let set before serving.

ingredients: 1 tbsp orange-flower water or a little limoncello
200 g fine caster sugar for rolling
steps: Cook the sugar and water to a thread syrup (about 110 C), add the almonds and zest and stir over low heat for 5 minutes until the paste comes away from the pan.
Cool slightly, add the orange-flower water and work into a smooth paste.
Roll into small marbles and roll in caster sugar.
Dry 1 hour, then wrap each in a twist of tissue paper with fringed ends.

ingredients: 1 bottle (700 ml) Mirto di Sardegna, bought from a licensed producer
a few myrtle sprigs to garnish (optional)
steps: Mirto is Sardinia's traditional liqueur made by steeping wild myrtle berries (mirto rosso) or leaves (mirto bianco) in spirit and sweetening it; buy it ready-made from licensed producers.
Chill the bottle in the freezer for a few hours so it pours thick and very cold.
Serve in small chilled glasses after a meal of porceddu or seadas, as a digestivo, garnished with a myrtle sprig.
